Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

CHAPTER 1

A BEAST OF AMBITION

1

“………”

When Subaru Natsuki saw himself in the mirror, he went dead silent.

He recognized his own face, of course, but this one was a relic of fading memories and belonged squarely in the past. It was none other than Subaru Natsuki’s childhood face staring back at him.

“What the…?”

When his hand holding the mirror started to tremble, so did his ashen, dumbfounded reflection. He tried to touch his face with his free hand. The boy in the mirror also reached out with the same tentative movements. Judging from his hands and his face, he was maybe ten years old.

Subaru had been a late bloomer and was always on the shorter side as a kid, but…

“What the hell is going on?!” Subaru shouted. This was no time for reminiscing.

What a nightmare. There was no other way to describe how absurd this was. Subaru had never felt desperate enough to return to his childhood in such a dramatic fashion. Something had clearly gone terribly wrong.

Becoming ten years younger overnight…

“I can’t just sit around like this…”

Regaining some of his composure, Subaru hurried to the door of the room.

There was no way Chaosflame inns just happened to offer complimentary rejuvenation packages with every stay. It was safer to assume that this was the work of an enemy.

I’ve gotta warn everyone and figure out a way to undo this…

“Guys, something terrible’s happened! I’m sure you can tell, but—”

“Ah! So you’re smaller, too!”

“Bwuh?!”

Finding the doorknob harder to reach than usual, Subaru managed to turn it and burst into the room, only to be greeted by an unbelievable scene that he probably should have seen coming.

A girl with an adorably cute face beamed at him and waved. Her clear blue eyes, distinctive blond hair, and unmistakable sunny disposition…

“It doesn’t seem possible, but…is that you, Medium?”

“That’s right! It’s the strangest thing. When I woke up, I became a kid again! But seeing that the same thing happened to you is a relief! At least I’m not alone!”

The girl who looked maybe twelve or thirteen was undoubtedly Medium O’Connell. She was dressed in a thin bit of cloth and was evidently suffering from the same condition as Subaru. Even after losing a decade’s worth of height, she was still half a head taller than Subaru.

“Look, this is serious. We can’t relax just because we’re not alone—Whoa?!”

“Uuuu!”

An unexpected collision took Subaru completely by surprise. As he tumbled over with an audible thud, he felt a weight settle on top of him. It made him groan like a squashed frog.

“Aaah! No, Louis! Subaru’s small now!”

“Aaa, uuu!”

“Gaaah! I’m tiny, too! I can’t lift you up!”

It felt like a wild animal had clambered onto Subaru’s chest, and though Medium tried her best to help, her shrunken body didn’t have the strength to stop the rampage.

Young Subaru Natsuki was helpless against the vile beast…

“Louis, stop! You’re going to crush Subaru!”

With that sharp rebuke, the offending creature was pulled away at last. Looking up, Subaru saw Louis receding into the distance with a sad look on her face, for some reason.

It was Talitta who had grabbed her. Subaru felt a wave of relief at seeing the woman in her formal black suit.

“Phew, thanks Talitta!” Medium said. “I wasn’t strong enough to lift her up.”

“Th-think nothing of it… Subaru, are you unharmed?”

“Unharmed isn’t how I’d phrase it, but… Anyway, I’m glad nothing weird happened to you, Talitta.”

Subaru accepted Medium’s outstretched hand and rose to his feet. He glanced across the room at the sofa. Sitting there and watching in silence was a black-haired man in a mask—the leader of this group, the fugitive emperor Abel.

Subaru had a thing or two to say about how the man had done absolutely nothing to help, but he was also thankful that he hadn’t transformed the way Subaru or Medium had.

“Abel, it’s at least good to see that nothing happened to—”

“Disgraceful.”

Abel interrupted Subaru with obvious displeasure. Subaru was speechless for a moment at how cold it was.

“…Huh, I think I have a pretty adorable baby face, personally.”

That was the most spiteful retort he could manage.

“Calling yourself a baby face, huh? That’s just like you, Bro. And yeah, you are cuter now.”

“…! You’re…”

Subaru was startled by the boy who emerged from one of the other bedrooms. He seemed to be around the same age as Subaru, aside from the ripped-up piece of cloth wrapped around his face.

He didn’t look familiar, but the way he talked and his missing arm made it obvious who he was.

“Al, right…? What’s that you got on your face?”

“Oh, yeah. Did I scare you? My helmet doesn’t fit anymore, and I didn’t have anything else on hand. Sorry, but try not to dwell on it.”

“You can say that, sure, but I’m obviously gonna…”

The visibly younger Al waved lightly. His face covering was haphazardly wrapped, leaving some black hair visible on the back of his head. This was a fresh look for him, but it was a minor detail next to the much bigger changes.

Almost looks like a half-assed serial killer in some old movie.

“…Do you really have to go out of your way to hide your face just because you can’t wear your helmet?”

“That’s not a very thoughtful comment, Bro. I’m not wearing a helmet for show or because I’ve gone crazy. It’s a complex. Just ’cause I look like a kid doesn’t mean I started thinking like one, too.” Al shrugged and gestured at his missing arm. “My arm didn’t grow back, and the scars on my face are still there, too. Same goes for you, right?”

“I guess so, yeah…”

Subaru looked down at his own body. He was wearing a loose shirt that was too large, but beneath it were several white scars that had not healed. They were proof of the time he had spent living in this world and looked out of place on such a young boy.

The scars were also proof that this was not some rewinding of the clock. His body had simply shrunk.

“But shrinking this much in a single night isn’t normal. That sort of thing doesn’t just happen randomly.”

“Yeah. Hmm…,” Medium said, before a new realization hit her. “Wait, I won’t be able to help Flop out with work anymore. Bro’s so scrawny! This might be a big problem!”

“Okay, yes, this is definitely a big blow to the O’Connell family business, but…”

Unless they changed back soon, there would undoubtedly be some serious future consequences. For now, though, Subaru wanted to focus on more immediate problems. His most pressing issue was the lack of clothes that fit, but Al and Medium fought for a living, which was a much bigger concern.

“You mentioned the helmet not fitting, but your sword’s probably an issue, too, right?”

“Sharp observation. I’m not totally useless, but I can’t really swing properly with this cute little arm.”

“Same for me,” Medium confirmed. “It’d probably be rough holding two swords. If it’s just one, then I can probably sort of…argh.”

“Watch out!”

Medium propped up one of her sheaths and drew, only for the sword to slip right out of her hands and bury itself in the floor, narrowly missing Subaru’s nose on the way down. Her face went pale.

“Wah wah wah! Sorry, Subaru! You’re not dead, right?!”

“I-I’m fine, but…that was really dangerous.”

Crestfallen, Medium retrieved the sword and carefully returned it to its sheath. Right up until a day ago, she had wielded her blades like an extension of herself. Now, she could barely hold one. A shocking revelation for someone whose identity revolved around fighting.

“So that means Talitta’s the only one who can fight now?”

“Eeeh! I can still do my best, even if I am small!”

“Look, I’m not doubting your moxie, but I don’t wanna break any labor laws…”

It was wonderful how Medium refused to give up in the face of incredible adversity, but it was important to grasp the reality of the situation.

With Al and Medium like this, the only reliable fighter we have is Talitta. As strong as she is, we can’t rely on her alone when we’re in the middle of enemy territory.

In fact, when that realization dawned on Talitta, her face started to develop a bad twitch.

“You are unexpectedly composed.”

Abel finally broke his silence. The way he spoke made it clear he had been observing them like test subjects.

“I don’t know about that,” Subaru said, snarling. “Maybe the panic just hasn’t set in yet. Or maybe I’ll only realize how big a deal my lost height and weight are after noticing all the new inconveniences.”

“Clearly, it has not impacted your barbed tongue.”

“My cunning and my ability to adapt are two of my few selling points.”

Subaru knew quipping back would just make him seem desperate to get the last word in. Naturally, he decided to do it anyway. And as expected, Abel’s gaze hardened.

“Always talking back…,” Abel said in obvious displeasure, before continuing. “Most likely, it was Orbart Dankelken who changed you.”

“What?!”

Subaru’s eyes went wide. This revelation was earth-shattering.

“You mean the old man we ran into at the palace yesterday…one of the Nine Divine Generals?!”

Orbart was the one who had been accompanying the false emperor at the Crimson Lazuli Palace—and was arguably the third strongest person in the entire empire.

“You sure it was him, Abel?” Al asked.

“There are others who could have changed your appearance, but this is no simple deception. That makes him the most likely suspect.”

“…Personally, I was wondering if that might be that foxy lady’s handiwork.”

While Subaru was recovering from his shock, Al helpfully interrogated Abel’s claim.

Subaru certainly shared Al’s suspicions. There were plenty of reasons to question if Yoruna was responsible. For one thing, the three victims were the same people who had paid her palace a visit. As things stood, Yoruna and Orbart were both prime suspects.

So why was Abel so sure it was Orbart…?

“Can that old man use some kind of magic to shrink people?” Subaru asked.

“There is no hard proof, if that is what you are after. The Nine Divine Generals all have their own secrets. Orbart is no exception. In addition, he is the leader of a group called Shinobi who are especially secretive.”

“Shinobi, huh…? So we’re talking ninjutsu, blending into the night, carrying out assassinations, spying on everyone. Stuff like that?”

“I am not familiar with this ninjutsu you speak of, but the rest are indeed Shinobi’s prime duties… Where did you learn of them?”

The moment he heard the word shinobi, Subaru started listing stereotypical ninja work. Of course, Abel’s gaze made it clear he wasn’t supposed to know all that.

“Oh, uh… Some people who have similar jobs back in my homeland were called ninjas, and…”

Subaru hurriedly made up an excuse and turned to Al for some help. Before he could say anything, Medium shouted “Ah!” in realization. Her big round eyes got even bigger.

“If this is all part of that old man’s scheme, then it probably happened when we were escaping! Remember how he jabbed you and me in the chest?”

“When we were escaping…? Ohhh.”

It took Subaru a second to recall the events of the day before. When they were escaping—or rather, when they were fighting for their lives to clear Yoruna’s spiteful demands. They had managed to evade Kafma’s thorns and were about to make their escape from the castle keep when Orbart joined the fray.

However, none of them had sustained any notable injuries.

I wrote it off back then, but there’s no way one of the Nine Divine Generals would let us off so easily.

“But who would’ve expected him to do this?! Also, Al didn’t get hit, right?!”

“…Sorry, Bro. I was duking it out with him right before I jumped. I wouldn’t be surprised if he jabbed me somewhere. I just didn’t bother worrying about wounds that didn’t kill me.”

Al muttered in a low voice—or at least as low as a young boy could manage—regretting how he had overlooked important details. Of course, there was no reason to be so hard on himself. He had helped get everyone out alive. And Medium had helped just as much. They had done their jobs admirably.

If anything, Subaru was the one who should have noticed.

I’m useless in a fight, so I should at least have been on the lookout for trouble.

“How am I supposed to face Rem like this…? I’m the same size as Beako. Emilia-tan’s gonna treat me like a kid more than ever…”

“I doubt the princess’d play with me even after I became tiny. Gotta say, it feels like there’s no upside in any of this…,” Al muttered.

“Y-you all seem surprisingly calm… I, of course, am completely stunned…”

Talitta had gone pale, finding it hard to stay composed as she held on to Louis, who was flailing around. She almost seemed to feel guilty for being the only one unaffected.

Of course, her take on the situation was the most reasonable of them all. Subaru and Al were simply putting up a brave front.

“Honestly, if I wasn’t joking about it, I’d want to scream.”

“Really?” Talitta asked Subaru.

“Yeah… That’s how disturbing this is.”

It wasn’t being in a younger body that bothered him. It was having his body changed against his will, undermining his very sense of self.

Subaru had experienced countless terrible situations since arriving in this world.

Death naturally topped the list, but over the past year and a half, he had endured plenty of other hardships. And as seasoned as Subaru was now, the feeling of being reshaped by someone else was still unbearable.

“So this is what it feels like to be violated by Lust…”

Subaru gritted his teeth and hugged himself. A low buzzing echoed in his head. It came from the memory of all the people in the Water Gate City who had been transformed into flies by the Archbishop of Lust, still waiting to be saved.

If being changed into a younger version of himself was this terrible, then he could not begin to imagine how dreadful it must feel to be transformed into something so fundamentally different.

Subjecting someone to this…

“Only a vicious old man would do such a thing,” said Abel, arms crossed. His comment took Subaru by surprise. It was like he had read his thoughts.

As their eyes met, Subaru opened and closed his small hand before asking, “This can be undone…right?”

“I cannot say for sure. However, it is natural to think there is some method of reversal.”

“What’s your basis for that?”

“What purpose could there be for a poison that does not immediately kill besides bringing someone to the negotiating table?”

Abel’s conclusion was persuasive.

If this is a ploy to get us to cut a deal, then…

“Then someone should be making contact sooner than—”

Just as Talitta started saying that, a knock came at the door.

“…!”

Everyone tensed and looked at the door. Was it Orbart, coming to feel them out after turning them into children?

“Apologies for intruding so early in the day. I am Lady Yoruna Mishigure’s messenger.”

The voice greeting them from the other side of the door was an unexpected one.

“That’s the deer-girl from yesterday…Tanza. Is this about a response to the letter?” Medium wondered aloud.

“Huh? Oh, right, yeah! The letter!”

Subaru initially deflated when he realized it wasn’t Orbart who had come knocking, until Medium’s question helped him realize why this visitor had come.

“Umm…it’s safe to let her in, right?”

Still feeling a little startled, Subaru checked with Abel before doing anything. The masked man was silent for a moment before finally nodding.

With that, Talitta opened the door and welcomed in the messenger.

“Please pardon me. I have come bearing a message from Lady Yoruna.”

The kimono-clad deer-girl Tanza crossed the threshold.

The young servant glanced around the room and furrowed her otherwise emotionless face. There were four children she did not recognize and a suspicious-looking man in a strange mask gathered there. If anything, it was impressive that she didn’t have a stronger reaction.

“It seems everyone is here… Well…”

“What?”

“…No, it is nothing. My apologies.”

Tanza failed to hide her interest in Abel’s mask. Even after she apologized, she didn’t stop glancing at him curiously. It was actually quite adorable seeing her act her age.

At the same time, it was hard to forget that she had come bearing crucial news, and a quiet tension filled the air.

Tanza bowed deeply and spoke once again.

“Regarding the letter delivered yesterday, Lady Yoruna is ready to make a formal reply. In addition, she wishes to invite all of you to the Crimson Lazuli Palace.”

“…She actually read the letter?”

Even knowing it was rude, Subaru could not help feeling a sense of relief that the letter had in fact been read. There was a distinct chance that Yoruna might have casually decided to tear up the letter even after he and the others had risked so much delivering it. This tense uncertainty was much like dealing with a haughty cat or Priscilla.

In any case, a formal invitation to the palace meant they must have made enough progress that it was worth entertaining a conversation. The only other pressing problem was the age regression…

“The author of the letter and those who visited yesterday to deliver the message are requested to attend.”

“Ack.”

“…?”

Tanza cocked her head and furrowed her brow at that unexpected groan.

Subaru grabbed his chest in an attempt to steady his pounding heart to not let on how shaken he was and summoned his best smile.

“It’s nothing, don’t worry about it.”

Whether she was willing to leave it at that or simply uninterested, Tanza carried on.

“When the bell tolls to mark fire time, please be ready at the gate of the Crimson Lazuli Palace.”

“Understood. You have done well. You may go.”

“…Yes sir. Excuse me.”

The time she had mentioned meant they should show up around noon.

Now that her work here was done, Tanza bowed one last time and turned to leave.

She didn’t get far before Subaru asked, “Um, just to be sure, the person who wrote the letter is the only person who absolutely has to go, and the messengers from yesterday are just extras, right? If, for whatever reason, those messengers might have trouble participating…”

“Lady Yoruna has requested the presence of the messengers.”

“………”

“In this city, no one can go against Lady Yoruna’s wishes.”

Her tone was matter-of-fact, but there was an unshakable conviction in Tanza’s parting reminder.

Once Subaru closed the door behind her, he took a deep breath and spun around.

“Strategy meeting! Now!”

He raised his much shorter arms and summoned his comrades.

2

Yoruna Mishigure had requested their presence at the palace.

Even if they were willing to risk bringing Abel to the palace, the biggest problem was Yoruna’s demand to have the messengers from yesterday accompany him.

If Abel’s conjecture was correct and their age regression had nothing to do with Yoruna, then even if the children went along, it was doubtful whether that would satisfy her.

In the worst case, it might be taken as a sign of bad faith and ruin any chance of striking a deal. They did have the option of being completely honest about their situation and hoping for the best, but…

“Revealing your cards without knowing the other party’s intentions is madness,” Abel flatly stated.

And just this once, Subaru was in complete agreement. Yoruna ruled this city on top of being one of the Nine Divine Generals. His initial impression was that she was a dangerous woman. They had plenty of reasons to be wary of her.

She was a potential ally who could help Abel retake his throne, but she was not someone they could trust without reservation.

“Even if we spilled our guts and told her everything, she might still have an issue with how you were dressed like a girl, Bro. What’cha gonna do if she’s all, like, ‘How dare you deceive me?’ or something like that?”

“Hmm, should I put together a kiddie Natsumi Schwartz getup just to be safe…?”

“P-please, no,” Talitta begged. “You’ll drive me crazy at this rate…”

Telling a lie to cover up another lie is a fairly standard trope, but I guess cross-dressing after turning into a kid to hide the fact that you cross-dressed in the first place does sound kinda insane.

Unlike with Al’s helmet, the wig’s size could be adjusted some, so it was technically possible…

“So what’s the plan?” Medium asked as she cocked her head. “We only have three hours left until it’s time to meet, right?”

She was holding Louis, who was basically the same size as she was now and mirroring her head movement.

Subaru scratched his cheek and said, “First of all, rejecting her invitation is not an option.”

“Damn straight,” Al said. “All our work would go to waste, and we would’ve gotten shrunk for nothing.”

“There would be no gain in that…,” Talitta agreed.

While Subaru nodded in response, he was still considering whether it made sense to retreat.

Insisting on making back the initial bet was the classic prelude to a gambler’s downfall. It was important to know when to cut your losses. This time, the losses happened to be measured in inches.

“I don’t know whether this should be considered a heavy price or a light one…”

“Yeah, rapid aging is obviously bad, but suddenly becoming a kid again is a toughie. Ain’t this super abusable?” Al asked.

“Yeah, if you think of it as a chance to redo everything starting from childhood but with all your memories intact…”

In a sense, restoring youth was sort of like Return by Death in that it increased potential opportunities.

Combining the knowledge and experience of an adult with the physical potential of a young child could make it possible to take on challenges that were previously unthinkable.

Compared to the alternative, age regression at least has some potential advantages…

“It’s easy to make that assumption, yes. But it’s not nearly that convenient.”

The moment a new voice chimed in, Subaru stopped breathing. He wasn’t alone. Everyone in the room froze. But the intruder seemed oblivious to the tension in the air.

“I went ahead and made some tea for myself, but does anyone else want some?” the intruder asked in an easygoing tone as he held up a teacup.

“…!”

Talitta immediately readied her bow and took aim at the wrinkled face of a tiny, almost child-sized old man.

Despite how close he was to the nocked arrow, the old man simply shrugged.

“Hey now, gimme a break. I don’t like having scary things pointed at me. Besides, once you get up in years, you gotta hit the head more often. So don’t make me wet myself. I’m practically trembling over here.”

“Don’t trifle with me…! How did you—?”

“—Orbart Dankelken.”

Talitta’s face turned red at the old man, who was unreasonably calm despite her arrow and her open hostility. But before she could finish her question, she was interrupted by Abel. The masked man hadn’t so much as budged from his seat on the sofa. Orbart Dankelken’s eyes narrowed beneath his big bushy eyebrows as he met Abel’s gaze.

The man who so boldly infiltrated their room was none other than the shinobi who was the suspected cause of their age regression.

Orbart broke into a smile and said, “Yesterday confirmed that I’m rather famous, but you leave quite the impression yourself. Where’d you buy a mask like that? I wonder.”

“Enough foolishness, you old tree. Why have you come here?”

“Youngsters just don’t indulge their elders in conversation anymore. The kids in the village keep getting better at ignoring me. I’m one lonely old man, I tell ya, kah-ha-ha-ha!”

Orbart’s hearty laugh hung in the air.

Subaru and the others were finally starting to recover from their initial shock, but the confusion was not entirely gone, and the wariness remained.

“Gramps, how did you get in here? I was watching the door.”

“Oh, you’re smaller, but you’re the little lady who looked like a dancing girl yesterday, aren’t you? Don’t worry, Gramps will answer your question. You let that deer-girl in, didn’t you? I came in at the same time.”

“At the same time? With Tanza? But…”

“But she was alone? Kah-ha-ha-ha! If that’s how it looked, that’s ’cause I wanted it to look that way. How I got in is a secret. Shinobi tricks are my bread and butter, and I can’t be losing my job.”

Orbart laughed again, sidestepping Medium’s question.

I don’t know how seriously I should take him, but this self-declared shinobi said something I can’t ignore right out of the gate. Asking him straight up will be faster than roundabout probing.

“Do you know what caused us to shrink?”

When Subaru posed the question as frankly as possible, Orbart’s eyes narrowed. His brow furrowed a bit in thought for a moment, before finally…

“Ah, you’re that girl who was in the red outfit yesterday! There’s no mistaking the dancing girl and the one-armed guy, so I was wondering who you were for a little while.”

Subaru couldn’t believe how fast the tension was shattered. Al snickered a little as he let himself relax.

“…Damn, Bro. Even the shinobi chief couldn’t see through your disguise.”

“Phew, that’s incredible! That level of transformation is something I’d like the kids in my village to learn. Have you considered teaching? I’d welcome you with open arms.”

“…Unfortunately, Natsumi Schwartz’s schedule is pretty tight. Depending on your answer, I might be able to find some time, though.”

“Ho-ho. So it depends on how I reply, huh?”

The disguise was an unexpected hook, but Subaru licked his lips at the opportunity that had just fallen into his lap.

I don’t know if an empty promise has any value here, but I’m not about to let this chance to talk with Orbart slip past me. If Abel’s right and this old man is the one who turned us into kids, then…

“If you know why our bodies changed, then…”

“Ah, that? I’m the one who did it. Interesting, isn’t it? My shinobi technique.”

“………”

There was no maneuvering needed at all. The old man outright admitted it. Subaru gulped. The line of questioning he had prepared was pointless now. Orbart smirked impishly.

“If you accidently kill someone before interrogating them, it’s a pain, right? Right. There’s all sorts of techniques to put them through the wringer without killing them. Isn’t that fun?”

And in the same breath, he took a sip of his warm tea.

3

The age regression afflicted Subaru, Al, and Medium.

Based on the testimony of Abel, who possessed intimate knowledge regarding the Nine Divine Generals, it had been more or less confirmed that the perpetrator was Orbart. However, to hear it straight from the horse’s mouth was surprising. Especially when he was so shameless about it.

“Whoa, hey. Everyone’s face suddenly looks scary. Didn’t anyone teach you some manners? You’re supposed to help the elderly, not harass them.”

The tension shot back up. Talitta had never lowered her bow, but now even Al and Medium were glaring dangerously at Orbart. No chance to calm things down.

“Cease the nonsense, Orbart. I am asking again: Why did you come here?” The greatest threat came from Abel, who fixed the old man with an imperious glare from behind his oni mask. “You are aware the ruler of this city, Yoruna Mishigure, has acknowledged these three as messengers and declared that no harm shall befall them.”

“M-my word, that’s right! Wasn’t yesterday’s match about keeping you from laying so much as a finger on us?! We put our very lives on the line! This attack is clearly at odds with that!”

“Hold on there, now. You’re getting all mixed up. Why don’t you calm down a little?”

As Orbart pointed out, Subaru had slipped into his Natsumi persona in the heat of the moment, but the facts of the matter remained the same. Yoruna had acknowledged them as messengers, and Tanza had confirmed that no one would touch them. To go against that would be to make an enemy of Yoruna.

“Of course, she would turn a blind eye to any such guarantees if the city was being threatened.”

“Ugh! N-now that you mention it…”

Abel’s comment completely extinguished the fiery blood rushing to Subaru’s head. The false emperor commanding Orbart had effectively yielded the right to negotiate with Yoruna. It was entirely possible that he would consider this endeavor a wash and decide to simply flip the entire table. That would mean going against Yoruna, who was considered notorious even among the Nine Divine Generals, but…

“…Mask…boy…”

Orbart scratched his chin with a finger, lips curled, while Subaru furrowed his brow.

Orbart is one of the Nine Divine Generals who should know the emperor pretty well.

Either way…

“Th-that’s just a flimsy excuse…!”

There wasn’t much Subaru could say in response to that.

“Do not get carried away, Orbart.”

It was the masked man brimming with authority who challenged the crafty old man. The light in his eyes brought an end to the old man’s taunting, forcing him to stop playing with his teacup.

Subaru grimaced as Orbart let out a loud, spittle-flecked laugh.

He’s…not someone we can just ignore.

Of course Chisha had clearly moved against Abel, so enticing him was out of the question, but…

“If Abel’s right, then Mr. Orbart might be up for grabs.”

Abel had mentioned there was some hope of winning over the generals whose loyalties were not set in stone. Yoruna had welcomed them to the negotiating table, so the possibility seemed to exist, at least.

But convincing Orbart to join us is gonna be…

“………”

Subaru glanced at Abel. As intelligent as he was, surely he would understand the unspoken message. The only card they had that might convince Orbart was Abel’s face underneath his mask.

We won’t get a better chance than this.

“—Abel.”

When Subaru quietly said his name, Abel’s attention clearly shifted. With the mask in the way, it was impossible to gauge his expression, but he was focused on Subaru now.

There was no telling what he was thinking, but he clearly understood what Subaru was planning to do.

“Emperor Vincent Volakia,” Subaru intoned.

“Huh?”

“You wanted to know why we came to meet Yoruna. Well, look no further. It’s Emperor Vincent Volakia.”

Now that they’d come this far, Abel did not argue with Subaru’s decision. He simply brought his long, thin fingers to his mask, and…

The shinobi leader smiled at the emperor driven from his throne. Perhaps it was more accurate to say he sneered, as befitting a vicious old man. Then he shared his ambition.

“I’ve always wanted to slay the emperor as my crowning achievement before old age takes me.”

The moment he revealed his ambition, the tension in the room finally snapped. In that moment, the rules preventing combat went right out the window. Talitta, Al, and Medium all leaped into action to smother Orbart’s dream.

However—

“It’s hard to use the techniques you’ve learned as an adult when you’re in the body of a child.”

Orbart twisted his neck and swung both hands, blood splattering from his fingertips. Subaru’s eyes widened as he took in the bloody scene.

“Gah…”

Al collapsed with a groan and his hand on his neck. He and Medium had rushed forward to pin Orbart down, but both of their necks had been sliced open. So much blood poured out that it was hard to believe so much had spilled out of such small bodies. It wasn’t long before the room’s bright interior was painted red.

“Seems like you can’t use the same technique you used yesterday. I was curious about it, but you went down before you could reveal the trick. Ahhh, looks like I screwed up.”

Orbart gave a half-hearted chuckle as the two went still. Between the blood and their twitching limbs, Subaru had no doubt they were dead.

And the only one who had been ready to attack Orbart at a moment’s notice…

“…Ah.”

When Subaru turned to see why the nocked arrow hadn’t taken flight, he was stunned. Talitta was pinned to the wall.

Talitta’s tall frame was fixed in place by a shuriken sticking out from the center of her chest. The stereotypically star-shaped throwing knife almost made it seem like some sick joke. It had struck her in the heart, and she had clearly died from the impact.

“…I see you will not heed the prohibition on violence.”

A man’s voice echoed in the room overflowing with death. It was Abel, surrounded by corpses that had piled up with frightening speed. He had risen from his seat and had leveled a penetrating gaze at the author of all that death.

Orbart wiped away a splatter of blood that had reached his cheek.

“I did not foresee your fascination with annihilation. That was an oversight on my part.”

“No, there’s no helping that. If word about my old-timer dream got out, I’d be so embarrassed that it’d kill me. Kah-ha-ha-ha!”

Al, Medium, Talitta—they were all dead.

The conversation between emperor and retainer sounded like it was happening in another world. But it wasn’t another world. This was reality. Reality. An unbearable reality. A reality they had reached because of Subaru’s wrong choice.

“Hm? Oh, yes, you’re still here.”

Orbart raised a brow at seeing Subaru totter forward into view. The old man shrugged, then pointed toward the dead.

“It’s not like you have to die, too. If you don’t get in the way, I won’t kill you.”

“Tha…”

“Ah, you’re the type that moves on impulse. This old man would prefer it if you think before you say or do anything, but I won’t wait long.”

When he heard how Orbart was calm enough to even crack jokes, Subaru’s mind went completely blank. No, not blank. It was pure red. It was hard to say whether it was because of rage or simply a reflection of all the blood that had been spilled.

Either way, Subaru’s body moved…

“Fool.”

Abel’s voice was filled with scorn. His eyes were boring straight into the back of Subaru’s head. The force of his gaze was palpable, even as Subaru thought about how right Abel was.

There was no meaning in trying to protect Abel like this now. But Subaru had already made the mistake. There was no undoing it.

“Uuu…”

“Oh, come now. Even the girl? I thought girls always hated Your Highness?”

Orbart put his hand to his forehead as Louis stood before him. Or rather, she stood in front of Subaru.

She was covering Subaru, who was covering Abel. The three of them were all lined up. It was an absurd series of human shields.

“I always figured you’d die alone, Your Highness.”

“…Do not assume that every person fits neatly in whatever box you assign them.”

“Kah-ha-ha-ha!”

Orbart laughed. Even in a situation like this, Abel had a comeback at the ready.

The old shinobi had little interest in Subaru or Louis, but he was not so kind as to overlook anyone who dared stand in his way.

And so…

“—I won’t forgive you.”

Subaru Natsuki seared into his mind the image of the old shinobi sneering viciously as he indulged his grand ambition. Then his adolescent body split open, and he sank into a pool of his own blood.

4

As the blood flowed, a hot feeling welled up where he had been struck. His body began to grow cold from the inside out.

Everything flowing out of him swallowed him from the feet up until he could no longer see, and when he sank all the way to the bottom—

“………”

The next instant, the blood he lost was flowing through his veins again, and he started to hear a grating sound in his ears.

Where did I come back? I’ve gotta—

“I went ahead and made some tea for myself, but does anyone else want some?”

That unforgettable, wicked voice signaled the start of a new battle for Subaru Natsuki.

BEHIND YOUR EYELIDS

1

The moment he heard that hoarse, elderly voice, it felt like all the blood in Subaru’s body started flowing backward. Goose bumps rose on his skin, and the air in his lungs seemed to freeze. It was like there was something profoundly sharp embedded in his chest, stirring his very soul.

Return by Death had activated, and it had brought him back to the worst possible moment.

“…!”

Before Subaru could react, Talitta took aim with her bow. Her target was of course the intruder—the old man, Orbart Dankelken, one of the Nine Divine Generals, and the person who had killed them all moments ago.

Even without knowing how that tragedy played out, everyone in the room was wound tight, wary of the unwelcome visitor.

Despite being in that same room, despite having an arrow aimed at him from such close range, Orbart merely shrugged, making a mockery of their caution.

“Hey now, gimme a break. I don’t like having scary things pointed at me. Besides, once you get up in years, you gotta hit the head more often. So don’t make me wet myself. I’m practically trembling over here.”

“Don’t trifle with me…! How did you—?”

“—Orbart Dankelken.”

Talitta’s face turned red in anger at Orbart’s flippant evasion, but Abel interrupted her, revealing the intruder’s identity. And thus began an interrogation that would be laughable if it were not so potentially bloody. Repeating the scene Subaru had just lived through was a path that led only to destruction.

With the gruesome memories so fresh in his mind, he knew he had to do something different.

But I don’t have any time to talk with everyone.

“Why…?”

Why had he wound up back here? It was a pointless question, but he could not help wanting to throw his hands up in defeat. Even knowing full well how haughty and selfish that thought was when his Return by Death allowed him a second chance. If it had at least triggered before Orbart appeared, he would have had a chance to discuss things.

It brought back memories of a recent struggle when he had died and returned so many times while dealing with Todd in Guaral. There had hardly been any time to react then as well.

The details were different, but the situation was similar.

A respawn point that locks you in a cage with a bloodthirsty beast.

Return by Death had always been capricious when it came to how much time it wound back, but this was brutal.

Trying to find a path forward from this dead-end start is…

“Ngh!”

“Whoa?! Why’d you go and do that?!”

“Uwaa?! What?!” “Uuu?! Aaa, uuu!”

To silence all the grumbling and complaints bubbling up in his mind, Subaru slapped both his cheeks with all his might. The sound echoed in the room, drawing everyone’s attention to him.

Sorry, I get that that would surprise anyone without a warning. But I needed it.

“Sorry about that. I was just motivating myself a bit.”

He scolded himself for wasting what little time he had crying about it. He was never the one who paid the price for his stupidity.

I can’t let that bloody disaster happen again.

“Motivation, huh? Just looks like red cheeks from here…hm? Were you that girl in the red outfit yesterday? I wondered why I didn’t recognize you.”

Orbart arched his bushy brows as he clocked Subaru.

Just like last time, this was where he made the connection between Subaru and Natsumi. If they identified Orbart as the cause of the age regression here, events would proceed along the same route as before.

I won’t make the same mistake twice. This old man is terrifyingly dangerous. The moment he believes Abel is the true emperor, he’ll try to fulfill his long-held ambition and kill us all.

It was safe to say he was their enemy.

“Phew, that’s incredible! That level of transformation is something I’d like the kids in my village to learn. Have you considered teaching? I’d welcome you with open arms.”

Stroking his chin with a joking air, Orbart smiled like a friendly old man, but that was nothing more than another tool in his toolbox. The reason he had silently sneaked in was the same reason he maintained this affable attitude. Everything he did was to gauge how they reacted. Subaru had to consider whatever Orbart said or did as more of his shinobi tricks meant to advance his sinister goal.

“Hey, are you the reason we’re all small, Mister?”

Just as there was a lull in the conversation, Medium asked a question. Orbart answered with an exaggerated laugh.

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! Aye, that’s right! It’s a shinobi technique, but it’s pretty darn interesting, ain’t it?”

“So it really was you, gramps…!”

“Don’t let it bother you, one-arm. If anything, you should be grateful. I might have accidently killed you, and then we wouldn’t have gotten a chance to talk like this. Instead, I only shrank you down some.”

Orbart confessed to his handiwork and then silenced Al by pointing out the clear gap in strength between them. What he said was true. If he had wanted to, he could have killed them in the brawl in the palace yesterday. The only reason he had simply turned them into children was because he happened to be curious why they were openly rebelling against the emperor.

Or at least that was what Subaru was thinking, but…

“Well, I’ll admit I did try to kill you, but those attacks were all stopped, so this was also a bit of a last resort. Ain’t that right, one-arm?”

“…I dunno what you mean.”

“Oh? Not gonna reveal your trick? Well, that’s your trump card, I imagine, so I guess that makes sense.”

“It’ll be the same every time I say it. I don’t know what you’re talking about.”

Al answered with a muffled voice from behind the wrappings covering his face. It should have been an unsatisfying answer for Orbart, and yet…

“Really? Well, all right, then.”

He just nodded, seemingly delighted by the response.

Subaru had no idea what the meaning of their exchange was. Al had done a masterful job protecting Subaru and Medium during the fighting that broke out in the palace.

I guess Orbart admires the effort?

But even if that were true, now that he had been turned into a child, Al’s technique wouldn’t work against the shinobi anymore. Subaru already knew that, unfortunately. That was why he would base all his decisions on a single unshakable principle in this situation—they had to avoid fighting Orbart at all costs. That meant they could not let Orbart take the initiative.

“…Mr. Orbart. You…”

Wanting to draw out the conversation so he could work on a strategy in the meanwhile, Subaru started to speak—only for Abel to interrupt him.

“You said that your technique shrank them.”

At first, Subaru’s blood ran cold, but one look at Abel’s face was all he needed to understand.

Abel was buying Subaru more time.

“Oh, right. I forgot I hadn’t finished explaining. It’s so easy to get off track when you get to my age. It might be about time for me to retire.”

“You? Spare me the bad jokes. If you claim to be frail from age, you should give up your rank already. That you have not proves your determination.”

“Oh, that’s a bold claim. As hard as it must be to see with that mask on, you think you can see through me?”

“Of course.”

Orbart’s eyes flashed with curiosity at Abel’s unflinching answer. And having taken the talking role, Abel was diligent in giving Subaru the time he so desperately needed. He had no idea how Abel had discerned what he wanted, but Subaru had no choice but to rely on him.

Without even glancing at Subaru, Abel crossed his arms.

“As a general first-class, third among your peers, you would accurately be called one of the top figures of the empire. However, you are greedy by nature. You are not remotely satisfied with your current position.”

“Better a greedy old man than a shriveled-up old man, no?”

Orbart answered Abel while unknowingly committing lèse-majesté. But even Abel did not fully grasp the darkness lurking within Orbart. There was no way he could have plumbed those depths.

There was a dark gleam in Orbart’s yellow eyes, as if taunting Abel, questioning whether he could actually see through it.

“And? What do you suppose it is that I want, then?”

“The First seat,” Abel answered in a quiet, steady voice.

Orbart’s breathing, which sounded like dried leaves, fell silent. There was no telling what sort of storm was raging in the silent shinobi’s heart, but it was clear that Abel’s claim had unsettled him.

It was enough that Al and Talitta both sprang into action to take advantage of the opening—

“Hey, one-arm. I know the feeling, but behave yourself. You too, bow girl.”

“Ngh! Do you have eyes in the back of your head or something?”

“Just call it a difference in training. I’m a lot older than you, after all. But from my perspective, most people seem like children. That’s the invincible logic of the elderly.”

Al and Talitta gulped at Orbart’s warning. The old man’s attention was focused on Abel, and while there had been an opening of some sort, this monster’s many years of training gave him the ability to notice even the slightest change around him.

He didn’t need to use his eyes to see through their paltry tricks and plans. This old man had transcended such mundane concerns long ago.

“Al,” Subaru said as he shook his head, warning him to not try anything.

He did not have a full grasp of Al’s true strength and abilities, but he probably used techniques optimized for defensive fights. The brutal truth was they would not work here, and he would simply get himself killed.

Enduring Al’s bitter gaze, Orbart’s attention remained on Abel.

“Still, though, saying I’m after the First seat at this age is quite a claim. What made you take a leap like that, mask boy?”

“Old age is not reason enough to drain the well of ambition. A shinobi tortures their body and mind to their very limits to reach a realm that only a handful can achieve. A shinobi is not complete until they die.”

“I see… You’ve done your homework.”

Orbart’s answer was bland, clearly different from before. At first glance, he seemed to be confirming Abel’s conjecture, but that couldn’t be further from the truth.

Subaru happened to know that Abel was actually wrong.

Orbart’s true desire was to murder his lord and emperor. Ascending to First seat of the Nine Divine Generals was a secondary or even tertiary ambition.

That said, the fact that there was still some emotion in Orbart’s voice was proof that Abel’s answer was not entirely off base. Abel had discerned the rapacious desires that consumed Orbart. Abel had presumed that his covetousness began and ended with reaching the pinnacle of the Nine Divine Generals, rather than as a means to a greater end, but that was a perfectly reasonable misunderstanding. How could he hope to realize that Orbart’s desire was to leave his mark in history even if it meant casting aside everything he had accomplished in his life, whether it be his title as general first-class or his position as the shinobi chief?

Abel was selfish and haughty and showed not a whit of concern for other people’s positions, but he was still the emperor of Volakia. He understood the value of his life in the line of succession. If he died, the empire would be shaken to its core. That was something he was keenly aware of as the emperor, and it conveyed a sense of responsibility anyone would feel, even if none would feel it so strongly as he.

But Orbart Dankelken was different.

He did not mind dying to achieve his ambition, and it did not matter to him how much trouble it caused the rest of the world. That abnormal and destructive line of thinking was the darkness that not even Abel could fully grasp.

However…

“Mr. Orbart, isn’t your goal the emperor, not the First seat?”

…Subaru Natsuki knew the darkness lurking within Orbart Dankelken.

2

In a flash, the color, the scent, the feel of the air changed.

“………”

Orbart hadn’t so much as budged under the watchful eyes of Al and Talitta, both of whom were bristling with open hostility and practically itching to act on it. But now his gaze turned to the child Subaru because he could not ignore what he’d just heard.

“Boyo, don’t start butting in all of a sudden. You about gave me a heart attack.”

“Is that because I interrupted? Or is it because…?”

“Because you’re right? Kah-ha-ha-ha! If that’s true, then I’d be one insane old man.”

“Going after the emperor, as in killing him? That’s a little too much of a leap in logic, Bro. What would be in it for him?”

“Well, I can understand the argument for infamy over being forgotten, but one-arm over there’s right. That line of thinking is a bit too out there.”

Al’s voice was stiff with disbelief, and Orbart naturally picked up on that doubt.

But his easygoing escape was about to get harder.

“You didn’t deny it, Mr. Orbart.”

Subaru knew this was risky.

“………”

Orbart’s goal was to assassinate the emperor. As such, they could not reveal either Abel or the fake emperor, meaning they had lost their only bargaining chips.

Keep our goals hidden while revealing his secret.

“Sheesh, how am I supposed to deal with folks who don’t listen?”

“If that’s how it’s gonna be, guess I’ll just have to change course, too.”

“…Don’t do anything rash, gramps.”

“I’m not, okay? I’m just gonna leave, since it’s a waste of time hanging around here.”

“…Do you really think you can just walk out of here?”

“Ahh, you don’t want to let me go because you want to unshrink your friends. Unfortunately, you’re asking too much. I’m gonna leave without doing a thing.”

“Me? I think I was twenty?”

“Then if you just wait ten years, you’ll be back to normal, won’t you? Not that I know for sure.”

Even if we avoid triggering the most dangerous event with Orbart, if we let him go, we’ll be stuck like this…

“What if I grant you an opportunity to kill the emperor?”

“We’re just talking past each other here. ‘Kill the emperor’? Do you hear yourse—?”

“If your aim is the emperor’s life, you should have had ample opportunity already, and yet you never acted. Because of the flames of the Sunlight Blade that protects the emperor.”

“You—”

But he was pulled back by the hand squeezing his. Looking to his side, he saw Louis peering into his eyes. Her blue eyes were wavering slightly, talking to him. Telling him she could fly at any moment.

“………”

Seeing her earnest gaze, Subaru just barely managed to get ahold of himself. Looking up, Yoruna was waiting quietly for a response to her question, not trying to hurry Subaru at all.

It’s too soon to give up.

She was asking if Tanza was why they were in the palace. That was right, but only partially right. So he gambled on that other part.

“Umm, Miss Yoruna… I mean, Lady Yoruna.”

“What is it?”

“Is Tanza in the palace?”

Making up his mind, he asked the question. Yoruna’s eyes narrowed. It was not even a second, but Subaru experienced what a rat caught by a fox probably felt.

Though that’s probably too generous a comparison. For us.

For a few seconds that seemed like an eternity, he waited…

“Unfortunately, Tanza is out on an errand. Though she should be returning any moment now…”

“…!”

Subaru clenched Louis’s hand at hearing that, clenched it hard enough that she started looking around to see where he was pointing.

He was apologetic, but that was not a signal; it was him celebrating. He had won his gamble.

Yoruna’s question was not because she realized their identity or their reason for being here.

“Dear me, Tanza is a troublesome one. I appreciate her devotion, but I cannot have her work as an attendant if she forgets her promises to her friends.”

“F-friends…?”

“She is an upright and honest girl, yes? Yet I am always telling her that it is not enough for that commendable devotion to be dedicated solely toward me.”

The way she said that made it seem like she really did believe they were Tanza’s friends.

It did not really befit the scary, mischievous, and immeasurable nature of the master of this Demon City that he had seen yesterday, though. It was like a kindly adult showing concern for a familiar child.

As if hammering that impression home, Yoruna exhaled slightly.

“While it is a result of Tanza’s carelessness, it would be unacceptable to send you away… Come, I will show you in.”

“Eh…?! Y-you will, Lady Yoruna?!”

“Au?”

Turning elegantly, she walked with a splendid, careful step that did not make a sound, even with how thick the soles of her shoes were. Subaru was almost taken in just by the sight, and he was taken aback at his slow reaction to her offer.

Yoruna hid her smile behind her sleeve.

“This is my palace. It is of course my role to provide hospitality. With Tanza out, I shall also keep you company.”

“Ah, umm…”

“This is the first time a friend of hers has come here. Now, please follow me.” Yoruna gestured with her chin.

Subaru was deeply unsure of what to do. He did not need to waste any time worrying about the possibility of a trap, since there was no reason for her to set out a trap for them. She only needed a finger to deal with Subaru, and maybe a couple more to handle Louis.

That meant it was an offer made in good faith.

But then what about how she seemed yesterday…?

“Uau.”

Louis pulled at Subaru’s hand as he struggled with doubts. Looking, he saw her pointing at Yoruna, seemingly telling him to follow. That was the last little push needed to get Subaru’s legs moving.

“………”

Shaking his head, he and Louis walked quickly to catch up to Yoruna. Waiting for that, she smiled and started walking again with a stride to match theirs.

And just like that, they began the odd experience of being shown through the Crimson Lazuli Palace by Yoruna herself.

“Are you children from elsewhere?”

“Y-you can tell?”

“Because you are unfamiliar faces, and you have not received my letter of love.”

She had said that before. That they were unfamiliar faces. And the love letter she mentioned did not ring a bell for Subaru, either, so rather than telling a bad lie, he simply nodded.

“Y-yes, Lady Yoruna. We came from outside the city…with, um, a scary adult.”

“A scary adult, you say? It sounds as if you’ve had it quite hard. Why were you with a scary adult?”

“We just sort of ended up together, I guess…”

He was cautious of her questions while sticking as close to the truth as he could.

It was to a large degree happenstance that he was working together with a scary adult: Abel.

Though I guess that should be past tense now.

It was hard to say if Abel would forgive him for running away with Louis.

And also…

“Can I even forgive myself…?”

I don’t think they have any right to blame me. I was wrong to hide her identity. But this is what happened when I didn’t hide it, so I was right to hide it. If anything, the only thing I should apologize for is not holding on to the secret longer and letting it slip now.

“…It seems you have a complicated relationship with that adult.”

“Eh?”

“A child should not wear such a grave expression… Shall I give that scary adult a punishment?”

Yoruna’s raised sleeve swayed gently as she offered her services.

“A punishment… Eh? You, Lady Yoruna?”

“Despite how it may look, I am actually quite strong,” she said with a chuckle.

Imagining Abel receiving the punishment, Subaru shook his head forcefully.

“Thank you for worrying about me, but it’s okay! I’m sure it would be better to just talk it through…”

“Is that so? If it is someone who can be reasoned with, then that is certainly for the best. In this world, there are all sorts who cannot be reasoned with, though.”

“…Lady Yoruna.”

“Hmm?”

He hesitated for a moment, unsure whether to say it, which caused Yoruna to stop.

Shrunken down like this, my decisiveness and mental capacity are worse, but the biggest problem is this lack of control, this feeling like I can’t stop myself. It was the same when I ran off with Louis. And sneaking into the palace without enough preparation. I just acted without thinking.

I was worried about saying it earlier, but…

“Umm, I’m surprised you listened to me. I just assumed that all important people are scary…”

He was fully aware it was a rude thing to say, and he could not bring himself to look her in the eyes as he finished, but her reaction was just a thoughtful sound before she spoke again.

“You do not appear to be demi-humans.”

“Umm, yes, that’s right.”

“From your eyes, how does this city appear to you?”

“This city…?”

It was a sudden question. Subaru looked out the small window in the hallway. It was rather high up in the wall, so with his current height, he could not look outside very well. But he could see a blue sky, and he knew the city lay just out of sight.

“It’s an amazing, bustling city. And it’s home to lots of different kinds of people.”

Carefully choosing his words, he tried to give as honest an answer as he could. He had the impression of a bustling and lively town from the very start. It looked that way, too, with how built up it was and with how everything connected and intermingled, and there was an incredible number of different races all living together there.

It was a city that left an impact on the eyes and ears.

“You are an honest child. But your words are a comfort to my ears.”

Yoruna’s lips broke into a faint smile. And then she looked out the window, at what was surely a different scene than what Subaru saw.

“This city is a gathering place for those who struggle to live elsewhere. Children who were treated as insignificant and had no place to go… Children who would not be noticed even if they called out and raised their voices.”

“Even if they…”

“If I did not lend an ear to those children in this final place they’ve found, then who else would?”

She puffed at the pipe as a warm light filled her eyes. When he realized it was affection, Subaru felt truly ashamed of himself.

“She is a deeply affectionate person. She loves her allies and loathes her enemies—A lover of all who live in the Demon City.”

That was how Tanza had described Yoruna yesterday. At the time, Subaru did not really understand what she meant. When he heard about the soul marriage from Abel, he had assumed it only referred to her power.

But this is probably what Tanza really meant.

It showed exactly what Yoruna Mishigure valued most of all.

“I’m sorry, Miss Yoruna… I thought you were a scary person…”

He acted without thinking again and said what he was truly thinking. Yoruna exhaled a stream of purple smoke with a smile when she heard that.

“There is no need to apologize. The reason important people seem scary is because they are also scared they may not seem scary enough. It is easier to be feared.”

“Important people want to be feared…?”

Huh. It feels like that’s something I should really remember.

It also felt like that was something that applied to Yoruna, too.

“You need not worry. I am not so pathetic as to be angered by a child over something so trivial. I just so happen to be in a good mood.”

“Au?”

“Yes, that is right. I just received a sign that a thing which I have long desired may at last be in reach.”

She looked pleased as she swung her sleeve again.

There was no sign of anger in her response. It was probably like she said; she was in a good mood, and she was not the sort to be immature in dealing with a child.

The letter Abel sent her is probably the reason why she is in a good mood…

“…”

Thinking that, Subaru this time held it in and carefully worried about what to do.

Whether the letter Yoruna interpreted as a step in the right direction would have its intended effect depended on Abel and the messengers safely reaching the Crimson Lazuli Palace. But it was none other than Yoruna’s attendant Tanza who was getting in the way.

It’s clear from before that she cares about Tanza. What side would Yoruna take if her wishes and Tanza’s clashed?

Yoruna, who had rebelled against the emperor before for the sake of a single person.

What will she do if she finds out the real situation…?

“…You have quite the grave expression again.”

Yoruna tapped her own brow, pointing out Subaru’s anguish. Drawn by her gesture, Louis tapped her forehead, too.

Looking at them, Subaru sighed slightly.

This might be getting ahead of myself, too. But I don’t have the brains to figure out if it’s right or wrong…

“Umm, there’s something I’d like to ask you, Miss Yoruna…”

A man sat atop the blue and red tiles lining the roof of the Crimson Lazuli Palace’s keep.

Taking in the special clear breeze that such high places enjoyed, he put his lips to a gourd he pulled from his cloak and wet his dry throat with liquor while looking out at the scene below.

“Kah-ha-ha-ha. It’s a grand view.”

The old man laughed while looking out at the various styles all mixing and melding, creating an intricate and fascinating cityscape. His hoarse laughter danced in the breeze, fading into nothingness. The way it seemed to be swallowed up in the hustle and bustle of the Demon City delighted the old man.

He loved chaotic things. A chaotic cityscape, the melting pot of all different races, the various motives and intentions going hither and thither. The confusion of it all just made him want to encourage it somehow.

“It’s a bad habit of old men to mix all their food up together to eat. But…”

Tilting the gourd up and then wiping the liquor that spilled out with his sleeve, he shrugged. Still sitting cross-legged, he spun on his butt and cocked an eyebrow.

It was quite the mouthwatering scene for an old man who loved chaos.

“Now, that’s a group I didn’t expect to see here.”

Three figures stepped out onto the tiles right in front of him.

“I found you, Mr. Orbart!”

A boy who pointed straight at Orbart, a blond-haired girl holding his hand, and standing behind them like their guardian, the ruler of the Demon City.

CHAPTER 6

AN UNYIELDING LOVE

1

He could feel the ticklish warm, sunny breeze gently tousling his hair, Louis’s hand in his, and the firm presence of the tall woman behind him.

He stood at the summit of the Crimson Lazuli Palace, atop the broad room that sat at its highest floor, on the tiles of the palace’s roof, at the place closest to the sky from which they could see all of Chaosflame.

This was the closest place to the abyss Subaru could think of.

“You’re really mean, Mr. Orbart.”

With his free hand, Subaru pointed at the old man drinking from a gourd, sitting on the roof of the palace.

There was a glugging sound as he drank the liquor in the gourd.

“Are you hungry, kiddo?”

“…H-hungry?”

“Aye, that’s right. You’ve been all aflutter since right after waking up. Didn’t have time to eat anything, did you? The condition of your stomach is what determines the condition of your head and your body, after all.”

Setting the gourd down, Orbart pulled another object out of his cloak. Subaru was a little wary as the old man unwrapped it and revealed a dark round thing the size of a golf ball.

“A ration ball. They’re crucial for us shinobi. Just one of these’ll tide you over for a day, keeping your head and body moving smooth. But it tastes terrible, this here ball.”

“It’s bad…”

“That’s right. It’ll make your eyes pop out. But I’ve been a shinobi a long time. I’ve got a long history with these here balls… Every time I ate one out on a job, I would think to myself, ‘When are those old men in the village gonna retire already, so I don’t have to eat this anymore?’”

As he looked at the ball in his hand, Orbart’s lips curled.

It looked like an emergency ration that had been made with no thought given to taste, so Orbart was probably telling the truth.

“But then why not do that? You’re the leader of the shinobi village, right? You’re important, aren’t you?”

“That’s right. I’m stronger and bigger than any of those old-timers who pushed me around… But for some reason, I still eat these.”

Orbart plopped the ration into his mouth, and even though he said how horrible it was, he bit down on it and swallowed, and then he opened his mouth to show he actually ate it.

“In the end, I couldn’t break the habit. This little ball with everything mashed up together without any concern for flavor or appearance is my favorite food. Funny, ain’t it? Kah-ha-ha-ha!”

Orbart’s teeth clicked together as he laughed. Something about his reaction was uncanny.

Subaru did not know what Orbart was trying to say with that story, but he felt like that was not just because of his immaturity. But I don’t think I should just ignore it, either.

It felt like it was some sort of praise or compliment from Orbart.

“Old Man Orbart, this is my palace.”

Once their conversation was finished, the master of the Demon City, Yoruna Mishigure, spoke up.

Meeting her blue eyes, Orbart stopped smiling.

“Of course. I know that well. It feels pretty good to sit my ass down without the owner knowing, too. The secret to a long life is doing things you love.”

“That is an odd thing to say for one who wishes to live long enough to reach an even older age.”

“Oh, you think that’s odd?”

“Is it not foolish for the secret to a long life to shorten your life?”

Putting her sleeve to her mouth, Yoruna smiled bewitchingly, taunting Orbart.

The air crackled as two Divine Generals stared each other down. Orbart just pulled out another ration ball and plopped it into his mouth.

“Well now, seems like you’re awfully angry, but does me having lunch with a great view really bother you so much? That’s not very nice.”

“As it happens, unlike you, I am not the sort to act boorishly over such a trivial matter. However, I have heard that you misled children and deceived my retainer, and as such, there are certain things I must do as the master of this city.”

“Ho-ho-hoo.”

Orbart’s eyes narrowed, and he whistled as Yoruna stared him down. He chewed the ration in his mouth and then turned his heavy brow and eyes to Subaru and Louis.

Guessing the meaning, Subaru gave a big nod.

“Sorry, but I told on you. This isn’t really against the rules you set. And you were the one who had us attacked.”

“Kah-ha-ha! Look at the balls on you, kiddo. But you’re right. I started it, so I won’t grumble, but…”

“…?”

“Your head’s having trouble keeping up with things, isn’t it? Good job figuring all that out. You wouldn’t happen to be a member of the Volakian royal family, would you? You’ve got a nasty personality just like them.”

“Please don’t say something so scary…”

Just on hair color alone, Subaru did have the same sort of black hair as the current emperor Abel, but there were too many differences aside from that. His face, the length of his legs, and…

“I know how to say thank you when someone does something for me.”

“And with a smile and in a loud voice. Just as a child should be. I would like Tanza to learn that from you. Nonetheless…”

Yoruna smiled and complimented Subaru’s mischievous answer, but then her voice settled to a lower register. The air chilled along with that, indicating this was the end of the preliminary discussion.

For no other reason than…

“I cannot chide my admirable retainer when she isn’t even present. Now then, where have you hidden her, Old Man Orbart?”

Yoruna’s question was the main reason she was here.

After stumbling into Yoruna the moment they entered the palace and learning a bit more about her personality, Subaru decided to take a big gamble.

He told Yoruna everything he could, including the general situation, and about the game of hide-and-seek unfolding across Chaosflame. Of course he kept Abel’s identity secret, and that several members of their party had been turned into children by Orbart. He mainly focused on how he and Louis were related to the messengers from yesterday and that they were currently chasing after Orbart in a game of hide-and-seek—and that Tanza was involved.

He pleaded his case as earnestly as he could and tried to the best of his ability to keep things as grounded as he could to resolve her suspicions. Hearing him out after he made up his mind, Yoruna thought for a few moments…

I am not the sort of woman who would fail to discern the truth in an earnest child’s plea.

And she agreed to accompany Subaru and Louis to the roof of the palace.

“Honestly, I didn’t think she was the sort of person who could be reasoned with like this…”

“Auau.”

“Yeah, I know.”

Louis pouted and swung her hand that was holding his. She was warning him not to let his guard down, and he nodded.

The reason they were able to reach this roof was thanks to multiple converging coincidences.

Separating from Abel and his wily tricks; figuring out the riddle, thanks to Ubirk’s advice; and being found directly by Yoruna, rather than by a guard, because he had come with Louis instead of Al or Medium.

And Subaru had gambled big even though he was the one who had changed the most from the age regression. The biggest reason Yoruna had listened was because he had been honest, and she interpreted that as the earnest plea of a child.

There were adults who would laugh off a child and not take them seriously, but there were also adults who took children at their word and answered earnestly.

I never would have thought one of the Nine Divine Generals standing atop the empire would be one, though.

“Someone said that she was mad…”

Logically, anyone who lived by Volakia’s dog-eat-dog philosophy could not condone her behavior.

But it sounded absurd to Subaru after she had been so kind to him. He was determined to correct the misunderstanding for Zikr whenever he got back to Guaral.

While he was deciding that, though, Yoruna had raised two fingers.

“I have two demands.”

“Demands, eh? Well, might as well say them.”

“First of all, return Tanza to me.”

“Hey now, sounds like you just can’t bear to let your kids go. As it happens, that girl’s got a mind of her own. If she didn’t, she wouldn’t go planning something while keeping it secret from—”

“Silence.”

Orbart was laughing as he practically admitted to conspiring with Tanza, but Yoruna interrupted him with a single sharp word. It was quiet but impactful, brimming with a power that seemed liable to change the very color of the sky. Slapping down Orbart’s snarky reply, Yoruna brought the pipe to her lips and slowly filled her lungs with smoke.

“As it happens, I will not hear Tanza’s appeal or explanation from any lips save her own. I especially will not have them twisted by a vicious old man’s tongue.”

“Kah-ha-ha, you really don’t like me.”

“I’m sure you can think of sufficient reasons why that might be.”

Yoruna cocked her head, the hair ornaments jingling as she flashed an aggressive smile. Her luxuriously braided hair and the ornamental hairpin sticking out, and even her adorned visage, were all her weapons.

Important people want to be feared.

It was Yoruna who taught Subaru that. And he started to wonder if it was not just fear. Maybe beauty was the same.

“Well, I heard the first demand. The next up is the second one.”

“But of course. Put an end to the game with these children.”

“Game, huh? You know, it may look like a game, but this is a serious match.”

“I made myself clear in His Highness’s presence yesterday, did I not? Messengers are not to be meddled with. Even His Highness will respect that.”

Ironically, that very message had been conveyed by Tanza as well.

In that light, Orbart’s actions looked like a difficult to accept betrayal. Yoruna showed no interest in any excuses about how he had not directly raised a hand.

Subaru’s heart was racing, caught somewhere between freezing over and emotions boiling over. Yoruna maintained a polite and welcoming tone, and her expression was as gentle as ever.

But she’s mad. I know that much. I’ve seen a lot of seriously mad people.

People who were seriously mad would feed their very life force into their fiery emotions. It was something you could feel on your skin just by being near them. That was the power of pure anger.

“Uuu…”

Louis groaned slightly at the dangerous mood hanging in the air. Even Louis dared not do anything reckless when Yoruna and Orbart were facing off against each other. They were nothing like the pursuers they had run into along the way here, and her animal instincts screamed that loud and clear.

Or maybe she was just concerned about Subaru getting caught up in the fighting…

“Ngh, Mr. Orbart!”

Shaking his head, Subaru shouted Orbart’s name. The mood in the air was crackling with tension, ready to erupt. Orbart dexterously moved just one eye to look at Subaru.

Once he had his attention, Subaru bit his lip and opened his mouth.

“L-let’s just call it a draw.”

“…Eh?”

Orbart’s left eye, and just his left eye, widened at that offer.

“Well…! It is a draw!” Subaru shouted impatiently. “You tried to do something that kinda sorta went against the spirit of the rules, and I told on you to Miss Yoruna. We both went over the line, so…”

“So we just apologize and call it there, huh?”

“Y-yeah, that’s right! That’s not so bad, is it? We can talk about what you wanted to know, and our problem can be resolved, too!”

What Orbart wanted to know was some secret of the emperor’s that Abel knew. Subaru did not know much about it, but Orbart would be more willing to accept that if he got something out of it. The whole point of the hide-and-seek was a test of intelligence and skill to see if their information could be trusted anyway.

“We found you twice, and not the three times we set, but…you can give us that, right? We worked hard to get all the way up to the top of this palace, so we deserve some praise!”

“Kah-ha-ha, ‘praise me,’ eh? You’re an honest kiddo. Out of curiosity, were you the one who figured out my hiding place here? Or was it that demon-masked youngster?”

“M-mhm, I did. I just happened to think of it… There was one other possibility, too.”

And Abel and them might just be going there.

Either way, sooner or later, they would come to the palace. Subaru had just gotten a head start because of Louis’s warp and Ubirk’s advice.

But if he could earn some credit here, it might make it easier for him to convince Abel and the others. And if it was still hard, he could maybe try to get Yoruna on his side.

Though there’s no telling how she would move if she knew Louis’s identity.

“Anyway! What do you say, Mr. Orbart? Will you take my…our offer?”

Brushing aside those negative thoughts, Subaru pleaded with Orbart.

He called it “our offer” because he was going to need Yoruna’s help smoothing this out. If she decided she could not forgive Orbart for involving Tanza in his scheme, then Subaru’s desperate plan would collapse.

But…

“………”

Closing an eye, pipe at her lips, Yoruna did not object. It seemed like she was willing to respect Subaru’s thoughts.

I’m so, so grateful. I seriously appreciate it.

He did not want to waste the trust or kindness or whatever it was that Yoruna had placed in him.

“Mr. Orbart.”

He called out again, expecting a compromise. Meeting his hopeful gaze, Orbart hooked a finger into his gourd and raised it to his lips, drinking the last drop.

“Hey, kiddo. I don’t have a clue if this is only how you think now as a child, or if that’s how your brain always worked, but…”

“………”

“Unfortunately, I don’t like dropping a match once I’ve started. Old men are stubborn, you know?”

Smirking unpleasantly, the old codger crushed the gourd in his hand, shattering it. The fragments flew through the air as Subaru gasped.

The next moment…

“You obstinate old man. You will regret refusing this child’s hand.”

Yoruna leaped, swinging her long leg down and splitting the palace’s keep in two with a thunderous crack.

She raised her thick-soled sandal high into the air and slammed it straight down.

In a flash, the palace keep split apart from the impact. It shattered and exploded with a loud crash, like a bomb had landed.

Loose tiles flew through the air, and a dense smoke rose as Yoruna stood gallantly at the heart of the explosion, kimono rustling in the air.

In a single breath, she had leaped and annihilated the palace keep with her awesome destructive power. The palace keep was split clean in two, marring the beautiful exterior of the Crimson Lazuli Palace.

“Whooooaaaa?!”

Subaru shouted as he was pulled away by Louis leaping out of the smoke. Rolling across the roof, he just managed to avoid getting caught in the destruction.

But…

“Damn it! Why’d it have to turn out like this…?!”

Pulled up by Louis, Subaru tearfully bemoaned this result.

Stubborn old Orbart refused my offer, so it turned into a fight even though I didn’t wanna fight and didn’t want to make anyone else fight either.

“Miss Yoruna!”

“You should stay back. I cannot easily restrain myself. And also…”

Yoruna did not look back as she drew her foot out of the roof and then brushed away the rubble from the hem of her kimono and then turned her eyes overhead.

“As expected, you are quite spry.”

In the rubble, smoke, and tile fragments, a small shadow spun in place—Orbart.

He laughed, baring his teeth.

“Weren’t we not supposed to get into it? …Does this mean you don’t mind anymore?”

“I am surprised that you believe you can win against me in this city. If you have gone senile, I would recommend you yield your Divine General title to another.”

“Kah-ha-ha! That’ll never happen. I’m planning to be the longest-lived Divine General.”

Both sets of eyes gleamed as they met, readying themselves.

Yoruna exhaled a puff of smoke from her mouth, and Orbart turned upside down in midair. Kicking off the smoke that had spread in the air, he flew like an arrow.

“Ngh!”

His slicing kick crashed straight into the puff of smoke Yoruna had just exhaled. The smoke, which should not have been solid or had any real mass, caught Orbart’s kick and absorbed the impact.

But even if his attack was blocked in an unexpected way, Orbart did not simply linger.

“Oooooshaaaa!!!”

Spinning his short legs quickly, he unleashed a furious succession of ten, twenty kicks. The smoke dispersed the impact of one or two kicks, but it scattered gradually with each kick, until finally it lost its form and was no longer useful as a shield.

That it even managed to work that way at all is weird, but…

“That’s an interesting trick. I’d like to have a scroll for it.”

“Unfortunately, it is a secret technique impossible for a shinobi who cannot love anyone.”

As Orbart broke through the smoke, Yoruna’s pipe swung right in front of his eyes. It was not really the right weight or length to be useful as a club, but when Orbart tried to meet it with his arm—or no, with a kunai hidden up his sleeve—there was a screech, and the kunai shattered. The old man’s tiny body went flying backward.

“Nuoo?! What is that pipe?!”

“A gift from long ago. One of my beloved accessories.”

“My kunai’s pretty old, and I liked it, too.”

Orbart landed with a splash of tiles, smirking provocatively at Yoruna’s response. The next moment, his smirk faded as he started bouncing all around Yoruna at a speed normal people could not follow.

In years past, there was a boxer who used to float like a butterfly and sting like a bee, and that was exactly what Orbart seemed to be re-creating with the shattered palace keep as his stage.

“You are bursting with energy, but perhaps a little too mischievous.”

The tiles exploded wherever Orbart stepped, and when he appeared the next moment, he let fly with a single sharp blow right at Yoruna, before flitting away again. With her supernatural reflexes, she caught the blows with her pipe or else dodged, responding with moves that seemed like a gentle dance.

Subaru was entranced by their superhuman clash.

“Au…!”

Louis was quivering at Subaru’s side as she watched the same scene unfold. It felt like this battle was being fought on a level where even Louis might not be able to intervene. No matter who won, the resulting destruction would be unbelievable.

If the disaster was left to fester, everyone in the city would notice, in which case, the people who adored Yoruna and Orbart’s presumed comrades in the false emperor’s group would all have to act.

What remained after that would be a war that consumed the entire city—far from the ideal that Subaru had pictured.

“Shiiiiiyaaa!”

The spinning old man raised his voice, piercing the roof right in front of Yoruna. The next moment, there was a shock wave through the roof, exploding beneath Yoruna, sending her high into the air and flipping the things in the air with the things on the roof.

“There, how do you like that?!”

The next moment, countless shuriken raced toward Yoruna from all directions.

When did he throw them? It was an unpredictable shinobi skill. The spinning blades traced different arcs that threatened to tear into Yoruna’s soft skin.

Just before her pale skin and beautiful kimono were shredded and stained with blood…

Sorry, Yoruna.
