Who could blame them for wanting to protect their peace? All the more so when the lord of the city cares so much about them.

What was so different about that from the world the girl he loved wanted?

“………”

This was a place where no one was tied down, where everyone had the freedom to be themselves and not hide, so this was a place where people felt free to express themselves, and it was brimming with an untamed energy that no one could deny.

In a sense, this was a utopia where anyone could live.

Should we really pull Yoruna away from a place like this?

All of it was—

Whatever intentions he had in repudiating me…

Orbart immediately pulled back his outstretched hand, but it was too late. His wrinkled old right hand turned to dust from the wrist down and disappeared.

“Child—”

“Uau!!!”

Yoruna’s eyes opened wide in shock as she pulled Louis close, holding the struggling girl tight while leaping back as fast as she could.

The next moment, a dark shadow filled their entire field of view, swallowing the tower of the beautiful Crimson Lazuli Palace, and then the upper floors and the middle floors.

“Your Highness! That…”

“………”

Kafma was bristling as he stood beside the emperor he was duty bound to protect. He sensed the insects within him all cowering as he watched the incredible scene unfolding in the distance through the window.

Vincent stood up and turned his sharp gaze on the blackening palace, eyes blinking in deep and careful thought.

“That’s…the palace…Lady Yoruna…”

“Aaa, aaaaa, aaaaaaaaaaa!!!!”

“Al?!”

Dumbstruck, the young ones stared in shock at what was happening.

As the destruction unfolded, Tanza feared for her mistress, and Al screamed louder than anyone in the city, perhaps the world.

Medium ran over, supporting Al’s shoulder, and unable to understand what was going on at all, she gulped and looked pleadingly toward Abel.

“Dear oh dear…this is a little beyond what I saw coming.”

“You are…”

Ubirk shaded his eyes, looking at the destruction of the palace in the distance while murmuring to himself, while Talitta, standing across from him, ground her teeth.

“…Is this the true nature of what you carry inside you?”

Abel saw the same thing that the false emperor and the crying child saw. Clenching his fists, hiding the lip he was biting hard enough to draw blood behind his mask, his expression became as twisted as the visage engraved in the mask as he glared at the darkness.

7

I love you.

I love you. I love you. I love you.

I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you.

I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you.

It exceeded all dimensions in scale, overwriting and crushing Subaru Natsuki’s very being—a love like a curse that would never let him go.

He had experienced a hellish world without love, and he also knew that he was still loved. But at the same time, it was important to understand that not every love should be affirmed.

There was a price to pay for not knowing that. Because he was ignorant of why it was feared, why it was avoided.

He transformed into a black shadow, swallowing and destroying everything while cheering.

Cheering a reunion, a confluence, an embrace, fetters, fate, striving.

Cheering a confession, regret, jealousy, mystery, exaltation, dedication.

He had known a hellish world devoid of love, so what hell would befall a world overflowing with love?

Subaru did not know. He did not know at all. But in this situation where no one understood anything, there was only one thing he could say.

The utopia for the persecuted, Demon City Chaosflame, had been toppled by none other than Subaru Natsuki’s karma.

Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

INTERLUDE

FILLING THE BLUE SKY

1

At the same time a beautiful palace far to the west was being consumed by a dark shadow…

“Ms. Priscilla?”

Rem, who was washing a bathing woman’s hair, watched as the woman stood up. Her hair slipped from Rem’s fingers as the woman went calmly to the bath’s window.

This was Priscilla Bariel, a regal woman with dazzling orange hair and snowy white skin, a woman whose connection with Rem was difficult to describe.

She was a fiery woman who acted with greater haughtiness than anyone in the fortified city where Rem had remained. She had declared she would keep Rem at her side while she remained in the city, and true to her word, she brought Rem everywhere, tasking Rem with waiting on her hand and foot, but also making time to speak with her.

The one constant was this daily bath time, but…

“Ms. Priscilla, you haven’t finished bathing…ah!”

Not listening, Priscilla opened the window without hesitation, her naked body entirely bare as the outside wind blew through the bathhouse.

The steam that had been billowing so luxuriously quickly scattered, but the surprises did not stop there. Priscilla leaned out the open window, stepping onto the balcony.

Rem frantically followed, holding a towel.

“Wh-what are you doing? People can see you! Just because this is the highest floor…”

“The sky.”

“The sky…? This balcony isn’t that high. Come now, let’s return before the water—”

She did not manage to finish her plea, though. Priscilla brought her finger to Rem’s lips. Wearing the towel laid over her shoulders like a cape, she looked at Rem with her blood-colored eyes.

“Look at the sky, Rem. It seems our vacation is at an end.”

Grasping the seriousness in Priscilla’s eyes, Rem gulped. And, wearing a bathing suit herself, she peered up at the same sky as Priscilla. She strained her blue eyes to see what Priscilla had seen.

But there was no need to try so hard, since…

“That…is…”

Atop the balcony, at the brightest point of the wind hour, there was a glittering in the enormous sun overhead. Black dots appeared in the almost white light. One, then two, then more and more. They continued increasing, until finally their identity became clear.

“Have those below raise arms at once. There is no trifling with a swarm of winged dragons.”

2

She peered down upon the city surrounded by high walls. Her golden eyes narrowed.

High up in the blue sky streaked with clouds, the greatest of beings flapped their wings as a strong wind roared past.

“Fortress city of Guaral.”

Her blood boiled in anticipation at the sight of her target.

That eagerness gradually spread around her, merging with the flapping wings and bestial cries.

It was a little hasty, but it was only natural that it stoked their instincts as hunters. They were apex predators, after all.

“………”

“I know. Let’s do our job properly, like the old-timer said.”

Heeding the admonition of the dragon she was astride, the girl crossed her arms and nodded.

Her blue hair gathered at her shoulders, and her golden eyes glimmered. She wore a flashy uniform, and on her back was her trusty winged blade. That was hardly enough to tell what sort of person she was, but there was one trait that proved she was special—the two black horns growing from her head.

“Everyone ready?”

Countless cries rose up in response, each coming from a majestic master of the open skies. A flock of several hundred dragons had arrived.

Once they descended, there would be roars and shrieks as countless lives were snuffed out.

On the precipice of a grand hunt, the horned creature—Madelyn Eschert—looked upon Guaral once more with her golden eyes and smiled.

This was a declaration of war from the Ninth Divine General, the flying dragon commander who had been ordered to raze the city.

“Tremble in fear. Flee. There’s nowhere to run. The dragons have come.”

<END>

AFTERWORD

Hello, everyone! Good job! This is Tappei Nagatsuki and the mouse-colored cat!

Thank you for reading Volume 29 of Re:Zero! This whole book was dedicated to the Chaosflame arc, but how did the worst hardship to befall Subaru since his sudden arrival in the Volakian Empire appear to you, dear reader? For me, it was very fun to write!

I’ve come up with all sorts of difficulties to inflict on Subaru Natsuki with his Return by Death ability, but I really put a lot of effort into the (self-described) Palace Clash Arc. As an author, it would be a great honor if you enjoyed it.

Incidentally, this volume was as densely packed as ever, and this time I could not choose what to do for the cover and went with something extravagant. The eye-catching cover illustration is, of all things, a character who only appears in the interlude at the very end!

This time, I selfishly pressed Otsuka to make the cover illustration something that anyone who read to the end of the interlude would recognize.

Please take the cover this time as a part of the story! Enjoy!

Now that I’ve cleared that up, it’s time to move on to the usual thanks.

Thank you to my editor I for the warm and generous forgiveness for the significant change to the plot’s contents. I believe your statement that “It’s important to just try writing it” is a wise view. In similar struggles in the future, I will keep to the idea of the plot as a general compass!

Thank you very much to the illustrator Otsuka for creating the illustrations with such attention to my requests with regular discussions! The age-regressed trio are practically new characters, so having an updated design and the like was a great help!

The designer Kusano played an even greater role in the cover illustration than usual, setting it up big and beautiful. Thank you very much! It is thanks to the work and support of everyone that this book exists!

Atori and Aikawa’s adaptation of the fourth arc in Gekkan Comic Alive is ongoing, and getting to see a copy of the draft every month, the beauty of the complete draft is breathtaking!

In addition, thank you very much to everyone else at MF Bunko J’s editorial division, the proofreader, and all of the bookstores. You all do so much to help make these books happen.

And my greatest thanks again go to you, the readers who continue to support this super-long series!

Honestly, it is still a shock to me, but next time is really the thirtieth volume! There still is no end in sight, so I will do my best to keep writing to the end, so please continue to support me! I really am always grateful for it!

May we meet again in the next volume, Volume 30!

February 2022

“And so the curtain falls on Volume 29. I have taken a leading role in the postscript in preparation for the thirtieth volume, but…”

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! Whoever was doing the casting messed up making me the costar! Me and the fox-girl got pretty chippy in the book, after all.”

“Agreed. Were it not for the child, I suspect you would not have stayed on this earth long enough for us to casually chat like this.”

“Well, it’s not so rare for even dead people to speak up here. Who knows? Even if one of us kicked it in the main story, we still might have ended up paired off here.”

“………”

“Oh, did I say something tasteless? Whoops, my bad, my bad.”

“The longer this continues, the shorter your life span seems to shrink, Old Man Orbart. Let us get to the subject at hand for both our sakes.”

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! That sort of consideration ain’t like you. But it’s not like I especially enjoy putting myself in harm’s way, so let’s get to it.”

“…As mentioned at the start, the next volume will be the thirtieth, a nice, big round number.”

“Kaaah! Thirty! That’s a pretty big number. I’m a nasty old man, obviously, but I can still be impressed by something that’s lasted so long.”

“Either way, the schedule is unchanged, and the release should come in June. Additionally, Volume 7 of the short story collection will also be released on the same day.”

“A short story collection! Well, with all that the kiddo’s suffered in the main story, it’d be hard to keep going without a little rest. Not to mention that I caused a lot of that suffering.”

“That you can behave so blithely despite knowing that shows you know no shame, Old Man… I must say I am impressed by the ease with which you live.”

“Hey now, don’t give me that. This is a little secret for you, but a shameless man’s got his own troubles, too.”

“Such thick skin that even sarcasm cannot penetrate. If that child had not intervened, I would have trampled you underfoot.”

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! Then I’ll have to thank the kiddo.”

“But of course, Old Man Orbart. I shall assuredly snap the unforgivable, haughty old tree with my own two hands.”

“Aye, aye, scary. I don’t wanna wet myself or die, so I’ll run to the ends of the world and wait for you.”

“Do so if you are able.”

CHAPTER 1

A BEAST OF AMBITION

1

“………”

When Subaru Natsuki saw himself in the mirror, he went dead silent.

He recognized his own face, of course, but this one was a relic of fading memories and belonged squarely in the past. It was none other than Subaru Natsuki’s childhood face staring back at him.

“What the…?”

When his hand holding the mirror started to tremble, so did his ashen, dumbfounded reflection. He tried to touch his face with his free hand. The boy in the mirror also reached out with the same tentative movements. Judging from his hands and his face, he was maybe ten years old.

Subaru had been a late bloomer and was always on the shorter side as a kid, but…

“What the hell is going on?!” Subaru shouted. This was no time for reminiscing.

What a nightmare. There was no other way to describe how absurd this was. Subaru had never felt desperate enough to return to his childhood in such a dramatic fashion. Something had clearly gone terribly wrong.

Becoming ten years younger overnight…

“I can’t just sit around like this…”

Regaining some of his composure, Subaru hurried to the door of the room.

There was no way Chaosflame inns just happened to offer complimentary rejuvenation packages with every stay. It was safer to assume that this was the work of an enemy.

I’ve gotta warn everyone and figure out a way to undo this…

“Guys, something terrible’s happened! I’m sure you can tell, but—”

“Ah! So you’re smaller, too!”

“Bwuh?!”

Finding the doorknob harder to reach than usual, Subaru managed to turn it and burst into the room, only to be greeted by an unbelievable scene that he probably should have seen coming.

A girl with an adorably cute face beamed at him and waved. Her clear blue eyes, distinctive blond hair, and unmistakable sunny disposition…

“It doesn’t seem possible, but…is that you, Medium?”

“That’s right! It’s the strangest thing. When I woke up, I became a kid again! But seeing that the same thing happened to you is a relief! At least I’m not alone!”

The girl who looked maybe twelve or thirteen was undoubtedly Medium O’Connell. She was dressed in a thin bit of cloth and was evidently suffering from the same condition as Subaru. Even after losing a decade’s worth of height, she was still half a head taller than Subaru.

“Look, this is serious. We can’t relax just because we’re not alone—Whoa?!”

“Uuuu!”

An unexpected collision took Subaru completely by surprise. As he tumbled over with an audible thud, he felt a weight settle on top of him. It made him groan like a squashed frog.

“Aaah! No, Louis! Subaru’s small now!”

“Aaa, uuu!”

“Gaaah! I’m tiny, too! I can’t lift you up!”

It felt like a wild animal had clambered onto Subaru’s chest, and though Medium tried her best to help, her shrunken body didn’t have the strength to stop the rampage.

Young Subaru Natsuki was helpless against the vile beast…

“Louis, stop! You’re going to crush Subaru!”

With that sharp rebuke, the offending creature was pulled away at last. Looking up, Subaru saw Louis receding into the distance with a sad look on her face, for some reason.

It was Talitta who had grabbed her. Subaru felt a wave of relief at seeing the woman in her formal black suit.

“Phew, thanks Talitta!” Medium said. “I wasn’t strong enough to lift her up.”

“Th-think nothing of it… Subaru, are you unharmed?”

“Unharmed isn’t how I’d phrase it, but… Anyway, I’m glad nothing weird happened to you, Talitta.”

Subaru accepted Medium’s outstretched hand and rose to his feet. He glanced across the room at the sofa. Sitting there and watching in silence was a black-haired man in a mask—the leader of this group, the fugitive emperor Abel.

Subaru had a thing or two to say about how the man had done absolutely nothing to help, but he was also thankful that he hadn’t transformed the way Subaru or Medium had.

“Abel, it’s at least good to see that nothing happened to—”

“Disgraceful.”

Abel interrupted Subaru with obvious displeasure. Subaru was speechless for a moment at how cold it was.

“…Huh, I think I have a pretty adorable baby face, personally.”

That was the most spiteful retort he could manage.

“Calling yourself a baby face, huh? That’s just like you, Bro. And yeah, you are cuter now.”

“…! You’re…”

Subaru was startled by the boy who emerged from one of the other bedrooms. He seemed to be around the same age as Subaru, aside from the ripped-up piece of cloth wrapped around his face.

He didn’t look familiar, but the way he talked and his missing arm made it obvious who he was.

“Al, right…? What’s that you got on your face?”

“Oh, yeah. Did I scare you? My helmet doesn’t fit anymore, and I didn’t have anything else on hand. Sorry, but try not to dwell on it.”

“You can say that, sure, but I’m obviously gonna…”

The visibly younger Al waved lightly. His face covering was haphazardly wrapped, leaving some black hair visible on the back of his head. This was a fresh look for him, but it was a minor detail next to the much bigger changes.

Almost looks like a half-assed serial killer in some old movie.

“…Do you really have to go out of your way to hide your face just because you can’t wear your helmet?”

“That’s not a very thoughtful comment, Bro. I’m not wearing a helmet for show or because I’ve gone crazy. It’s a complex. Just ’cause I look like a kid doesn’t mean I started thinking like one, too.” Al shrugged and gestured at his missing arm. “My arm didn’t grow back, and the scars on my face are still there, too. Same goes for you, right?”

“I guess so, yeah…”

Subaru looked down at his own body. He was wearing a loose shirt that was too large, but beneath it were several white scars that had not healed. They were proof of the time he had spent living in this world and looked out of place on such a young boy.

The scars were also proof that this was not some rewinding of the clock. His body had simply shrunk.

“But shrinking this much in a single night isn’t normal. That sort of thing doesn’t just happen randomly.”

“Yeah. Hmm…,” Medium said, before a new realization hit her. “Wait, I won’t be able to help Flop out with work anymore. Bro’s so scrawny! This might be a big problem!”

“Okay, yes, this is definitely a big blow to the O’Connell family business, but…”

Unless they changed back soon, there would undoubtedly be some serious future consequences. For now, though, Subaru wanted to focus on more immediate problems. His most pressing issue was the lack of clothes that fit, but Al and Medium fought for a living, which was a much bigger concern.

“You mentioned the helmet not fitting, but your sword’s probably an issue, too, right?”

“Sharp observation. I’m not totally useless, but I can’t really swing properly with this cute little arm.”

“Same for me,” Medium confirmed. “It’d probably be rough holding two swords. If it’s just one, then I can probably sort of…argh.”

“Watch out!”

Medium propped up one of her sheaths and drew, only for the sword to slip right out of her hands and bury itself in the floor, narrowly missing Subaru’s nose on the way down. Her face went pale.

“Wah wah wah! Sorry, Subaru! You’re not dead, right?!”

“I-I’m fine, but…that was really dangerous.”

Crestfallen, Medium retrieved the sword and carefully returned it to its sheath. Right up until a day ago, she had wielded her blades like an extension of herself. Now, she could barely hold one. A shocking revelation for someone whose identity revolved around fighting.

“So that means Talitta’s the only one who can fight now?”

“Eeeh! I can still do my best, even if I am small!”

“Look, I’m not doubting your moxie, but I don’t wanna break any labor laws…”

It was wonderful how Medium refused to give up in the face of incredible adversity, but it was important to grasp the reality of the situation.

With Al and Medium like this, the only reliable fighter we have is Talitta. As strong as she is, we can’t rely on her alone when we’re in the middle of enemy territory.

In fact, when that realization dawned on Talitta, her face started to develop a bad twitch.

“You are unexpectedly composed.”

Abel finally broke his silence. The way he spoke made it clear he had been observing them like test subjects.

“I don’t know about that,” Subaru said, snarling. “Maybe the panic just hasn’t set in yet. Or maybe I’ll only realize how big a deal my lost height and weight are after noticing all the new inconveniences.”

“Clearly, it has not impacted your barbed tongue.”

“My cunning and my ability to adapt are two of my few selling points.”

Subaru knew quipping back would just make him seem desperate to get the last word in. Naturally, he decided to do it anyway. And as expected, Abel’s gaze hardened.

“Always talking back…,” Abel said in obvious displeasure, before continuing. “Most likely, it was Orbart Dankelken who changed you.”

“What?!”

Subaru’s eyes went wide. This revelation was earth-shattering.

“You mean the old man we ran into at the palace yesterday…one of the Nine Divine Generals?!”

Orbart was the one who had been accompanying the false emperor at the Crimson Lazuli Palace—and was arguably the third strongest person in the entire empire.

“You sure it was him, Abel?” Al asked.

“There are others who could have changed your appearance, but this is no simple deception. That makes him the most likely suspect.”

“…Personally, I was wondering if that might be that foxy lady’s handiwork.”

While Subaru was recovering from his shock, Al helpfully interrogated Abel’s claim.

Subaru certainly shared Al’s suspicions. There were plenty of reasons to question if Yoruna was responsible. For one thing, the three victims were the same people who had paid her palace a visit. As things stood, Yoruna and Orbart were both prime suspects.

So why was Abel so sure it was Orbart…?

“Can that old man use some kind of magic to shrink people?” Subaru asked.

“There is no hard proof, if that is what you are after. The Nine Divine Generals all have their own secrets. Orbart is no exception. In addition, he is the leader of a group called Shinobi who are especially secretive.”

“Shinobi, huh…? So we’re talking ninjutsu, blending into the night, carrying out assassinations, spying on everyone. Stuff like that?”

“I am not familiar with this ninjutsu you speak of, but the rest are indeed Shinobi’s prime duties… Where did you learn of them?”

The moment he heard the word shinobi, Subaru started listing stereotypical ninja work. Of course, Abel’s gaze made it clear he wasn’t supposed to know all that.

“Oh, uh… Some people who have similar jobs back in my homeland were called ninjas, and…”

Subaru hurriedly made up an excuse and turned to Al for some help. Before he could say anything, Medium shouted “Ah!” in realization. Her big round eyes got even bigger.

“If this is all part of that old man’s scheme, then it probably happened when we were escaping! Remember how he jabbed you and me in the chest?”

“When we were escaping…? Ohhh.”

It took Subaru a second to recall the events of the day before. When they were escaping—or rather, when they were fighting for their lives to clear Yoruna’s spiteful demands. They had managed to evade Kafma’s thorns and were about to make their escape from the castle keep when Orbart joined the fray.

However, none of them had sustained any notable injuries.

I wrote it off back then, but there’s no way one of the Nine Divine Generals would let us off so easily.

“But who would’ve expected him to do this?! Also, Al didn’t get hit, right?!”

“…Sorry, Bro. I was duking it out with him right before I jumped. I wouldn’t be surprised if he jabbed me somewhere. I just didn’t bother worrying about wounds that didn’t kill me.”

Al muttered in a low voice—or at least as low as a young boy could manage—regretting how he had overlooked important details. Of course, there was no reason to be so hard on himself. He had helped get everyone out alive. And Medium had helped just as much. They had done their jobs admirably.

If anything, Subaru was the one who should have noticed.

I’m useless in a fight, so I should at least have been on the lookout for trouble.

“How am I supposed to face Rem like this…? I’m the same size as Beako. Emilia-tan’s gonna treat me like a kid more than ever…”

“I doubt the princess’d play with me even after I became tiny. Gotta say, it feels like there’s no upside in any of this…,” Al muttered.

“Y-you all seem surprisingly calm… I, of course, am completely stunned…”

Talitta had gone pale, finding it hard to stay composed as she held on to Louis, who was flailing around. She almost seemed to feel guilty for being the only one unaffected.

Of course, her take on the situation was the most reasonable of them all. Subaru and Al were simply putting up a brave front.

“Honestly, if I wasn’t joking about it, I’d want to scream.”

“Really?” Talitta asked Subaru.

“Yeah… That’s how disturbing this is.”

It wasn’t being in a younger body that bothered him. It was having his body changed against his will, undermining his very sense of self.

Subaru had experienced countless terrible situations since arriving in this world.

Death naturally topped the list, but over the past year and a half, he had endured plenty of other hardships. And as seasoned as Subaru was now, the feeling of being reshaped by someone else was still unbearable.

“So this is what it feels like to be violated by Lust…”

Subaru gritted his teeth and hugged himself. A low buzzing echoed in his head. It came from the memory of all the people in the Water Gate City who had been transformed into flies by the Archbishop of Lust, still waiting to be saved.

If being changed into a younger version of himself was this terrible, then he could not begin to imagine how dreadful it must feel to be transformed into something so fundamentally different.

Subjecting someone to this…

“Only a vicious old man would do such a thing,” said Abel, arms crossed. His comment took Subaru by surprise. It was like he had read his thoughts.

As their eyes met, Subaru opened and closed his small hand before asking, “This can be undone…right?”

“I cannot say for sure. However, it is natural to think there is some method of reversal.”

“What’s your basis for that?”

“What purpose could there be for a poison that does not immediately kill besides bringing someone to the negotiating table?”

Abel’s conclusion was persuasive.

If this is a ploy to get us to cut a deal, then…

“Then someone should be making contact sooner than—”

Just as Talitta started saying that, a knock came at the door.

“…!”

Everyone tensed and looked at the door. Was it Orbart, coming to feel them out after turning them into children?

“Apologies for intruding so early in the day. I am Lady Yoruna Mishigure’s messenger.”

The voice greeting them from the other side of the door was an unexpected one.

“That’s the deer-girl from yesterday…Tanza. Is this about a response to the letter?” Medium wondered aloud.

“Huh? Oh, right, yeah! The letter!”

Subaru initially deflated when he realized it wasn’t Orbart who had come knocking, until Medium’s question helped him realize why this visitor had come.

“Umm…it’s safe to let her in, right?”

Still feeling a little startled, Subaru checked with Abel before doing anything. The masked man was silent for a moment before finally nodding.

With that, Talitta opened the door and welcomed in the messenger.

“Please pardon me. I have come bearing a message from Lady Yoruna.”

The kimono-clad deer-girl Tanza crossed the threshold.

The young servant glanced around the room and furrowed her otherwise emotionless face. There were four children she did not recognize and a suspicious-looking man in a strange mask gathered there. If anything, it was impressive that she didn’t have a stronger reaction.

“It seems everyone is here… Well…”

“What?”

“…No, it is nothing. My apologies.”

Tanza failed to hide her interest in Abel’s mask. Even after she apologized, she didn’t stop glancing at him curiously. It was actually quite adorable seeing her act her age.

At the same time, it was hard to forget that she had come bearing crucial news, and a quiet tension filled the air.

Tanza bowed deeply and spoke once again.

“Regarding the letter delivered yesterday, Lady Yoruna is ready to make a formal reply. In addition, she wishes to invite all of you to the Crimson Lazuli Palace.”

“…She actually read the letter?”

Even knowing it was rude, Subaru could not help feeling a sense of relief that the letter had in fact been read. There was a distinct chance that Yoruna might have casually decided to tear up the letter even after he and the others had risked so much delivering it. This tense uncertainty was much like dealing with a haughty cat or Priscilla.

In any case, a formal invitation to the palace meant they must have made enough progress that it was worth entertaining a conversation. The only other pressing problem was the age regression…

“The author of the letter and those who visited yesterday to deliver the message are requested to attend.”

“Ack.”

“…?”

Tanza cocked her head and furrowed her brow at that unexpected groan.

Subaru grabbed his chest in an attempt to steady his pounding heart to not let on how shaken he was and summoned his best smile.

“It’s nothing, don’t worry about it.”

Whether she was willing to leave it at that or simply uninterested, Tanza carried on.

“When the bell tolls to mark fire time, please be ready at the gate of the Crimson Lazuli Palace.”

“Understood. You have done well. You may go.”

“…Yes sir. Excuse me.”

The time she had mentioned meant they should show up around noon.

Now that her work here was done, Tanza bowed one last time and turned to leave.

She didn’t get far before Subaru asked, “Um, just to be sure, the person who wrote the letter is the only person who absolutely has to go, and the messengers from yesterday are just extras, right? If, for whatever reason, those messengers might have trouble participating…”

“Lady Yoruna has requested the presence of the messengers.”

“………”

“In this city, no one can go against Lady Yoruna’s wishes.”

Her tone was matter-of-fact, but there was an unshakable conviction in Tanza’s parting reminder.

Once Subaru closed the door behind her, he took a deep breath and spun around.

“Strategy meeting! Now!”

He raised his much shorter arms and summoned his comrades.

2

Yoruna Mishigure had requested their presence at the palace.

Even if they were willing to risk bringing Abel to the palace, the biggest problem was Yoruna’s demand to have the messengers from yesterday accompany him.

If Abel’s conjecture was correct and their age regression had nothing to do with Yoruna, then even if the children went along, it was doubtful whether that would satisfy her.

In the worst case, it might be taken as a sign of bad faith and ruin any chance of striking a deal. They did have the option of being completely honest about their situation and hoping for the best, but…

“Revealing your cards without knowing the other party’s intentions is madness,” Abel flatly stated.

And just this once, Subaru was in complete agreement. Yoruna ruled this city on top of being one of the Nine Divine Generals. His initial impression was that she was a dangerous woman. They had plenty of reasons to be wary of her.

She was a potential ally who could help Abel retake his throne, but she was not someone they could trust without reservation.

“Even if we spilled our guts and told her everything, she might still have an issue with how you were dressed like a girl, Bro. What’cha gonna do if she’s all, like, ‘How dare you deceive me?’ or something like that?”

“Hmm, should I put together a kiddie Natsumi Schwartz getup just to be safe…?”

“P-please, no,” Talitta begged. “You’ll drive me crazy at this rate…”

Telling a lie to cover up another lie is a fairly standard trope, but I guess cross-dressing after turning into a kid to hide the fact that you cross-dressed in the first place does sound kinda insane.

Unlike with Al’s helmet, the wig’s size could be adjusted some, so it was technically possible…

“So what’s the plan?” Medium asked as she cocked her head. “We only have three hours left until it’s time to meet, right?”

She was holding Louis, who was basically the same size as she was now and mirroring her head movement.

Subaru scratched his cheek and said, “First of all, rejecting her invitation is not an option.”

“Damn straight,” Al said. “All our work would go to waste, and we would’ve gotten shrunk for nothing.”

“There would be no gain in that…,” Talitta agreed.

While Subaru nodded in response, he was still considering whether it made sense to retreat.

Insisting on making back the initial bet was the classic prelude to a gambler’s downfall. It was important to know when to cut your losses. This time, the losses happened to be measured in inches.

“I don’t know whether this should be considered a heavy price or a light one…”

“Yeah, rapid aging is obviously bad, but suddenly becoming a kid again is a toughie. Ain’t this super abusable?” Al asked.

“Yeah, if you think of it as a chance to redo everything starting from childhood but with all your memories intact…”

In a sense, restoring youth was sort of like Return by Death in that it increased potential opportunities.

Combining the knowledge and experience of an adult with the physical potential of a young child could make it possible to take on challenges that were previously unthinkable.

Compared to the alternative, age regression at least has some potential advantages…

“It’s easy to make that assumption, yes. But it’s not nearly that convenient.”

The moment a new voice chimed in, Subaru stopped breathing. He wasn’t alone. Everyone in the room froze. But the intruder seemed oblivious to the tension in the air.

“I went ahead and made some tea for myself, but does anyone else want some?” the intruder asked in an easygoing tone as he held up a teacup.

“…!”

Talitta immediately readied her bow and took aim at the wrinkled face of a tiny, almost child-sized old man.
