chapters.text:
Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

Despite how close he was to the nocked arrow, the old man simply shrugged.

“Hey now, gimme a break. I don’t like having scary things pointed at me. Besides, once you get up in years, you gotta hit the head more often. So don’t make me wet myself. I’m practically trembling over here.”

“Don’t trifle with me…! How did you—?”

“—Orbart Dankelken.”

Talitta’s face turned red at the old man, who was unreasonably calm despite her arrow and her open hostility. But before she could finish her question, she was interrupted by Abel. The masked man hadn’t so much as budged from his seat on the sofa. Orbart Dankelken’s eyes narrowed beneath his big bushy eyebrows as he met Abel’s gaze.

The man who so boldly infiltrated their room was none other than the shinobi who was the suspected cause of their age regression.

Orbart broke into a smile and said, “Yesterday confirmed that I’m rather famous, but you leave quite the impression yourself. Where’d you buy a mask like that? I wonder.”

“Enough foolishness, you old tree. Why have you come here?”

“Youngsters just don’t indulge their elders in conversation anymore. The kids in the village keep getting better at ignoring me. I’m one lonely old man, I tell ya, kah-ha-ha-ha!”

Orbart’s hearty laugh hung in the air.

Subaru and the others were finally starting to recover from their initial shock, but the confusion was not entirely gone, and the wariness remained.

“Gramps, how did you get in here? I was watching the door.”

“Oh, you’re smaller, but you’re the little lady who looked like a dancing girl yesterday, aren’t you? Don’t worry, Gramps will answer your question. You let that deer-girl in, didn’t you? I came in at the same time.”

“At the same time? With Tanza? But…”

“But she was alone? Kah-ha-ha-ha! If that’s how it looked, that’s ’cause I wanted it to look that way. How I got in is a secret. Shinobi tricks are my bread and butter, and I can’t be losing my job.”

Orbart laughed again, sidestepping Medium’s question.

I don’t know how seriously I should take him, but this self-declared shinobi said something I can’t ignore right out of the gate. Asking him straight up will be faster than roundabout probing.

“Do you know what caused us to shrink?”

When Subaru posed the question as frankly as possible, Orbart’s eyes narrowed. His brow furrowed a bit in thought for a moment, before finally…

“Ah, you’re that girl who was in the red outfit yesterday! There’s no mistaking the dancing girl and the one-armed guy, so I was wondering who you were for a little while.”

Subaru couldn’t believe how fast the tension was shattered. Al snickered a little as he let himself relax.

“…Damn, Bro. Even the shinobi chief couldn’t see through your disguise.”

“Phew, that’s incredible! That level of transformation is something I’d like the kids in my village to learn. Have you considered teaching? I’d welcome you with open arms.”

“…Unfortunately, Natsumi Schwartz’s schedule is pretty tight. Depending on your answer, I might be able to find some time, though.”

“Ho-ho. So it depends on how I reply, huh?”

The disguise was an unexpected hook, but Subaru licked his lips at the opportunity that had just fallen into his lap.

I don’t know if an empty promise has any value here, but I’m not about to let this chance to talk with Orbart slip past me. If Abel’s right and this old man is the one who turned us into kids, then…

“If you know why our bodies changed, then…”

“Ah, that? I’m the one who did it. Interesting, isn’t it? My shinobi technique.”

“………”

There was no maneuvering needed at all. The old man outright admitted it. Subaru gulped. The line of questioning he had prepared was pointless now. Orbart smirked impishly.

“If you accidently kill someone before interrogating them, it’s a pain, right? Right. There’s all sorts of techniques to put them through the wringer without killing them. Isn’t that fun?”

And in the same breath, he took a sip of his warm tea.

3

The age regression afflicted Subaru, Al, and Medium.

Based on the testimony of Abel, who possessed intimate knowledge regarding the Nine Divine Generals, it had been more or less confirmed that the perpetrator was Orbart. However, to hear it straight from the horse’s mouth was surprising. Especially when he was so shameless about it.

“Whoa, hey. Everyone’s face suddenly looks scary. Didn’t anyone teach you some manners? You’re supposed to help the elderly, not harass them.”

The tension shot back up. Talitta had never lowered her bow, but now even Al and Medium were glaring dangerously at Orbart. No chance to calm things down.

“Cease the nonsense, Orbart. I am asking again: Why did you come here?” The greatest threat came from Abel, who fixed the old man with an imperious glare from behind his oni mask. “You are aware the ruler of this city, Yoruna Mishigure, has acknowledged these three as messengers and declared that no harm shall befall them.”

“M-my word, that’s right! Wasn’t yesterday’s match about keeping you from laying so much as a finger on us?! We put our very lives on the line! This attack is clearly at odds with that!”

“Hold on there, now. You’re getting all mixed up. Why don’t you calm down a little?”

As Orbart pointed out, Subaru had slipped into his Natsumi persona in the heat of the moment, but the facts of the matter remained the same. Yoruna had acknowledged them as messengers, and Tanza had confirmed that no one would touch them. To go against that would be to make an enemy of Yoruna.

“Of course, she would turn a blind eye to any such guarantees if the city was being threatened.”

“Ugh! N-now that you mention it…”

Abel’s comment completely extinguished the fiery blood rushing to Subaru’s head. The false emperor commanding Orbart had effectively yielded the right to negotiate with Yoruna. It was entirely possible that he would consider this endeavor a wash and decide to simply flip the entire table. That would mean going against Yoruna, who was considered notorious even among the Nine Divine Generals, but…

“If he chooses the path of destruction, then the annihilation of the city will be inevitable. Of course, it would come at considerable cost.”

“Huh. You sure talk like you’ve seen through everything, mask boy.”

“…Mask…boy…”

Orbart scratched his chin with a finger, lips curled, while Subaru furrowed his brow.

While Abel seemed as cool as ever, Subaru was going to get an ulcer from this harrowing back-and-forth.

Orbart is one of the Nine Divine Generals who should know the emperor pretty well.

It went without saying, but even with a mask covering part of his face, Abel was just Abel. He made no effort to alter his voice or manner of speech. It would not be strange at all for Orbart to recognize him. Yet Abel was completely unconcerned and simply behaved as he always did.

Orbart showed no sign of recognizing Abel’s identity, either. Of course, Subaru could not casually point it out. That left him no choice besides following along while holding back the shivers.

Either way…

“We haven’t heard your answer yet, Mr. Orbart.”

“…Well, being called ‘Mister’ certainly feels more respectful than being called ‘gramps.’ For that, I’ll overlook the fact that you were pretending to be a young lady.”

“Mr. Orbart!”

Subaru snapped at the old man and glared at him for dodging the question. Orbart raised his hands in surrender.

“Fine, fine. You’re right. His Highness said to heed the fox.”

“In that case…”

“Come, now. I jabbed you all during the scuffle yesterday. You can’t complain about dying during a fight, and this is the same. I don’t think you have any reason to be mad, since I used my technique on you while we were going at it.”

“Th-that’s just a flimsy excuse…!”

“Yeah, and? What can you do about it?”

Orbart raised an eyebrow and smirked. He had shut down Subaru’s argument.

His excuse was pure sophistry, but it did make sense. If someone succumbed to their wounds after a ceasefire was brokered, most would not consider that a violation of the ceasefire.

There wasn’t much Subaru could say in response to that.

“Do not get carried away, Orbart.”

It was the masked man brimming with authority who challenged the crafty old man. The light in his eyes brought an end to the old man’s taunting, forcing him to stop playing with his teacup.

“I asked you why you are here. How many times must I ask, before you decide to answer?”

“You just don’t know how to enjoy yourself, do you? Well, not playing along is the right choice, I suppose.” Orbart put his empty teacup on the table and then cracked his neck. “To be honest with you, fox or no fox, I’m not planning to go against His Highness’s orders. So I can’t lay a hand on any of you. The only reason I came here was to chat over some tea.”

“Chat over tea? With us?”

“Aye.” Orbart nodded and pointed out the window, to the street outside. “That little speech at the palace yesterday was exciting, even for me. But there’s no end to the number of people who’d love to get their hands on His Highness, and so far, they’ve all failed. So I was curious about why you wanted to walk on such a dangerous tightrope.”

“…And what are you going to do with that information?”

“Huh? Obviously, I’ll decide once I hear it. Anyway, it’d be a problem if you lied, so I set a little trick in advance. Kah-ha-ha-ha!”

Subaru grimaced as Orbart let out a loud, spittle-flecked laugh.

It would be easy enough to just write him off as a crazy old man with a twisted sense of humor, but he was the one who had turned them into kids, and he was also one of the Nine Divine Generals they needed to win over to retake Abel’s throne.

He’s…not someone we can just ignore.

“If anything, this might be a chance…”

Under normal circumstances, even contacting one of the generals was a difficult task, never mind recruiting them as allies.

Now three of them were all in one place. Their party had already met Chaosflame’s ruler Yoruna, and Orbart was sitting right in front of them. Moreover, Chisha Gold was likely pretending to be the emperor.

Of course Chisha had clearly moved against Abel, so enticing him was out of the question, but…

“If Abel’s right, then Mr. Orbart might be up for grabs.”

Abel had mentioned there was some hope of winning over the generals whose loyalties were not set in stone. Yoruna had welcomed them to the negotiating table, so the possibility seemed to exist, at least.

But convincing Orbart to join us is gonna be…

“………”

Subaru glanced at Abel. As intelligent as he was, surely he would understand the unspoken message. The only card they had that might convince Orbart was Abel’s face underneath his mask.

This was a one-in-a-million chance that had fallen into their laps. Bound by the restrictions set by the fake emperor and Yoruna, Orbart could not directly harm them. That was why he had resorted to roundabout tactics in the first place.

We won’t get a better chance than this.

“—Abel.”

When Subaru quietly said his name, Abel’s attention clearly shifted. With the mask in the way, it was impossible to gauge his expression, but he was focused on Subaru now.

There was no telling what he was thinking, but he clearly understood what Subaru was planning to do.

“Emperor Vincent Volakia,” Subaru intoned.

“Huh?”

Orbart raised an eyebrow.

Peeling back the thick, bushy brows covering his eyes, the old man regarded Subaru with suspicion. It was a natural reaction, but not what Subaru had been hoping for, so he pressed on.

“You wanted to know why we came to meet Yoruna. Well, look no further. It’s Emperor Vincent Volakia.”

“What in the world are you getting at? Try to keep it simple so an old-timer like me can follow along.”

“Of course. Abel, if you please.”

Orbart still looked extremely dubious as Subaru again addressed the masked man.

Now that they’d come this far, Abel did not argue with Subaru’s decision. He simply brought his long, thin fingers to his mask, and…

“…What in the world…?”

Orbart murmured as Abel revealed his face. Staring back at him was none other than the handsome Emperor Vincent Volakia.

He blinked in surprise, clearly not expecting to find himself face-to-face with the emperor.

“His Highness? But that doesn’t make sense. Then who was I—?”

“Put those many years of wisdom to work, Orbart. You already know the answer.”

“So it was someone simply using Your Highness’s face and voice… I see.” For a moment, the old shinobi was gripped by shock, but he quickly recovered and connected the dots. “That was…Chisha, then? He sure fooled me… But it’s not like Your Highness to do nothing after someone got the better of you.”

“Do you presume to know my intentions?”

“Ho-ho, scary, scary.”

Orbart croaked, waving his hands to mollify Abel.

The old man wasn’t wrong, though. So far, Abel had been getting hammered like a punching bag. But his almost unnatural ability to remain calm despite the circumstances helped keep Subaru steady.

Orbart instinctively understood as well—Abel was the true emperor of Volakia.

“I did find it strange that Your Highness suddenly wanted to meet the fox again.”

“That was yet another move designed to pin me down,” Abel confirmed.

“Ha-ha, old-timers like me can’t keep up with you young whippersnappers. Isn’t it a little too greedy being so young and smart and handsome, too? Don’t you agree, kids? Maybe not, since you’re young, too. But I guess that’s my fault, isn’t it?! Kah-ha-ha!”

Orbart laughed uproariously at his terrible joke.

Grimacing, Subaru looked over at Talitta. She still had her bow trained on Orbart.

“Talitta, you can lower your bow. Mr. Orbart is—”

“What? No, you don’t have to do that. Besides, she can’t possibly let down her guard in front of someone she’s still not sure isn’t an enemy.”

“Huh?”

Orbart’s recommendation caught Subaru by surprise.

It’s almost like he’s warning us he’s still dangerous…

“But we already explained…”

“I heard you. And I said I would decide after hearing you out, didn’t I? Well, I’ve decided.”

Subaru was at a loss for words while Orbart’s expression remained unchanged.

Abel scoffed and said, “This was always a card that had no guarantee of succeeding even if we played it. I see you’ve made up your mind.”

“That’s not like you, Your Highness. It’s a fatal mistake not having any other cards to play. And you’ve got no luck at all to run into me, out of all the generals. After all, I’ve always wanted to try it once.”

“Oh? And what might that be?”

The shinobi leader smiled at the emperor driven from his throne. Perhaps it was more accurate to say he sneered, as befitting a vicious old man. Then he shared his ambition.

“I’ve always wanted to slay the emperor as my crowning achievement before old age takes me.”

The moment he revealed his ambition, the tension in the room finally snapped. In that moment, the rules preventing combat went right out the window. Talitta, Al, and Medium all leaped into action to smother Orbart’s dream.

However—

“It’s hard to use the techniques you’ve learned as an adult when you’re in the body of a child.”

Orbart twisted his neck and swung both hands, blood splattering from his fingertips. Subaru’s eyes widened as he took in the bloody scene.

“Gah…”

Al collapsed with a groan and his hand on his neck. He and Medium had rushed forward to pin Orbart down, but both of their necks had been sliced open. So much blood poured out that it was hard to believe so much had spilled out of such small bodies. It wasn’t long before the room’s bright interior was painted red.

“Seems like you can’t use the same technique you used yesterday. I was curious about it, but you went down before you could reveal the trick. Ahhh, looks like I screwed up.”

Orbart gave a half-hearted chuckle as the two went still. Between the blood and their twitching limbs, Subaru had no doubt they were dead.

And the only one who had been ready to attack Orbart at a moment’s notice…

“…Ah.”

When Subaru turned to see why the nocked arrow hadn’t taken flight, he was stunned. Talitta was pinned to the wall.

Talitta’s tall frame was fixed in place by a shuriken sticking out from the center of her chest. The stereotypically star-shaped throwing knife almost made it seem like some sick joke. It had struck her in the heart, and she had clearly died from the impact.

“…I see you will not heed the prohibition on violence.”

A man’s voice echoed in the room overflowing with death. It was Abel, surrounded by corpses that had piled up with frightening speed. He had risen from his seat and had leveled a penetrating gaze at the author of all that death.

Orbart wiped away a splatter of blood that had reached his cheek.

“I did not foresee your fascination with annihilation. That was an oversight on my part.”

“No, there’s no helping that. If word about my old-timer dream got out, I’d be so embarrassed that it’d kill me. Kah-ha-ha-ha!”

Al, Medium, Talitta—they were all dead.

The conversation between emperor and retainer sounded like it was happening in another world. But it wasn’t another world. This was reality. Reality. An unbearable reality. A reality they had reached because of Subaru’s wrong choice.

“Hm? Oh, yes, you’re still here.”

Orbart raised a brow at seeing Subaru totter forward into view. The old man shrugged, then pointed toward the dead.

“It’s not like you have to die, too. If you don’t get in the way, I won’t kill you.”

“Tha…”

“Ah, you’re the type that moves on impulse. This old man would prefer it if you think before you say or do anything, but I won’t wait long.”

When he heard how Orbart was calm enough to even crack jokes, Subaru’s mind went completely blank. No, not blank. It was pure red. It was hard to say whether it was because of rage or simply a reflection of all the blood that had been spilled.

Either way, Subaru’s body moved…

“Fool.”

Abel’s voice was filled with scorn. His eyes were boring straight into the back of Subaru’s head. The force of his gaze was palpable, even as Subaru thought about how right Abel was.

There was no meaning in trying to protect Abel like this now. But Subaru had already made the mistake. There was no undoing it.

“Uuu…”

“Oh, come now. Even the girl? I thought girls always hated Your Highness?”

Orbart put his hand to his forehead as Louis stood before him. Or rather, she stood in front of Subaru.

She was covering Subaru, who was covering Abel. The three of them were all lined up. It was an absurd series of human shields.

“I always figured you’d die alone, Your Highness.”

“…Do not assume that every person fits neatly in whatever box you assign them.”

“Kah-ha-ha-ha!”

Orbart laughed. Even in a situation like this, Abel had a comeback at the ready.

The old shinobi had little interest in Subaru or Louis, but he was not so kind as to overlook anyone who dared stand in his way.

And so…

“—I won’t forgive you.”

Subaru Natsuki seared into his mind the image of the old shinobi sneering viciously as he indulged his grand ambition. Then his adolescent body split open, and he sank into a pool of his own blood.

4

As the blood flowed, a hot feeling welled up where he had been struck. His body began to grow cold from the inside out.

Everything flowing out of him swallowed him from the feet up until he could no longer see, and when he sank all the way to the bottom—

“………”

The next instant, the blood he lost was flowing through his veins again, and he started to hear a grating sound in his ears.

His sense of hearing was strangely heightened. In the quiet room, he could feel the blood coursing through him. He could hear it. As that sensation spread to his entire body, he started breathing heavily.

The pain and emptiness faded into the distance. His vision flickered. He gritted his teeth.

Where did I come back? I’ve gotta—

“I went ahead and made some tea for myself, but does anyone else want some?”

That unforgettable, wicked voice signaled the start of a new battle for Subaru Natsuki.

chapters.title: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29
chapters.text:
Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

CHAPTER 2

BEHIND YOUR EYELIDS

1

The moment he heard that hoarse, elderly voice, it felt like all the blood in Subaru’s body started flowing backward. Goose bumps rose on his skin, and the air in his lungs seemed to freeze. It was like there was something profoundly sharp embedded in his chest, stirring his very soul.

Return by Death had activated, and it had brought him back to the worst possible moment.

“…!”

Before Subaru could react, Talitta took aim with her bow. Her target was of course the intruder—the old man, Orbart Dankelken, one of the Nine Divine Generals, and the person who had killed them all moments ago.

Even without knowing how that tragedy played out, everyone in the room was wound tight, wary of the unwelcome visitor.

Despite being in that same room, despite having an arrow aimed at him from such close range, Orbart merely shrugged, making a mockery of their caution.

“Hey now, gimme a break. I don’t like having scary things pointed at me. Besides, once you get up in years, you gotta hit the head more often. So don’t make me wet myself. I’m practically trembling over here.”

“Don’t trifle with me…! How did you—?”

“—Orbart Dankelken.”

Talitta’s face turned red in anger at Orbart’s flippant evasion, but Abel interrupted her, revealing the intruder’s identity. And thus began an interrogation that would be laughable if it were not so potentially bloody. Repeating the scene Subaru had just lived through was a path that led only to destruction.

With the gruesome memories so fresh in his mind, he knew he had to do something different.

But I don’t have any time to talk with everyone.

“Why…?”

Why had he wound up back here? It was a pointless question, but he could not help wanting to throw his hands up in defeat. Even knowing full well how haughty and selfish that thought was when his Return by Death allowed him a second chance. If it had at least triggered before Orbart appeared, he would have had a chance to discuss things.

It brought back memories of a recent struggle when he had died and returned so many times while dealing with Todd in Guaral. There had hardly been any time to react then as well.

The details were different, but the situation was similar.

A respawn point that locks you in a cage with a bloodthirsty beast.

Return by Death had always been capricious when it came to how much time it wound back, but this was brutal.

Trying to find a path forward from this dead-end start is…

“Ngh!”

“Whoa?! Why’d you go and do that?!”

“Uwaa?! What?!” “Uuu?! Aaa, uuu!”

To silence all the grumbling and complaints bubbling up in his mind, Subaru slapped both his cheeks with all his might. The sound echoed in the room, drawing everyone’s attention to him.

Sorry, I get that that would surprise anyone without a warning. But I needed it.

“Sorry about that. I was just motivating myself a bit.”

He scolded himself for wasting what little time he had crying about it. He was never the one who paid the price for his stupidity.

I can’t let that bloody disaster happen again.

“Motivation, huh? Just looks like red cheeks from here…hm? Were you that girl in the red outfit yesterday? I wondered why I didn’t recognize you.”

Orbart arched his bushy brows as he clocked Subaru.

Just like last time, this was where he made the connection between Subaru and Natsumi. If they identified Orbart as the cause of the age regression here, events would proceed along the same route as before.

I won’t make the same mistake twice. This old man is terrifyingly dangerous. The moment he believes Abel is the true emperor, he’ll try to fulfill his long-held ambition and kill us all.

It was safe to say he was their enemy.

“Phew, that’s incredible! That level of transformation is something I’d like the kids in my village to learn. Have you considered teaching? I’d welcome you with open arms.”

Stroking his chin with a joking air, Orbart smiled like a friendly old man, but that was nothing more than another tool in his toolbox. The reason he had silently sneaked in was the same reason he maintained this affable attitude. Everything he did was to gauge how they reacted. Subaru had to consider whatever Orbart said or did as more of his shinobi tricks meant to advance his sinister goal.

“Hey, are you the reason we’re all small, Mister?”

Just as there was a lull in the conversation, Medium asked a question. Orbart answered with an exaggerated laugh.

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! Aye, that’s right! It’s a shinobi technique, but it’s pretty darn interesting, ain’t it?”

“So it really was you, gramps…!”

“Don’t let it bother you, one-arm. If anything, you should be grateful. I might have accidently killed you, and then we wouldn’t have gotten a chance to talk like this. Instead, I only shrank you down some.”

Orbart confessed to his handiwork and then silenced Al by pointing out the clear gap in strength between them. What he said was true. If he had wanted to, he could have killed them in the brawl in the palace yesterday. The only reason he had simply turned them into children was because he happened to be curious why they were openly rebelling against the emperor.

Or at least that was what Subaru was thinking, but…

“Well, I’ll admit I did try to kill you, but those attacks were all stopped, so this was also a bit of a last resort. Ain’t that right, one-arm?”

“…I dunno what you mean.”

“Oh? Not gonna reveal your trick? Well, that’s your trump card, I imagine, so I guess that makes sense.”

“It’ll be the same every time I say it. I don’t know what you’re talking about.”

Al answered with a muffled voice from behind the wrappings covering his face. It should have been an unsatisfying answer for Orbart, and yet…

“Really? Well, all right, then.”

He just nodded, seemingly delighted by the response.

Subaru had no idea what the meaning of their exchange was. Al had done a masterful job protecting Subaru and Medium during the fighting that broke out in the palace.

I guess Orbart admires the effort?

But even if that were true, now that he had been turned into a child, Al’s technique wouldn’t work against the shinobi anymore. Subaru already knew that, unfortunately. That was why he would base all his decisions on a single unshakable principle in this situation—they had to avoid fighting Orbart at all costs. That meant they could not let Orbart take the initiative.

“…Mr. Orbart. You…”

Wanting to draw out the conversation so he could work on a strategy in the meanwhile, Subaru started to speak—only for Abel to interrupt him.

“You said that your technique shrank them.”

At first, Subaru’s blood ran cold, but one look at Abel’s face was all he needed to understand.

Abel was buying Subaru more time.

“Oh, right. I forgot I hadn’t finished explaining. It’s so easy to get off track when you get to my age. It might be about time for me to retire.”

“You? Spare me the bad jokes. If you claim to be frail from age, you should give up your rank already. That you have not proves your determination.”

“Oh, that’s a bold claim. As hard as it must be to see with that mask on, you think you can see through me?”

“Of course.”

Orbart’s eyes flashed with curiosity at Abel’s unflinching answer. And having taken the talking role, Abel was diligent in giving Subaru the time he so desperately needed. He had no idea how Abel had discerned what he wanted, but Subaru had no choice but to rely on him.

Without even glancing at Subaru, Abel crossed his arms.

“As a general first-class, third among your peers, you would accurately be called one of the top figures of the empire. However, you are greedy by nature. You are not remotely satisfied with your current position.”

“Better a greedy old man than a shriveled-up old man, no?”

Orbart answered Abel while unknowingly committing lèse-majesté. But even Abel did not fully grasp the darkness lurking within Orbart. There was no way he could have plumbed those depths.

There was a dark gleam in Orbart’s yellow eyes, as if taunting Abel, questioning whether he could actually see through it.

“And? What do you suppose it is that I want, then?”

“The First seat,” Abel answered in a quiet, steady voice.

Orbart’s breathing, which sounded like dried leaves, fell silent. There was no telling what sort of storm was raging in the silent shinobi’s heart, but it was clear that Abel’s claim had unsettled him.

It was enough that Al and Talitta both sprang into action to take advantage of the opening—

“Hey, one-arm. I know the feeling, but behave yourself. You too, bow girl.”

“Ngh! Do you have eyes in the back of your head or something?”

“Just call it a difference in training. I’m a lot older than you, after all. But from my perspective, most people seem like children. That’s the invincible logic of the elderly.”

Al and Talitta gulped at Orbart’s warning. The old man’s attention was focused on Abel, and while there had been an opening of some sort, this monster’s many years of training gave him the ability to notice even the slightest change around him.

He didn’t need to use his eyes to see through their paltry tricks and plans. This old man had transcended such mundane concerns long ago.

“Al,” Subaru said as he shook his head, warning him to not try anything.

He did not have a full grasp of Al’s true strength and abilities, but he probably used techniques optimized for defensive fights. The brutal truth was they would not work here, and he would simply get himself killed.

Enduring Al’s bitter gaze, Orbart’s attention remained on Abel.

“Still, though, saying I’m after the First seat at this age is quite a claim. What made you take a leap like that, mask boy?”

“Old age is not reason enough to drain the well of ambition. A shinobi tortures their body and mind to their very limits to reach a realm that only a handful can achieve. A shinobi is not complete until they die.”

“I see… You’ve done your homework.”

Orbart’s answer was bland, clearly different from before. At first glance, he seemed to be confirming Abel’s conjecture, but that couldn’t be further from the truth.

Subaru happened to know that Abel was actually wrong.

Orbart’s true desire was to murder his lord and emperor. Ascending to First seat of the Nine Divine Generals was a secondary or even tertiary ambition.

That said, the fact that there was still some emotion in Orbart’s voice was proof that Abel’s answer was not entirely off base. Abel had discerned the rapacious desires that consumed Orbart. Abel had presumed that his covetousness began and ended with reaching the pinnacle of the Nine Divine Generals, rather than as a means to a greater end, but that was a perfectly reasonable misunderstanding. How could he hope to realize that Orbart’s desire was to leave his mark in history even if it meant casting aside everything he had accomplished in his life, whether it be his title as general first-class or his position as the shinobi chief?

Abel was selfish and haughty and showed not a whit of concern for other people’s positions, but he was still the emperor of Volakia. He understood the value of his life in the line of succession. If he died, the empire would be shaken to its core. That was something he was keenly aware of as the emperor, and it conveyed a sense of responsibility anyone would feel, even if none would feel it so strongly as he.

But Orbart Dankelken was different.

He did not mind dying to achieve his ambition, and it did not matter to him how much trouble it caused the rest of the world. That abnormal and destructive line of thinking was the darkness that not even Abel could fully grasp.

However…

“Mr. Orbart, isn’t your goal the emperor, not the First seat?”

…Subaru Natsuki knew the darkness lurking within Orbart Dankelken.

2

In a flash, the color, the scent, the feel of the air changed.

“………”

Orbart hadn’t so much as budged under the watchful eyes of Al and Talitta, both of whom were bristling with open hostility and practically itching to act on it. But now his gaze turned to the child Subaru because he could not ignore what he’d just heard.

“Boyo, don’t start butting in all of a sudden. You about gave me a heart attack.”

“Is that because I interrupted? Or is it because…?”

“Because you’re right? Kah-ha-ha-ha! If that’s true, then I’d be one insane old man.”

Orbart tried to boldly laugh off Subaru’s comment, but Subaru was sure he was not nearly as calm as he was pretending to be. After all, his secret, long-held ambition had just been revealed. His darkness was something even Abel’s eyes could not penetrate until it was too late.

“Going after the emperor, as in killing him? That’s a little too much of a leap in logic, Bro. What would be in it for him?”

“Well, I can understand the argument for infamy over being forgotten, but one-arm over there’s right. That line of thinking is a bit too out there.”

Al’s voice was stiff with disbelief, and Orbart naturally picked up on that doubt.

But his easygoing escape was about to get harder.

“You didn’t deny it, Mr. Orbart.”

Subaru knew this was risky.

“………”

The color, the scent, the feel of the room did not revert back to normal. Subaru’s back was wet with sweat from the tension and his mental image of Orbart. This was honestly a dangerous gamble, but it was the only idea he had come up with in the little time he was given.

Orbart’s goal was to assassinate the emperor. As such, they could not reveal either Abel or the fake emperor, meaning they had lost their only bargaining chips.

But even so, Subaru used the time Abel had gained him to turn the tables on Orbart.

Keep our goals hidden while revealing his secret.

“We meant what we said in the palace keep yesterday. Dragging Emperor Vincent Volakia from his throne. That should line up well with your goal.”

“Whoa there, now. Don’t peg me as a conspirator against His Highness. That kid’s got no openings and never lets his guard down. Just thinking about it makes me wanna wet my pants.”

“I’m not going to stop until you actually deny it. You want to kill the emperor despite being one of the Nine Divine Generals who report directly to him.”

Subaru pressed on without fear, latching on to the possibility he had found.

Of course, the danger he felt from Orbart had not lessened in the slightest. He knew full well that one wrong step and it would end in a bloody massacre again, but so long as he did not make the absolute worst choices, they should be able to avoid total disaster.

That was like a suicide bombing to cap off his career.

So long as he could not be sure, Orbart would not pull the trigger in the middle of negotiations. He may have been an ambitious monster who was willing to cast aside duty and loyalty, but he would still play the part of the Divine General, faithfully following the fake emperor’s order not to lay a hand on them until the right moment. And also…

“…So that was the ulterior motive I could not grasp.”

Even if Orbart did not acknowledge it, thanks to Subaru’s hounding, everyone else was starting to notice the darkness lurking inside the vicious old man who was one of the Nine Divine Generals and led the Shinobi.

“Sheesh, how am I supposed to deal with folks who don’t listen?”

Orbart scratched his head in exasperation at Abel and everyone else staring at him. The old monster sighed, looking less worried and more bothered by being saddled with an annoying kid.

“If that’s how it’s gonna be, guess I’ll just have to change course, too.”

“…Don’t do anything rash, gramps.”

“I’m not, okay? I’m just gonna leave, since it’s a waste of time hanging around here.”

“…Do you really think you can just walk out of here?”

Judging the tide of the conversation to be turning against him, Orbart started acting like he was going to leave, when Talitta glared down her arrow at him. She had stayed perfectly still, aiming at Orbart the entire time. But Orbart’s only response was closing one eye and glancing at Subaru and Medium and Al.

“Ahh, you don’t want to let me go because you want to unshrink your friends. Unfortunately, you’re asking too much. I’m gonna leave without doing a thing.”

“But without you, we won’t be able to go back to normal, right?”

“Kah-ha-ha! That’s not true. How old are you actually, little lady?”

“Me? I think I was twenty?”

“Then if you just wait ten years, you’ll be back to normal, won’t you? Not that I know for sure.”

Medium had been serious, so she pouted at his joking response, but regrettably, that was not enough to get Orbart to change his mind. And using force was not an option.

Even if we avoid triggering the most dangerous event with Orbart, if we let him go, we’ll be stuck like this…

“What if I grant you an opportunity to kill the emperor?”

Subaru gulped at the sudden change of mood and stared blankly at Abel. The true emperor had nonchalantly put his own life in the balance and managed to draw a perked eyebrow from Orbart.

“We’re just talking past each other here. ‘Kill the emperor’? Do you hear yourse—?”

“If your aim is the emperor’s life, you should have had ample opportunity already, and yet you never acted. Because of the flames of the Sunlight Blade that protects the emperor.”

“You—”

“I can tell you how to bypass those flames.”

Orbart’s expression transformed completely from his prior deceptions.

“The Sunlight Blade’s flames…”

Subaru did not know the meaning of what Abel was saying, but it was shocking enough to peel back the mask that Orbart had maintained throughout and make his true intent blatantly obvious.

I’m assuming there’s some secret mechanism that protects the emperor of Volakia. It’s been getting in the way of Orbart’s ambition, and Abel’s offering a solution.

This had to be one of the greatest secrets of the Volakian imperial family, and something Orbart was plenty wary of.

“…I thought you were just some random kid who refused to show his face or respect his elders. Who are you? That ain’t something to bring up, not even as a joke.”

“Would one who dares to raise the flag of rebellion against this great and grand empire lean on sophistry or speak in jest? If so, they would be nothing more than a megalomaniacal villain, or otherwise a monumental figure with nerves of steel.”

“And you’re saying you’re neither?”

“Of course.”

Is he serious, or is he playing word games? Maybe both?

“………”

Orbart’s bushy brows furrowed as he silently scrutinized Abel’s words, and then, after some thought, he glanced outside.

“That was the bell for fire time, wasn’t it?”

“Huh?”

Subaru only managed a blank confusion, but Medium helpfully chimed in.

“Right, that foxy Yoruna called for us, so it’ll be a problem if we’re small!”

“Foxy Yoruna! Kah-ha-ha-ha! You’ve got guts, little lady.”

Orbart was amused by the cheeky way Medium referred to Yoruna, and after a good laugh, he put his hand to his chin.

“That’s right. Now the thought of trying to take His Highness’s life is so disrespectful that I won’t even dignify it with a laugh, but I will admit I’m curious about this supposed method for overcoming the flames guarding the Emperor of Volakia.”

“…! In that case—”

“Whoa there, kid. I know I got your hopes up, but I’ve got my position and future plans to think about… So how about a friendly little wager?”

Orbart stuck his finger out and placed it right on Subaru’s nose as he leaned forward excitedly.

Subaru froze. The old man had been so fast, his eyes hadn’t even registered him moving. The thought of challenging Orbart to a contest chilled him to the bone.

“A-and supposing we say no?”

“Then you won’t get what it is you want, right?”

“Argh…”

“And, since it seems like you have something that I want, you best believe I’ll come at you with every shinobi technique I have when you’re sleeping.”

Orbart’s smile made it clear he had no intention of holding back if it came down to that. If they let him leave now, there was nothing stopping him from asking the fake emperor to rescind his order so he could openly attack Subaru and the rest of the party. That was the exact sort of nasty idea this vicious old man would come up with.

“What are the rules?”

From the moment he made the offer, there was no avoiding this contest. That was why even when Subaru remained silent, Abel asked the inevitable question.

“Well now, you don’t have much time before the fox-girl’s summons. And it’s quite a hassle that I can’t lay a hand on you, either… Ah, this’ll do just fine.”

“Just fine for us? Or just fine for you?” Subaru’s asked tensely.

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! No need to be so scared. I mean for both of us, of course.” Orbart showed the palms of his hands. “It’s tag.”

“…Huh?”

“I play all the time with the youngsters in the village. Nice and simple, right?”

3

Subaru and the rest of the party were at a loss at how they should react to the old man’s gruff proposition.

“Tag…?”

Subaru had been on tenterhooks, wondering what sort of impossible challenge they would be given, but the strangely peaceful-sounding suggestion ground his brain to a halt.

“What?” Orbart cocked his head, simmering Subaru’s suspicions into a deep, distrustful stew. “You look confused. Don’t tell me you don’t know tag.”

“That’s… Of course I know the game. I just didn’t expect it to come up.”

Orbart confirmed he really was talking about the children’s game.

I can’t imagine anything else it could be. Then again, playing tag in a ninja village has to involve special rules.

“Probably stuff like you’re allowed to kill the other players or something…”

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! Of course not. If a terrifying rule like that got popular, there’d be no shinobi left, before you know it. And by my hand, too. How awful that’d be.”

Orbart dismissed Subaru’s concern, but it wasn’t very reassuring, given everything else he had done so far. He didn’t seem the type to hesitate to spill the blood of his comrades or even to destroy his own village if the need arose.

“What is the structure of this tag you are proposing?”

While Subaru was racked with suspicion, Abel moved the discussion along.

“Ho-ho.” Orbart cracked a smile “You’re more up for this than I expected, mask boy.”

“Fool. We are already well past the point of indecision now that we’ve already revealed that we possess information you want.”

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! True enough.”

Orbart burst out laughing. The simple truth was that Orbart could get the information he wanted, competition or no competition. The point of this game of tag was to determine whether it would be through negotiations or torture.

“Don’t worry, there’s no catch. One team runs away, and the other team chases… I’ll be the runner. Chasing after so many people is rough for an old bag of bones like me.”

“So if we catch you, we win? That’s nice and easy to understand.”

“It is certainly easy to understand, but…”

Medium was optimistic after hearing the rules, but Talitta was more wary. If he had to pick, Subaru would lean toward Talitta’s side. The rules were simple, and there was no room left for uncertainty, meaning that differences in strength would be very apparent.

Unfortunately, even when they combined everyone on their side together, Subaru’s party couldn’t even come close to Orbart. Sensing their general uneasiness, Orbart closed an eye and spoke up again.

“Well, if it’s too much when so many of you are little runts, I suppose I could loosen the rules a little bit.”

“…And how would you do that?”

“Let’s change the tagging part. Instead of catching me, you just have to find where I’m hiding. In exchange, you’ll have to find me three times.”

“Three times…?”

“I hide three times. You find me three times. If you can’t, you lose. In that case, it’s less a game of tag and more a game of find. Hmm, doesn’t really roll off the tongue…” Orbart cocked his head.

“How about hide-and-seek?”

“Oh, good one. Let’s use that.”

Orbart snapped his fingers, taking a liking to the name. Then he spread his arms, holding up one finger on either hand.

“If it’s tag, you only have to catch me once. If it’s hide-and-seek, you have to find me three times. I think it goes without saying which one has better odds,” Orbart said.

Subaru gulped. Just like the old man said, this was an obvious choice. Why attempt to catch someone as strong and skilled as Orbart if they didn’t have to?

There’s no reason at all to risk it, but…

“You’re being awfully generous. Going out of your way to give us a better chance of winning almost makes me suspicious there’s some trick to it.” Al’s black eyes glared through gaps in the cloth he was using instead of his now ill-fitting helmet.

“I’m hurt,” Orbart said with a shrug. “Are you sure you don’t have the wrong idea? I’d rather you win. That’s why I’m testing you, to see if there’s any value in listening to your story.”

“You’re testing us, huh…?”

“I’m brimming with curiosity at what you have to say. However, not only have I been framed by a random lie, but my loyalty to His Highness has been brought into question. I’m worried about how I’ll be spending my twilight years, that’s all.”

“Ngh…”

Orbart pointedly wagged his finger and danced around Al’s suspicions. Of course, none of that was very convincing, but it made enough sense that Al hesitated to press the issue.

Of course Subaru was not naive enough to believe that was all Orbart was up to, but there wasn’t enough time or information to probe which of the two options Orbart was forcing them to take.

Frankly, it took everything Subaru had just to reach this point.

“If we are to accept your proposition, then the rules must be made clear.”

“Oh? What do you mean?”

“What you said yourself. If our chance of victory is higher, then we should not leave room for pointless debate. Especially when what we both want is clear.”

“…Kah-ha-ha-ha.”

Apparently reaching the same conclusion, Abel watched Orbart closely as he began to hammer out the terms of the challenge. The implication was clear—they had accepted the competition and had decided on the format.

Orbart chuckled in a low voice. Abel met his gleaming eyes and nodded.

“We choose hide-and-seek.”

4

Both sides agreed upon three rules:

Neither side could harm the other; hiding had to be limited to somewhere within the city; and a clear definition of the win conditions had to be established. All three were rules necessary for hide-and-seek.

The win conditions deserved special attention.

“I get that the odds of us winning are higher in hide-and-seek versus tag, but why three times? Do you have to be so stingy? Why not just make it once either way?”

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! Don’t be so greedy, kiddo. Even against me, you could get lucky and find me once, but three times? That takes skill.”

“Some might say luck is just another skill.”

“Too bad for you, I don’t believe in leaving things to fate. Same goes for most people in the empire, really. You sure do say some strange things.”

A fitting idea for a nation that practiced extreme meritocracy. It left no room for excuses.

There was neither good nor bad luck. Results were achieved solely by strength and skill. For people who struggled to get by, it was a suffocating way of life. There was no place in the empire for people like Subaru when he stopped going to school. As proof…

“It’s a small detail, but just to be sure, Mr. Orbart… You can’t pick a hiding place that we physically can’t reach. Not much we can do if you’re in a totally isolated place like inside a wall or something.”

“Kah-ha-ha, you’re a real finicky one. Though that’s exactly what I would’ve done if you hadn’t mentioned it.”

“………”

“Just to be clear, I meant what I said about not wanting to win at all costs. But don’t forget, this is a test for you.”

In other words, he was judging them on their talent, shrewdness, and on how quickly they thought on their feet. Naturally, any loopholes in the rules were fair game. His kindly old grandpa routine was all a facade, and if he decided Subaru and the others were of no value to him, he wouldn’t hesitate to cut them down. And Subaru knew this wasn’t an idle threat.

“Well, I can’t imagine that mask boy will miss anything obvious like that.”

Orbart flashed a crafty grin while jerking his chin in Abel’s direction.

Subaru glanced over at Abel and Al, getting a nod from both before steeling himself to face the challenge.

“If we win, you’ll have to return us back to normal.”

“And if I win, you’ll have to wait ten years. And, if His Highness and that fox-girl change their minds, I’ll pry your secret out of you my own way.”

Subaru felt a swell of fear at the implication that would involve shinobi interrogation techniques. Finally, before the crafty old man left for his first hiding place, Subaru asked…

“So, what’s the first hint?”

It was a question that would be laughed off as absurd in a serious match, but Orbart did not sneer at it. Because that was one of the conditions Subaru got him to swallow for hide-and-seek. The reason Orbart turned them into children and the reason he was testing them was all because he wanted to judge their quick thinking and resourcefulness. He naturally did not want to strike a deal with idiots. Because of that, Orbart had accepted Subaru’s request that they be given hints to test whether their wisdom and teamwork made them fitting comrades in his quest for the emperor’s head—

“First up is a preliminary test… I’ll be hiding somewhere near the inn, behind your eyelids.”

“…Behind our eyelids?”

“Now, it’s time for you youngsters to put those heads together. Let this old man have a little bit of fun.”

With a casual wave, he turned around and walked away. Subaru could feel the tension building in the air as he leisurely sauntered toward the exit. Every single person in the room had the same thought that if they all jumped him now, they had a chance to resolve everything in one fell swoop. But no one dared try.

That was the right choice.

“Kah-ha-ha-ha.”

Just before the door shut, Orbart laughed, sensing the reason for their hesitation. He played the role of vicious old man to perfection, right down to that low, growling laughter.

Once he left the room and only allies remained…

“Talitta, lower your bow. There is no one left to turn it on.”

“…As you wish…”

An embarrassed look crossed Talitta’s face as she obeyed Abel. Of course. Orbart had been calm and at ease from start to finish, even with her arrow pointed straight at him.

As a Shudrak, and as the next chief of her people, she took the crafty old man’s complete sense of ease as an insult. Due to her insufficient strength, he had looked down on the Shudrak people.

Talitta had originally joined them on their journey to bolster her resolve to lead the Shudrak. Instead of building confidence, it was having the opposite effect.

“You serious about going along with that old man’s game, Bro?”

Al spoke up, breaking the silence for Subaru, who was struggling to find the words for Talitta. His tone dripped with annoyance and discontent, which seemed extra mismatched with his current appearance. And Al usually took most anything in stride, which made this moment stand out all the more.

But with Orbart just doing whatever he feels like, I get why he’s pissed.

“It’s not like I love how this is turning out, either, but there is at least a smidgen of a chance remaining, right?”

“A smidgen, huh…?”

“A chance of us getting back to normal, right, Subaru?”

Medium was sitting cross-legged on the floor. She was holding down Louis, who struggled to break free. They were practically the same size now, but Medium had presumably learned the skills to keep Louis contained during her time in the orphanage.

“Yeah.” Subaru nodded. “If we had upset him there, we’d be stuck in our tiny bodies…which is not okay for our next steps or any future plans. Getting back to normal is an absolute must.”

“…There was the option of just surrounding him and giving him a smackdown.”

“Don’t be crazy. The reason we’re not dead is because he’s following the emperor’s order. Without that, we wouldn’t be able to raise a finger against him.”

“…You sound like you’ve already seen it happen.” Al averted his eyes, almost like he wanted to say that was impossible.

His perception and his phrasing were dead-on. Subaru had seen that scenario play out with his own eyes. Both the thing that Al thought was impossible and what Subaru did not want to acknowledge.

And speaking of not wanting to admit something…

“You’re awfully quiet. Are you in shock that Mr. Orbart is after your life?”

“Fool. I knew full well he harbored an ambition that outstripped his position. Although I did not think it extended all the way to taking the emperor’s head. I thought there was nothing to gain by such an act, but if what he sought was a final sense of achievement and infamy in death…” Abel shrugged. “Truly incomprehensible.”

Driven from his throne and forced into a corner, Abel still did not know how to admit defeat. No matter the time or place, he always took the best choice available to survive and work toward reclaiming his throne. The idea of willingly throwing away your life and seeking fame and glory in death was something he could not even begin to understand.

On that point, Subaru had mixed feelings but was generally in agreement. The thought of being praised after death did not appeal to him in the slightest.

Either way…

“…At the same time, Mr. Orbart is surprisingly oblivious. Even with that level of ambition, he didn’t recognize you at all, even when you were standing right in front of him.”

Subaru at least wanted to get a jab in. Abel showed no effort at all to hide his identity, and Orbart showed no sign of seeing through it. It had been stomach-churning to watch in real time, but maybe a shinobi’s eyes weren’t as impressive as he’d thought they’d be…

“What are you talking about?”

“Huh?”

“I am wearing this mask. Orbart’s reaction is entirely reasonable.”

As he touched the cheek of the mask, there was a puzzled tone to his voice as he looked at Subaru, who simply furrowed his brow in response. His confusion was obvious in the wrinkles on his forehead. Abel’s puzzlement quickly became open disappointment.

“This mask warps the perceptions of others. An effect that hides the identity of the wearer.”

“Wha…?! Perception blocking?! But wasn’t that mask originally in the Shudrak village…?”

“Y-yes, it was. It is said that long ago, when the emperor and the Shudrak pledged their friendship, the emperor used the mask to visit the jungle without being noticed…”

“So it had that kind of backstory…”

Subaru’s jaw hung open at that big reveal. Abel’s disappointment remained, however.

“Did you seriously think I was just wearing this mask this whole time for show or a flight of fancy?”

“………”

Unable to say anything, Subaru could only endure the contemptuous gaze in silence.

It was his fault for chalking the mask up to another of Abel’s oddities and not asking about it, but Abel had to be at least partly to blame for assuming he would understand it without any explanation.

Because of that, I had to embarrass myself for no reason and spend all that time pointlessly worried, too.

Abel’s haughty speech and arrogant behavior made it seem like he was making no effort at all to hide himself, but all the worrying Subaru had been doing about getting caught had been for naught.

“Hey, hey, Al, is there some reason why you’re hiding your face like Abel?”

“In my case, it’s a complex I have about the scars on my face… Actually, that’s enough about me. Hide-and-seek’s already started. We better get moving.” Al pointed outside, toward the street.

Chaosflame was one of the great cities of the empire, several times larger than the fortified city of Guaral. Big enough that the thought of finding a shinobi out there was hopeless.

And they only had two hours and six people to do it three times.

“He called it a preliminary test, but there’s too many possibilities. You got a plan here?” Al asked Subaru.

“I wouldn’t really call it a plan…but there is something I’d like to try.”

“I have several potential strategies in mind. Most likely, they differ from what that clown has in mind.”

“Demoted from strategist to clown, huh? Aren’t you a little too bent out of shape over the mask thing?”

Abel seemed to find it deeply unamusing that Subaru had assumed his oni mask was just a fanciful fashion choice, but Subaru could only grimace and endure his frosty attitude.

Either way, they could only spend so much time chatting—

Better get moving.

“Aaa, uuu!”

“Oh, all fired up, Louis?! All right, let’s look for that old gramps!” Medium cried.

“Uuu!”

Louis was coming along, since they obviously couldn’t just leave her behind. Seeing her so excited, Medium broke into a smile as she lugged one of her twin blades. Al put his sheathed sword on his back, and while Subaru wasn’t confident he could use it, he got his whip ready all the same. With the bare minimum amount of gear, the party was ready to venture into the Demon City.

“Is that old man really going to take us on fair and square? Doesn’t it feel like he’d stab us in the back without a second thought?”

“He said it himself, but Orbart’s aim is not victory. He is taking a roundabout approach to appraise us with this game. To judge whether our bold declaration can be trusted or not.”

Al still doubted Orbart’s intent, but Abel was absolutely certain. Subaru agreed that there was no need to worry about deception. He was reluctant to just trust anything Orbart said at face value, but if his goal really was to take the emperor’s head, it would be convenient if their goal and the information they were offering were real. Orbart wanted to be convinced they could walk the walk.

And for that sake…

“I didn’t get to ask before, but about that Sunlight Blade’s flames thing…”

“Unfortunately, there is not time to engage in a long lecture on the history of the Volakian Empire. Your superficial thinking aside, my plan of action is not something that can be accomplished by standing still inside this inn.”

“Tch…fine, I get it.”

Subaru scoffed when Abel made it clear he had no intention of elaborating. Judging from the conversation with Orbart, the emperor of Volakia enjoyed some sort of special protection, and so long as that was active, he couldn’t be killed. At least that was how it seemed.

If that is true, then there’s one thing I want to find out.

“Does that flame or whatever protect you even now?”

“You are tedious. Or will you become my enemy as well once you hear the answer?”

“…I’ve got nothing to gain from that.”

Subaru grimaced at the implication and dropped the subject. A glance at their party confirmed everyone was ready to leave.

“The enemy is boss of all the shinobi, and we’ve got four kids on our side. But when it comes to hide-and-seek, with so much youth in body and spirit, we have the advantage! We’ll win for sure!”

“Wh-what sort of logic is that…?” Talitta asked.

“Pay him no heed. It is just meaningless prattle.”

It really was just a little joke, so he wasn’t surprised by their response, but Subaru furrowed his brow all the same in a show of dissatisfaction.

Then Subaru continued, raising his voice more than necessary.

“Anyway! Everyone, be extra careful of your surroundings. Let’s go!”

“Yeah!”

“Auu!”

“…You’re really fired up, Bro.”

Subaru didn’t look very put together as he raised his fist in his slapdash outfit. Medium and Louis answered in kind all the same, raising their fists to match his, while Al just sighed.

Meanwhile, their strongest fighter, Talitta, looked nervous and anxious. There was no telling what expression Abel was making behind his mask, but he looked as cocky as ever despite holding absolutely nothing in his hands.

With their party assembled, they all left the room…

“…And right back inside we go.”

“Huh?”

After taking one emphatic step forward, Subaru spun 180 degrees. Seeing him turn back to face the door of the room they had just left, Al made a silly noise.

Subaru pushed the door open and pointed straight into the room they’d just vacated.

“I found you, Mr. Orbart.”

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! Hey, c’mon now, no fair, finding me so quickly. That’s just embarrassing. Seriously, I’m turning red here!”

Orbart must have slipped in right after they left. The old man laughed from his belly when he saw Subaru pointing right at him.

5

“Are you serious, Bro…?!”

Al was dumbfounded when they spotted Orbart just about to rebrew his cold tea.

“Ah, Mister!” “Aaa!”

Medium and Louis shouted in surprise, while Talitta peered into the room, eyes opened wide.

The last one to react was Abel.

“I see… Behind our eyelids.”

“The sort of person who’d go for a competition like this always tries something like this for the first round,” Subaru explained, chest puffed out with pride as he remembered a nostalgic scene.

chapters.text:
Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

It was the first time he’d met Beatrice in the corridors of the former Roswaal Manor. She had created a looping hallway with her magic. But because he saw through her scheme immediately, he had completely foiled her prank.

But today’s opponent was Orbart, someone he had no positive feelings toward at all, so he just stuck his tongue out tauntingly.

“I saw right through you, nasty old man.”

“Kaaah, how embarrassing. You’re really something vicious, little boy.”

“Don’t go giving me a weird stage name! Anyway, this counts as our first win!”

I’m not going to let you weasel out of this by claiming you were caught off guard since it happened so fast.

“Of course,” Orbart confirmed, setting down his teacup. “Pulling tricks within the bounds of the rules ain’t the same as a free-for-all. Despite how I look, I keep my word. So you win the first round. Two more to go.”

“Oooh! Good one, Subaru! That’s one down in ten seconds!”

“Yeah, we did it!”

Medium celebrated as Subaru breathed a sigh of relief.

“This is all…”

Just as he was about to say ‘thanks to Beako,’ he thought back to that adorable little girl. But then his mind blanked out for a moment.

“………”

There was a strange feeling, and something felt ever so slightly off in his mind. Before he could try to find some other clear answer, though—

“The first round was well outside my expectations, but now the real contest starts.”

Flashing a grin, Orbart leaped onto the windowsill. Just as he was about to leave, Subaru reached out with his hand.

“Mr. Orbart! The next hint!”

“Right, let’s see… An abyss with a view.”

That was all Orbart said before he slipped out and disappeared into the city.

“Wait, gramps…! Damn, he’s already gone!”

Al rushed over to the edge of the window and scanned the surroundings, before clutching his wrapped head in frustration.

It was virtually impossible to catch Orbart once he started running away. If this had been a game of tag instead of hide-and-seek, they would have lost before the contest even began.

But…

“Subaru, where will he hide next…?” Talitta asked.

“Yeah, did you figure it out, Subaru? You know where it is?”

“Um…that’s, well…”

As Talitta’s and Medium’s expectations rose, Subaru’s words got caught in the back of his throat. He was honored that they had such high hopes for him, but immediate answers back-to-back was a little too much to ask for.

“Sorry, nothing’s coming to me. I got the last one right because I’ve seen it before…”

“Ahhh, sorry! We can’t just leave everything to you! Let’s think about it together!” Medium said.

“That’s…true. I am not the best at using my head, but I will think, too.”

Subaru bowed apologetically, but Medium and Talitta were sympathetic.

It was a staple to guess that the first hiding place was right at the start. Even if it had been wrong, it wouldn’t have taken up much time, so it was an easy theory to test. From here on out…

“It’s a race against time.”

“…Can’t think of the next place, Bro? I guess that’s to be expected.”

“To be expected…? I get that I’m not the most reliable, but hearing you say it so bluntly is kinda soul-crushing.”

Just as the real hide-and-seek was beginning, Subaru felt like he’d been stabbed in the back. The assessment was fair, but he would have preferred at least a little sugarcoating.

Even good friends should watch their manners.

But Al just waved his hand.

“Ah, sorry, that’s not what I meant. Just saying it makes sense you don’t know, Bro. Since I’m here with you and all.”

“Huh? Sorry. You kinda lost me. Are you saying I lose a few IQ points when you’re around or something? How’s that work?”

“That’s not it, either. It’s kinda hard to explain…ya know?”

“I’d love to agree, but I still don’t really get it…”

What really confused Subaru was how Al seemed to not be very sure himself. He decided to set aside the issue for the moment to focus on something more productive.

There’s still Orbart’s hint… We should figure that out first.

“Behind our eyelids was the starting room. An abyss with a view is probably a similar sort of riddle, but…”

“‘With a view’ makes it sound like a high place, doesn’t it?”

“But ‘abyss’ means, like, a hole, right? A hole would be in the ground, wouldn’t it?”

Or maybe it referred to a specific place somewhere in Chaosflame.

Either way, it did not seem like the sort of thing they could find an answer to by staying in the room. It was finally time for them to set out into the city.

“…I can’t really wrap my head around it. What’s your idea, Abel?”

“It is not one that can be set in motion here, as I said. Some place with many people…ideally one frequented by people coming and going from the city.”

“Some place popular with outsiders? Where would that be…?”

Al twisted his head, puzzling over that. Subaru raised his hand.

“Well, the standard location to find lots of people coming and going…that’d be a place to get a drink, right?”

“A tavern?”

“Yeah, I think that would be a good place to try.”

There was some room to debate whether searching for Orbart straight up or helping Abel carry out his plan would be faster in the end, but it seemed wise to focus on Abel for now.

“Going to a tavern with children in tow… That will surely draw attention.”

“Not like we got much choice at this point when four out of six of us are kids. And since we’re already having that conversation, wearing an oni mask is gonna get us looks. Or does the percep…the mask’s effect make your face look different?”

“It merely conceals my identity; it does not look any different than an oni mask.”

“Then that will definitely get looks…”

Brushing off Abel’s misplaced annoyance, Subaru sighed and shrugged.

At long last, they exited the room and emerged from the inn. They did try to ask about taverns at the entrance, but their timing was bad, and they could not find the owner.

But in such a large town, there was no way they would fail to find some bar, so they all stepped out into the street.

“Would it be better to all go together or split up? A group searching for Mr. Orbart, and a group going with Abel…”

Just as he was proposing they split up…

“…Huh?”

He noticed a red flame out of the corner of his eyes. It flashed bright—

6

“Oh, good one. Let’s use that.”

“Wha?”

One moment, the flickering red dazzled his eyes, and then the next, he heard a familiar voice.

Subaru made a strange noise that was met with a snicker. His eyes widened at the low, raspy laugh.

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! What are you making such a strange noise for? I just complimented you on the good name.”

“…Mr. Orbart…”

The old monster swayed with laughter as he stood right in front of Subaru.

It had all happened so quickly. Subaru blinked over and over, unable to understand. Then, gulping, he made a declaration.

“I—I found you, Mr. Orbart.”

“…? What? You think the contest has started already?”

“Eh…?”

Subaru was still dazed but didn’t want to miss his chance. However, it didn’t take long for Orbart’s bemused comment and their surroundings to clue him in.

They were inside some room even though he and his search party had just stepped out onto the street.

Wait, this isn’t just any room.

“…No way…”

This was their room at the inn—the same room they had left moments ago. And since they were currently talking face-to-face with Orbart, he had to face the truth…

Even under the nominal protection of rules that should have kept anyone from attacking, he had still Returned by Death.

chapters.title: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29
chapters.text:
Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

CHAPTER 3

SOUL MARRIAGE

1

Subaru Natsuki’s small brain was rocked by incomprehension.

That would be a fair description for the shock he’d just experienced. Subaru had wound back to the rules negotiation with Orbart, without even noticing he had died. He had to face reality, even if he didn’t want to.

“…In the middle of hide-and-seek, when there shouldn’t have been any risk of death…”

Putting his hand over his mouth, Subaru tried to remember what had happened. But there was nothing special. They had won the first round, and then everyone left the inn to begin the second round. That was it. And then the world went dark.

And then I found myself back here all of a sudden.

“…”

“If we are to accept your proposition, then the rules must be made clear.”

“Oh? What do you mean?”

While Subaru sank into thought, negotiations continued with Orbart. Abel and Orbart were talking, leading up to the choice of competition that was implicit in setting the rules. In other words…

“Hide-and-seek.”

2

Afterward, there was a discussion with Orbart regarding the specifics of the game. That went exactly like how Subaru remembered, too. There were no new clauses, and none of the clauses from before were left out, either. As a result, the rules were exactly the same.

Naturally…

“What’s up, Bro? You’re not looking so good.”

After Orbart left, Al said this as Subaru looked down.

The contest had already started, and Orbart had given the first hint. Thanks to Abel and Al, things had proceeded pretty much the same as last time.

The only real difference was that this time Subaru had not really been involved in the back-and-forth.

It was understandable that Al would be concerned, as Subaru had yet to recover. The shock of his sudden return was just too great.

“Sorry… I guess I started feeling really tired during all that talking.”

“Hey, keep it together, Bro. Unlike me and Medium, your strengths should still be unaffected by being smaller.”

“My strengths…?”

“Of course! Your strength is being really smart! My big bro is incredible, too, but so are you. I’m fine even if my boobs are small now!”

Medium cheerfully picked up on Al’s encouragement, patting her now flat chest while still holding Louis. Eyes wide, Subaru slowly exhaled.

They’re right. Strictly speaking, being larger or smaller doesn’t really affect what I’m good at. I can do what I usually do even shrunken down.

He pushed himself to get back on his feet to face that sudden death head-on and overcome it.

“…No need to stare at me. The anti-perception effect on that mask is enough. You don’t need to pull out the oni glare, too.”

“It seems you are aware of your surroundings, at least. But I am surprised. I had thought at this point you were a simpleton who did not notice the effects of this mask.”

“…I wouldn’t have been that shocked if you were the sort of weirdo who liked to wear masks like that.”

Subaru reset himself with a little sarcasm, and Abel stopped looking like he was gauging some useless tool, instead pocketing whatever other barbs he had prepared.

With that, things settled a little bit, so Subaru used the opening to bring up something he wanted to ask.

“By the way…do you think there’s any chance of Mr. Orbart breaking the rules?”

“Huh? What, like ignoring the rules and attacking us?”

“Yeah. I was just thinking it would be scary if that happened, but—”

“Absolutely not.”

Because he died right after they left the inn, Subaru was trying to gather everyone’s attention on Orbart, but Abel immediately shot down that idea.

“He will not,” he continued. “There is nothing for Orbart to gain from such an action. Therefore, the chance of it happening is zero.”

“B-but! He wants to kill the emperor! You didn’t predict that, either…so there might be a chance!”

“The concept of fame after death is foreign to me. However, I can understand the existence of such an obsession and that there are some who desire it. However, the terms set earlier do not align with that goal.”

“………”

“What you are concerned about is not the actions of a person, but a death wish.”

Pierced by Abel’s sharp gaze through the mask’s eyes, Subaru felt his heart freeze. The particular way Abel rephrased it at the end had a different weight to it.

But even when he said it so confidently, it still felt off to Subaru.

After all, Orbart had in fact attacked them once already.

But that was still consistent with Orbart’s goal, and even if I don’t sympathize, I can at least understand the logic. Everything lined up at the worst possible time.

When he thought about it that way, Subaru had to admit this time was undeniably inconsistent. Killing them now didn’t make sense for Orbart.

Meaning…

“What’s going on…?”

“Hey, hey, are you worried about something, Subaru? Is it something outside?”

Right as Subaru was sinking deep into thought, Medium peered into his eyes. Her round blue eyes were right in front of his, making him jump back.

“Wah!”

“Whoa.” Medium grabbed Subaru’s hand, pulling him close. “There, there, Subaru. Relax. Relax.”

“Ah.”

Hugging his head to her chest, Medium started patting his back. Her gentle hands and the sound of her heartbeat gently melted away Subaru’s anxiety and confusion. He exhaled.

“Better?” Medium asked. “Whenever my head ends up a big mess, my big bro would do this for me. And someone did it for him, too, a long time ago.”

“…I feel…better.”

“Mhm, good! So, think you can tell us why you’re worried about outside?”

He could hear Medium’s voice coming from right above his head, but it wasn’t pressuring him to hurry. Even as a child, Medium was as bighearted as ever, and Subaru would have loved to indulge in her warmth even more. But time was pressing, so he slowly, awkwardly started thinking again.

“That’s, um…for some reason, it feels like, it’s really…dangerous outside…”

“Outside feels dangerous?”

“Th-that’s right. Like someone is…targeting us…”

Medium nodded energetically, listening carefully to Subaru’s vague comments.

Honestly, he hated himself for being so vague and unclear. If he could not be clearer, then Medium aside, Al and Abel would not take it seriously.

So…

“Before, when we left the inn, we di—”

Before he could finish, the whole world fell silent.

“………”

The sound of Medium’s heartbeat vanished. Her face had been right there. Now it was gone. Her breathing, her hands…they all disappeared someplace out of reach.

Everything grew distant.

Color faded away, sound died out, time ceased to flow, and he lost control of his own body.

Unable to speak, to breathe, to move his eyes, at the edge of his consciousness, something disgusting, terrifying, hair-raising slowly drew near.

Why did you break the taboo? the dark shadow seemed to lament as it sidled closer.

Why did you forget? the slender dark fingers slipping into his chest seemed to ask.

Why do you repeat this so many times? The witch’s voice that blotted out everything approached.

“—I love you.”

It was a voice he had not heard in quite some time, dragging Subaru into hell.

Unable to move, his heart in her clutches, his body was racked by a terrible pain. A warning. A violation. An assault—a searing brand to remind him not to forget again.

And…

“Subaru?”

Suddenly, sound, color, and the flow of time returned. He felt in control of his own body again.

The blood flowed through his veins once more, drowning out the gentle beat of Medium’s heartbeat.

But terror still gripped Subaru’s soul.

He could only curse himself for touching on the taboo, for invoking the witch’s wrath. Why had he invited so much pain and suffering upon himself? Why had he forgotten the unbreakable rule, the rule that his Return by Death could not be revealed to anyone? Even attempting to violate that taboo meant a punishment by the witch. If it was just Subaru, then that would be one thing…

“That was close…”

Subaru muttered to himself as he checked Medium’s condition while she kept hugging him. He also confirmed that Abel, Al, Talitta, and Louis were all still fine.

There was a possibility that confessing his ability would inflict the punishment on someone close to him instead, sometimes fatally. That was the worst possible outcome for Subaru.

Emilia had been killed once this way. Ever since, Subaru had been extremely careful, warning himself constantly to be vigilant and to never make the same mistake again.

I got lucky. But I can’t risk taking that gamble again.

“Medium…thank you. I’m fine now.”

“Really? You look like you’re hurting even worse than before, though…”

Putting on a brave face, Subaru slipped out from her arms. Both to avoid exposing her to more danger and because he couldn’t afford to wallow any longer.
