chapters.title: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29
chapters.text:
Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

Even if I can’t explain it well, I have to do all I can to save everyone.

“Sorry for the awkward phrasing, but I have the feeling that it’s dangerous outside…”

Still cowering from the witch’s interruption, Subaru chose his words carefully, but Abel had a sharp question for him.

“What would you have us do, then? We cannot defeat Orbart by remaining inside this building. If we do not play his game, you three will remain children. Is that what you want?”

“Ngh, that’s…”

“Come on, Abel. You don’t have to be such a hardass about it,” Al said, doing his best to mediate. “Let’s simmer down. Bro woke up today and discovered he’s a little kid again. And then he had to deal with a mean old man, so it makes sense his mind’s a jumble. Besides, this isn’t the first time he’s said something erratic, right?”

“Fool. I will not deny his erratic comments, but this situation is what sets it apart.”

Al and Abel stared each other down. The tension was palpable even though both of their expressions were hidden behind a mask or face wrappings.

Al’s comment made Subaru think back to everything that had happened with Abel so far.

Theirs was not an especially long relationship, but even when Subaru proposed capturing Guaral without spilling any blood, Abel was tolerant enough to actually entertain the harebrained idea. Of course, that was primarily because Subaru’s ideas had been useful to Abel.

If I want things to move similarly here, then…

“I—I know where the location behind our eyelids is!”

“What?”

Abel looked dubiously at Subaru holding his hand up emphatically.

Subaru instinctively grimaced as the scary glare from behind that scary mask bored into his head.

It’s not gonna be much of a debate if I cower from a single look.

“I’ll warn you Abel, if you don’t listen to Bro here, there’s not much point in bringing him along. And if you’re gonna leave him out, then I’m not gonna feel like helping out, either.”

Al’s voice dropped as he stood next to Subaru. It was as low as a preteen boy could manage, but it was enough to convey that he was serious. The intensity of Abel’s gaze slowly dissipated.

I didn’t pay much attention before, but these two don’t really get along, huh?

Al was only accompanying them because he had promised to help Subaru. As a fellow Lugunican, he did not have strong feelings about whether Abel reclaimed his throne or not.

At most, his master, Priscilla, wanted it, but…

“Personally, I don’t really care who stands at the top of a country that’s given me nothing but grief.”

“Oh?”

“W-wait! Wait! Stop! Don’t fight! I’m the one who’s at fault!”

As the air between them started to crackle, Subaru gave out first. He moved in between them, waving his arms and trying to prevent a falling-out.

“I see,” Talitta said with a nod. “Subaru is correct. We are in the enemy’s trap in the middle of enemy territory. We have to be warier than ever… That is the important part, right?”

“Right, right! I’m with Subaru and Talitta! It’d be a problem if we got any smaller, right? So let’s be extra careful! Right?”

“Uuu!”

Medium agreed with Talitta, and Louis raised her hands supportively as well.

“Everyone…”

Subaru was moved. Louis aside, his warning had at least gotten through to Medium and Talitta and Al.

The question was whether being careful would be enough for them to survive, but if it came to it, Subaru would just have to put his life on the line to save everyone.

“So?”

“What?”

“So where do you think the location behind our eyelids is?”

Whether he recognized Subaru’s relief or not, Abel calmly returned to the earlier subject.

Noticing Al scoff in annoyance, Subaru turned toward Abel…

It’s nothing new that this emperor really sucks at dealing with people, but…

“You should prepare to get punched by Al once we’re back to normal.”

…and gave him a warning for something a little further down the line.

3

“Right, then…‘an abyss with a view.’”

“Wait, gramps!…Damn it, he’s already gone!”

Orbart slipped out the window and disappeared into the Demon City. Al immediately gave chase, but by the time he reached the window, the crafty old man was nowhere to be found.

“Subaru, where will he hide next…?”

“Mhm, mhm, Subaru’ll know, right? You can guess, right?”

Following the same general conversation as last time, Subaru revealed Orbart’s first hiding place, and now Talitta and Medium both looked at him, full of expectation.

However, unfortunately, the second clue wasn’t nearly as simple.

They would have to work together to unravel what Orbart meant by “abyss with a view.”

“What do you think, Abel? Bro got results, didn’t he?”

“It is a result worthy of being called an accomplishment.”

“…That’s all?”

“There’s no time to spare. What else is there?”

“…Really…?”

The bickering from before was weirdly lingering. But Abel’s attitude was not any different. Al was being oddly insistent about it. Meanwhile, Abel showed no concern for Al’s anger, so it was mostly just Al tilting at windmills.

Anyhow…

“‘With a view’ makes it sound like a high place, doesn’t it?”

“But ‘abyss’ means, like, a hole, right? A hole would be in the ground, wouldn’t it?”

“Those are both good points. Also…right, didn’t you want to go someplace with lots of people, Abel?”

While they were sharing ideas, trying to guess Orbart’s next hiding spot, Subaru wanted to try out Abel’s idea that never got off the ground last time, so he turned the conversation in that direction.

But Abel remained unnaturally silent.

“Hey, Abel. What is it?”

“…You are not mistaken. A place with many people, particularly many outsiders, would be ideal. To gather help.”

“Help? Wait, you don’t mean…?” Al answered in exasperation.

Subaru had not heard the reason for going to a tavern last time, but now that he knew it was to gather people, he grasped Abel’s immature hide-and-seek strategy.

“When carrying out a search, the most fundamental need is numbers. When confirming the rules with Orbart, he did not say anything forbidding the hiring of others. So he cannot complain.”

“Ha-ha, that’s some twisted logic…but not unprecedented. It’s gonna cost money to hire people, though.”

“Arrangements have been made. Talitta.”

“Yes, it is here.”

Nodding, Abel had Talitta retrieve one of the pieces of luggage they had brought in from the carriage. The bag was locked and looked sturdier than the rest.

“Before leaving Guaral, I had Zikr open the town’s vault. Money is the most efficient way to recruit extra hands, so there is no reason not to use it.”

“…Crafty.”

Al sounded almost annoyed as Abel shrugged and ordered Talitta to carry the bag.

Abel’s plan was to hire people for a search party, and if he had the resources to do that, then there wasn’t much reason to argue.

So our goal is a tavern where outsiders gather.

Once everyone prepared themselves for venturing outside, it was time to deal with the problematic development from last time…

“Avoid the main entrance and go out the back,” Abel said.

Subaru was stunned. The sudden about-face made everyone else’s eyes widen, too.

“Huh? You believe what Subaru said?”

“It is always best to be cautious. But since he pinned down Orbart’s location once, his warning is worth considering. That’s all.”

“…Al’s fist won’t be the only one you have to watch out for.”

Abel harrumphed at Subaru’s bitter warning. His high-and-mighty act aside, Abel’s decision to move carefully was helpful. If he had not suggested it, Subaru would have had to come up with a plausible reason to take the back door.

“I guess that’s his way of saying you did a good job, Bro.”

“…I guess. Well, this is sort of how it’s always been.”

For some reason, he had started to doubt Abel’s creed of always rewarding success and punishing failure.

Subaru had already realized that understanding that philosophy would make it easier to get along with Abel, and yet for some reason, it felt like he was constantly relearning how to interact with him.

“Still, though, good job figuring out the old man’s hiding spot. Was almost like you read a strategy guide.”

“Strategy guide… Now that’s a phrase that brings back memories… Would sure be convenient if we could consult one. I only figured it out thanks to experience.”

“Experience? At hide-and-seek?”

“Something like that. There was a time that… Hmm…”

As he smiled awkwardly, Subaru’s thoughts froze.

The reason he had thought Orbart would be in the starting room was because that was a classic move. And there should have been someone who tried to pull it on Subaru before Orbart.

That’s why I thought of it immediately with Orbart’s hide-and-seek. But when was that?

Subaru made awkward grunting sounds, trying to remember.

“Hey, you’re supposed to be a kid again. Don’t be forgetting things like an old man, Bro.”

“Forget…”

“Okay, look, whatever happened in that memory, it was probably someone in your crew, right? Doubt it would be that silver-haired girl, so that little girl who’s always…”

“—Beatrice!”

“Whoa!”

Subaru’s face shot up, making Al recoil in surprise. But Subaru was too preoccupied to notice that.

“What a sick joke…”

He was dumbfounded.

This is crazy, no matter how you look at it. Beatrice. Beatrice!

His partner and the most adorable great spirit there was. The first prank she had pulled on him had been the key to finding Orbart.

If anyone deserved kudos, then it was both of them. Together.

How did that slip my mind? There’s no way that would normally happen.

“Subaru! Al! Come quickly!”

Talitta’s sharp voice cut through Subaru’s astonishment. Looking up, he saw her peering through the back door of the inn, a tense wariness written across her beautiful face. The reason for that was none other than the danger that had found them last time—

“We are already surrounded. There are at least one hundred of them.”

“Ngh?!”

A tiger at the front, and wolves at the back.

That was the first thing that sprang to mind when Subaru heard Talitta’s report. But that idiom didn’t do justice to how wildly outnumbered they were.

I thought something bad was coming, but a hundred is…

“A hundred enemies?!”

“Yes, at least. More may be coming.”

Al’s voice cracked in a fuss, but Talitta answered him calmly.

Talitta seemed like she didn’t handle surprises well, so her reaction was unexpected. But in this situation, the more people who were calm, the better.

Especially when Subaru was already off-balance dealing with his scrambled brain.

“Just surrounding us? Any sign of movement?”

“Not yet. They may be waiting for the rest of their allies, but…”

“If they are not attacking, then we have not met whatever requirement they are waiting for.”

As he shook his head at Talitta’s suggestion, Abel’s eyes grew thoughtful.

But he did not need long. After just a few seconds, he spun around, hand against the brow of the mask, and looked at Subaru.

Subaru gulped at the intensity of the gaze, even through the mask.

“What will compel them to attack?”

“Huh…?”

He did not know what to do with that sudden question, or the air he had just inhaled.

“Answer me. What is the condition that will cause them to attack?”

Subaru’s eyes spun, and he was unable to answer as Abel pressed him again. Finally, he managed to grasp what he was being asked, but even understanding it, he did not have an answer.

I can’t explain what I don’t know. I haven’t even figured out who they are.

“Answer me.”

Barreling through Subaru’s unease and confusion, Abel demanded to know. Even as Subaru struggled and failed to answer, the furious masked man grabbed him by his small shoulders.

“Answer me! Subaru Natsuki!”

“I—I don’t know! Just…if we go out, they’ll attack us… That’s all!”

Answering in the pressure of the moment, Subaru grabbed his chest. He had reflexively revealed information he knew from Return by Death. He cowered at the possibility of encroaching on the taboo, but nothing happened.

Time did not stop, and the demonic hand that inflicted his punishments did not appear.

But instead…

“Uuu!”

Louis burst in between the two of them, as if to protect Subaru, knocking away the arms gripping him by the shoulders.

Abel looked at Louis with annoyance, but she quickly received support from a reassuring ally—Medium.

“Don’t bully Subaru! I’ll tell on you to my big bro!”

“…What would the point of that even be? And I simply made him reveal the necessary information.”

Abel was unmoved, answering Medium’s accusatory eyes without concern. Medium’s cheeks puffed up in a pout, but Subaru was in no place to notice any of that.

He could not believe he just let Abel say and do whatever he wanted. And the way he had been taken aback by his threatening demeanor. The feeling that he could not put into words…that was fear.

It’s as if…

“Like an adult talking to a kid. And not just because of looks,” Al spat.

Subaru grabbed at his chest and looked down. That was probably what Al thought at seeing that exchange, but the phrasing he used brought the big, fuzzy feeling Subaru had been struggling with into focus. The instinctive fear he had felt with Abel was the power dynamic between an adult and a child.

He had become a child in body, but he was starting to become one in mind as well, and it was noticeably affecting his thoughts…

“Listen. I have discerned who has deployed this force,” Abel announced.

“…! Seriously?” Al asked in surprise.

Abel held up two fingers for everyone to see.

“First of all, the number of people capable of raising a group of one hundred or more people in the Demon City is limited. That leaves only two options. The emperor’s group and the true culprit.”

“Sounds like you’ve already ruled out the fake emperor and his people. Anything to back that up, Abel?”

“Orbart’s actions would be contradictory if the orders came from Chisha.”

Subaru was convinced. If these hundred people were working for the fake emperor, then that would mean he had withdrawn the hands-off order, in which case Orbart would gladly capture them and commence the torture.

“I get it, but it’s an unpleasant sort of trust… Still, though, isn’t there a chance of him twisting things somehow?”

“Then let me ask you this: Do you think I would adopt such a plan?”

“Not at all,” Talitta answered, without hesitation, and Al reluctantly shook his head, too.

That was the false emperor’s dilemma—so long as he was trying to pass as Abel, his decisions would have to match Abel’s. He couldn’t do anything the real Abel wouldn’t do. Chisha had to fully embody the stiff and unyielding emperor to be convincing.

“But if the fake you isn’t responsible, then…”

“Yeah, it’s gotta be the other option, since Abel was calling them the culprit anyway.”

Medium and Al looked to Abel for an answer. Naturally, everyone, other than Louis, who did not understand the situation, focused on Abel.

Lowering one of his two fingers, he continued.

“Given the conditions Orbart set and the crowd gathering outside… When you consider who has the standing to set the pieces on the board this way, the possibilities are naturally limited.”

“So, in all your wisdom, Abel, why don’t you tell us who—?”

“It is Chaosflame,” Abel declared.

But that name didn’t ring any bells. That was only natural, since it was not the name of a person but of the entire city.

“Chaosflame…in other words, the residents of the Demon City. Besides the emperor, there is no other force capable of mobilizing so many people in this city.”

Unlike Subaru and the others who were dumbfounded by the situation, he had already considered all the possibilities. While Abel readily accepted the identity of the enemy, Subaru struggled to understand. But if he was right, then that would be a really big deal.

If it’s the people of the city waiting for us outside, then the mastermind who sent them has to be—

“Does that mean Yoruna told them to attack us?” Medium asked.

“…Kind of hard to imagine another possibility,” Al said. “Not like anyone else knows who we are and has a reason to sic a mob on us.”

“…Abel? What do you think?”

A person capable of mobilizing the residents of Chaosflame. The obvious choice would be the ruler of this city, Yoruna Mishigure, but even though she was as inscrutable as Orbart, if not more, she had made a big show of acknowledging them as messengers. Would she really pull a dirty trick like this after all that?

That was the implication in Subaru’s question, and Abel tapped the forehead of his oni mask.

“It doesn’t make sense.”

That succinct answer was unfortunately not enough to get Subaru and the others to understand, and perhaps sensing that, he continued with a sigh.

“The letter you delivered yesterday offered a reward that she desires.”

“Something she wants…meaning the position of empress?”

“Becoming your wife, Abel?”

Al and Medium immediately chimed in when he brought up the letter. From what they talked about yesterday, the thing Yoruna wanted was the emperor, whether it be Abel or someone else who held the throne.

That’s presumably what she wants above all else.

“What are you doing, putting that in a letter?”

“Do not trivialize this problem to your standards. I offered her what she wanted. That is why she summoned us back to the palace. That is why it does not make sense to also send attackers.”

“Ah, well, maybe she hates the idea of marrying you so much, she’d rather kill you…”

Or it’s because maybe he wrote something insulting in the letter. He’s already this bad when you talk to him directly, so there’s a decent chance he was arrogant as hell in writing, too.

But Abel just snorted at their guesses.

“I would do it if the need arose. Emotions are secondary. I am not Priscilla.”

“I was thinking she felt sort of similar to the princess when it comes to how dangerous they can be!”

Subaru agreed there. Priscilla and Yoruna were both scary. But with how confidently Abel said it, he couldn’t help but feel like there was some logic to Abel’s explanation, too.

Then he thought back to what she said yesterday.

“I am the master of this city, and I would not lie before my retainers.”

And then she made a promise. As proud as she was, it was hard to imagine she would go back on her word. If anything, it seemed more in character for her to come straight out and declare war herself.

“Neither Chisha nor Yoruna Mishigure makes sense as the mastermind behind these assassins, but nonetheless, it appears that the residents of the Demon City have risen up against us. And thus—”

“The enemy is Chaosflame, huh…?”

“Indeed.”

With Abel’s acknowledgment, Subaru and the rest were finally caught up. They now understood that there weren’t a lot of clear answers.

While they were doing that—

“They are reaching the limits of their patience. What shall we do?”

Talitta was watching the outside and warned them that there wasn’t much time left.

We’ve been under the assumption they’ll only attack once we go outside, but if they’re ready to go at a moment’s notice, there’s really no telling when they might try to force their way in.

They needed to escape the inn. However, if they went outside without a plan, they would die like last time…

“Talitta, draw their attention.”

“Abel?!”

He had issued the cruelest order.

Talitta’s face tensed, and Subaru’s voice cracked as he shouted, but Abel ignored him and kept his eyes on Talitta.

“Run wild and draw the attention of those outside. We will escape during your diversion.”

“Abel, I get the idea, but there’s gotta be a better—”

“There isn’t,” he said, cutting off Al. “At present, this is the path with the greatest chance of success, given our current tools. Had you not shrunk in size, there would be other possibilities, but that is not the reality we are living in.”

“No, this can’t be right!”

“Auuu!”

Al was concerned for Talitta, but Abel immediately cut him off. Subaru clenched his jaw at that cold judgment, and Louis erupted in indignation, too, but—

“No, I will do it. I shall draw them away.”

“Talitta! That’s too…”

Talitta shook her head and accepted Abel’s crazy order.

Subaru wanted to come up with a better plan that would keep her safe, but his mind was filled with both unease and growing wariness of what the crowd outside would do.

“Talitta, give me the bag. I will need it after this.”

“Of course. I will hold their attention, so please escape in the meantime. I do not think I will have a chance to signal…”

Abel took the bag Talitta was carrying and slipped it over his slender shoulder.

“There’s no need. I will leave the timing to Medium.”

“Eh? Me?” Medium’s eyes widened.

Turning to her, Abel nodded.

“Yes. Though you are smaller now, your sharp eye remains unchanged. You are the most capable of choosing the right moment to break out.”

“Mm, got it. I’ll watch carefully! Be careful, Talitta!”

“Of course.”

The conversation barreled along, leaving Subaru in the dust.

Abel is one thing, but Talitta and Medium also have nerves of steel. Talitta especially, when she’s got the most dangerous role of all.

“I’ll be going now.”

Gripping her bow, she put her hand on the door. Unable to restrain himself, Subaru shouted, “Talitta! Um, don’t die…!”

“………”

He hated himself for saying something so basic. If he couldn’t offer a useful idea or a surefire strategy, then he should at least have said something more encouraging. And yet all he managed was a trembling plea.

But Talitta’s eyes softened slightly.

“Yes, we’ll again.”

Smiling faintly, Talitta leaped out, and as she proceeded into enemy territory, Abel said one last thing.

“Talitta, there is no need to hold back. Fight with everything you have. So long as they are enjoying the protection of soul marriage, none of the people of this city will die so easily.”

It was neither encouragement nor a strategy but an eerie admonition.

4

The moment she stepped outside, Talitta sensed a giant swell of hostility.

Her dark skin prickled in anticipation. Talitta’s narrowed eyes took in her surroundings with one glance.

To a Shudrak who lived as a hunter in the jungle, grasping the lay of the land and the situation in an instant was a fundamental skill and one that Talitta had mastered.

And as her sister Mizelda had entrusted her to lead their people, she needed to be even better than her fellow Shudrak. And she was.

“Ah.”

She made a faint noise in the back of her throat as she took stock of the number of enemies who were homing in on her. There were approximately one hundred people in the area who intended to attack her and her companions, but fewer than twenty had noticed her flying out the back door. She readied herself to start shooting their legs—

“—No.”

She remembered Abel’s warning to hold back nothing right before she left.

Abel was haughty and handsome. The sort of man who met Mizelda’s standards, but not someone Talitta was particularly good at dealing with. She was more prone to being pushed around and getting dragged into things, so she often struggled to voice her own opinion when interacting with people like her sister and Abel.

She preferred people who would listen to her. Especially since she took time to gather her thoughts and was prone to getting flustered when hurried too much.

Yes, someone like Flop is very much…

“…! What am I thinking?”

Her face turned red for a moment. She quickly drew her bow, as if to wipe it away. In one fluid motion, she had nocked three arrows at once, adjusting each one slightly with a deft grip, aiming at the vitals of three different targets. Then she released, landing every shot.

Her archery skill was unmatched even among her fellow Shudrak.

“Hunting is nice.”

It suited her personality, since she didn’t have to talk to anyone. Her prey certainly didn’t want to talk to her, and she had no desire to convey her emotions to her prey, either. The only real interaction was when her arrow struck home, and the result, life or death, did not require any long debate.

“—OOOOOOH!”

With a rousing roar, new attackers rushed out of an alley, taking the place of the men who had fallen. A large, broad bull-man more than six feet tall, with two short, thick horns at the top of his head, was in the lead, charging straight at Talitta.

The road was narrow, and there was nowhere to run to the left or right. So Talitta ran forward instead.

“Gah?!”

The bull-man’s eyes widened in shock. His surprise only grew when Talitta’s shoe crunched his nose as she used him as a launching pad and left him with a bloody nose.

Spinning through the air, she rose above the buildings lining the street.

While spinning, she managed to take stock of her surroundings once again, allowing her to also see the enemies positioned on many of the rooftops and raised walkways that filled this city.

“I don’t have enough arrows.”

Even as she said that, she reached into her quiver and pulled out several arrows. She began loosing a furious barrage of missiles at blinding speed, three at a time, cutting down all her targets. She had to make every shot count and trusted her instincts to decide who seemed the strongest.

The way they stood, the tension in their body, their expressions—everything was factored in.

“Uwaaaaa?!”

Arrows rained down like a hailstorm, and people fell one after the other. Following Abel’s warning, every shot was aimed at a vital point. Many were hit in their necks and chests, and whenever possible, Talitta aimed at eyes and mouths.

Around thirty enemies had already been dispatched.

However, she had run out of arrows, so the next step was to recover some ammunition.

“…This is a little unexpected.”

Back on the ground, Talitta had intended to head toward the fallen but paused instead.

She was a hunter. She had taken the life of countless creatures. There was some variance depending on the prey, but she was incredibly proficient at locating the vitals of her targets.

She had been confident all her enemies were dead.

“Gh…gh…”

And yet all the people she had hit were merely groaning as they climbed to their feet. Not a single one had died.

Even if they hadn’t sustained mortal wounds, they should have at least been out of the fight. Standing up should have been impossible. And yet they did. Rather than looking to be on the verge of death, they were glaring at Talitta with fierce determination.

She noticed their eyes were different.

“What is that?”

Furrowing her brow, she questioned the bull-man who had risen to his feet. He did not answer, but the change was impossible to ignore.

His right eye was covered by a bright red flame.

His was not the only one. Every person Talitta had shot had a bright red flame in one of their eyes, some right, some left. And it was not just those who had been hit by Talitta’s arrows, either. Those who had come afterward to surround her all had the same red flame over one eye. A flame burning with a wavering light giving off sparks.

But even more surprisingly, the same flame lapped at their wounds, healing them. The bull-man’s broken nose and everywhere people had been hit by arrows, everything.

“…You were a little too vague, Abel.”

Talitta exhaled as the scene combined with Abel’s warning earlier. From what he said, he clearly predicted that something like this would happen.

Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

I wish you had been clearer.

“My role is to be a decoy, not to wipe out the enemy.”

When it came to grabbing their attention, she had done a good job so far.

As for what came next…

“…That’s it for my arrows.”

One after the other, the wounded snapped the arrows still sticking out of them. With no more arrows to recover, Talitta could no longer rely on her formidable archery.

However, that did not mean she had no options.

“A knife and throwing stones are also tools in a hunt.”

Talitta crouched, drawing the knife hidden beneath her formal clothes, raising it together with her bow that had lost its ammunition.

Talitta’s battle had only just begun.

5

Using the opening created by Talitta’s hard fighting, the rest of the party fled through the back door of the inn and ran down the alley. Praying they would not be found while their hundred pursuers were focused on Talitta, they ran and ran, and ran some more.

“Stop. It appears we have shaken off those who were surrounding the inn.”

“Ngh.”

Abel was in the lead when he called a halt, and Subaru pitched forward as he slid to a stop.

His heart was pounding, and his lungs were aching for oxygen. He had almost tripped several times along the way as he ran his hardest in order not to let Talitta’s efforts go to waste.

Thanks to that, they were able to flee into an empty alley without losing anyone along the way.

“But I wonder if Talitta is okay?” Medium said aloud. “She was moving way, way more than I thought she could.”

“Hah, hah…yeah that was crazy. She was like hop, hop, hop and then bam, bam, bam…”

“Bro, are you doing that on purpose or what?”

“…? What do you mean?”

Subaru cocked his head at Al’s question as he caught his breath. He hadn’t intended to say anything strange. He was simply agreeing with Medium and recalling how Talitta had been fighting.

That really was crazy.

The Shudrak warrior was relatively introverted and meek, and he did not know where she ranked in strength among her people, but he had clearly underestimated her.

Now that I think about it, it makes perfect sense.

She had been chosen directly by the previous chief, her older sister Mizelda, and no one among the Shudrak, all of them powerful fighters, raised an objection.

But even for Talitta…

“…How are they fine after being hit by her arrows?”

They had only caught a glimpse of Talitta’s battle with the hundred around the inn, but even that was more than enough to convey just how abnormal the opponents were.

They were resilient enough to resist her attacks and boasted a strength that could not be explained by their demi-human bodies.

And yet they were all dressed like normal townsfolk.

None of them had weapons or armor. That was the eeriest part of it all.

“At that rate, even Talitta will get caught eventually. Is it okay if we don’t go back to help?”

“That is unnecessary. Trust Talitta’s eyes. She is a hunter to her core… She knows well when to pull back and flee. Having burdens come back will just lead to more deaths.”

Abel addressed Medium’s concern with cold, hard logic.

“…Now that you mention it, it sounded like you had some idea of what that was all about,” Al said, pointing at his eye.

He of course did not mean his own eye, but the strange red flame that had appeared in the eyes of all the people Talitta had been fighting.

“What did you call it? Soul marriage…?”

“Yes, soul marriage. I have read about it in an old text. A secret technique that was supposedly lost to time.”

“Lost…as in there aren’t any records of it? But…”

“Most likely, Yoruna Mishigure is the wielder of the secret technique. Though if she is, it could hardly be called sane.”

Crossing his arms and leaning against a wall, Abel shared his conclusion in a heavy voice.

Not sane? I don’t know what effects this secret technique has, but…

“Abel, don’t beat around the bush. What is this soul marriage thing…? You’re hiding too much! Th-this isn’t just your problem to deal with!”

The blood rushed to Subaru’s head, and he erupted at Abel.

It was impossible to forget that flame in their eyes. That flickering red was burned into his memory in his final moment of his last death.

They are definitely the ones who killed me that time…

“Soul marriage is a secret technique that binds the souls of caster and target. This allows a fraction of the caster’s power to be shared, giving the linked the ability to wield power that is normally beyond them.”

Abel finally revealed what he knew. Perhaps Subaru had gotten through to him. However, the roundabout description was hard to parse, and Subaru’s eyes were spinning.

“Perhaps this is easier for you to understand. The caster of the technique, Yoruna Mishigure, has formed a contract linking her soul with everything and everyone that constitutes the Demon City.”

“Wha…?”

Abel used a word that Subaru was intimately familiar with. It was scary to imagine something so important and precious used to describe what was happening here.

“Yoruna Mishigure has connected her own soul with the entirety of this city. As such, all of the residents possess the right to wield a fragment of her power.”

“That’s absurd…” Al murmured in shock.

“As I said, it is not the work of a sane person.”

Subaru felt the same shock of disbelief as Al, and he could only agree with Abel’s conclusion.

The soul marriage technique was, as Abel explained, very similar to the contract forged by a spirit mage and their spirit. If a soul could be equated to Odo, then Subaru and the adorable girl in the big dress, Beatrice, could be described as being linked by a soul marriage.

And the same could be said for Emilia and the little gray cat, Puck.

“But those are just one-to-one relationships…”

“That is the abnormality of Yoruna Mishigure.”

Abel nodded as Subaru’s scattered thoughts slowly came together. There was no fear or disgust in his voice; he simply stated it matter-of-factly. Perhaps because it was so evenhanded, leaving it to the listener to interpret for themselves, it affected Subaru a great deal.

“While only a fragment of their soul is given, as the number of targets increases, the soul of the caster is gradually worn down. To apply that technique to an unknown number of targets and maintain one’s sense of self requires incredible strength of mind. Or else…no, I suppose that is an unnecessary comment.”

Keeping just that final part to himself, Abel finished explaining how soul marriage worked. After hearing that, Subaru thought with growing confidence that the person he met yesterday was scary.

Sharing your soul with so many people…

It would be like Subaru sharing his soul with people besides just Beatrice. Of course, there were some people he might trust. Medium and Al here would not do anything bad with it. But if asked whether he could entrust it to Abel, he would definitely grumble and not want to do it.

“Uuu…”

“Ah.”

His attention was drawn by the little sound and the sudden tug at his shirt.

Louis, her long blond hair tied up behind her head, had behaved herself, keeping up with them while they ran.

No, not just until now.

Louis was surprisingly reasonable, not throwing any tantrums or causing a fuss. She did what she was told and tried her best not to slow them down. And more than anything, it seemed like the reason she grabbed Subaru’s shirt was not because she was worried or scared, but because she was looking for some way to ease Subaru’s anxiety.

“You…”

She was a loathsome, scary, unforgivable being.

He had thought that for so, so long, and he never doubted whether he should. The primary reason he had not abandoned her after being transported to Volakia was because Rem cared about Louis.

Even now, not wanting Rem to hate him was the primary reason Louis was still with him.

And yet…

“Argh, damn it! None of this makes sense!”

“Ngh!”

Subaru was afflicted by feelings he could not put into words, but he was interrupted by Al’s gruff annoyance. Kicking the wall with his small foot, he scratched at his neck.

“In reality, we don’t really know if this is actually that soul marriage thing and our enemy is that lady Yoruna, or if that Old Man Orbart was just lying!”

“A-Al…?”

The man who was so breezy, who took everything in stride, and who knew how to bend with the breeze, who was always devil-may-care in a reassuring way…that man was nowhere to be found. Seething with agitation, he pressed Abel.

“What are you gonna do, Abel? I ain’t gonna keep hanging around like this. I’ve got things more important to me than you getting your shit back, so—”

“I care little about your wishes. However, there is a way to confirm the matter.”

“Confirm what?”

“Whether the resilience of those people is truly due to soul marriage or not.”

Abel pointed to the road connecting to the alleyway. It felt like the road next to the dark alley was almost empty. Glancing out, he saw that there were abandoned tents and empty-looking houses.

It did not seem like Abel was pointing to anything in particular, but…

“There’s nothing there—”

“Pick any random passerby and attack them. If the wound heals, they are under the effects of soul marriage. If not, we can discard the theory that soul marriage is being used.”

Abel made that unbelievable proposal with a completely uninterested tone.

He’s fine with hurting someone, anyone, to test his idea.

The thought was so stupid, so absurd, that the blood rushed to Subaru’s head.

“That’s—”

“Then what will you do? Can you propose an alternative plan?”

Subaru reflexively snapped, but Abel immediately shot back.

The black eyes peering out from the mask pierced Subaru’s heart and made his face grow hot, as if Abel was making fun of him for being shallow and thoughtless. But he couldn’t just stay silent. He did not want to quietly turn tail.

“Th-there must be some other way…”

“If so, then tell me. I will listen to any plan worthy of consideration. Though it would be cruel to expect any such plan from you at the moment.”

“That’s…!”

“You are too scared of making sacrifices.”

With a cold, cruel voice, he hit the crux of what was firing Subaru up.

Feeling like he really had been shot right through the heart, Subaru gritted his teeth and looked down.

I hate sacrifices. Allies, it goes without saying, but even for our enemies, the fewer dead or injured, the better.

Subaru was being rebuked for being naive and immature.

“But what’s so wrong with that?”

“This is not a debate. I am simply stating the truth. If you wish to fulfill your wishes, then you need either ingenuity or strength. If either is insufficient, then you have no choice but to adopt a more realistic wish or to make a compromise. Much like the planning and execution of your bloodless victory.”

“………”

“If you wish to avoid casualties, then you need the strength to achieve those results. If you truly wish for it from the bottom of your heart, then holding back at all is contradictory.”

That accusation tore into Subaru’s heart.

He didn’t know what Abel’s intentions were. But those eyes staring out at Subaru through the mask were probing Subaru’s incomparably weaker eyes for his true feelings.

I don’t get it. I really don’t. How am I holding back?

He racked his brain as hard as he could, fighting back tears, but he couldn’t come up with an answer that made sense.

With my smaller arms, legs, and lungs, I can’t jump around like Talitta. The whip I brought is big and heavy, and I can’t really use it right now. But if I don’t want people to get hurt, then…

“Then I should be the only one who gets hurt!”

His thoughts awhirl, Subaru shouted at Abel in frustration.

I know I’m too weak and too stupid. That was a problem Subaru Natsuki had long had before being shrunk down.

Subaru clenched his eyes shut, feeling something warm welling up from inside. Before that turned into a clear and obvious stream of tears, he turned around and started running.

“Bro?!” “Subaru!”

Al and Medium shouted, but he ignored them as he ran outside. To make up for what Abel had said was lacking. To reach the results he wanted…

“Come and get me! I’m right here!”

Subaru stood in the middle of the street, spreading his arms wide and shouting as loud as he could.

A child’s shrill voice echoed in the quiet street. His shoulders heaved, and his breaths came raggedly after all his shouting. That was when he noticed—a white-haired boy who was around the same age as Subaru looked, just outside the alley, staring at him in surprise.

“Ah.”

He immediately regretted running outside. He’d been rash.

Terror stabbed straight into his heart while his face burned from shame. Subaru turned around to go back for the scolding that surely awaited him.

“Wait.”

“Eh?”

When he felt someone grabbing his arm, he looked up in surprise.

It was none other than the white-haired boy. He was wearing plain clothes and had short, frizzy hair—or rather, it looked short because it was so curly.

Subaru’s lips flapped in confusion, trying to explain what had just happened.

“Sorry.”

“Eh?”

The next moment, Subaru was sent flying by the boy who had a flame in his right eye. He didn’t understand why his whole world was spinning. It had happened so suddenly, he was still trying to catch up.

“Whaaaaaaaa?!”

Questions like why and how bounced around his skull as his insides rattled. The boy who threw Subaru had that telltale flame in his eye. It was probably connected to the soul marriage Abel had mentioned, but Subaru had no way of confirming it while hurtling through midair.

As he spun and fell into the blue sky, Subaru couldn’t do anything.

“Ah—”

His shout was cut short as a strange weightlessness caught his spinning body. It was the sign he had reached the apex of the throw and would soon begin falling, but there was little meaning in that distinction for Subaru.

“Hiiiiyaaaaaaaah!”

His screams echoed back from the fast-approaching ground. It felt like death itself was surging toward Subaru.

“Al!”

“I know!”

He heard the shouts of familiar voices. Then there was a snap of something stretched tight being cut, and then the clatter of multiple thin pieces of metal falling. Subaru had no way of knowing what caused those noises as the ground rushed up to meet him—but right before he slammed into it, he stopped.

“Wah, waaaah, waaaaaaah…wargh!”

Something soft caught him but failed to completely halt his momentum. Subaru spilled onto the hard ground, rolling and rolling until he finally came to a stop. He could taste blood in his mouth, and everywhere ached, but…

“I’m…alive…?”

As he pushed himself up, Subaru could hardly believe he hadn’t died. He had kept his wits about him long enough to grasp that it was Al and Medium who had saved him. To catch him, they had cut down one of the tents in the street, stretching it out tight to make an on-the-spot cushion.

That was what stopped Subaru from slamming straight into the ground. But they had paid a price for it.

“Owwwwww…”

“A-Al! Medium!”

Subaru saw them both lying in the street. With their bodies shrunken down, they couldn’t perform like they usually did and had been knocked back by the impact of catching Subaru. And there was more bad news…

“I was hoping to end it with that…”

The face of the boy who threw Subaru was twisted in agony. Looking at Subaru and the other two, he bit his lip. His right eye continued to burn with the red flame.

Between that flame and the strength to throw Subaru like that, there was no room for doubt. He was one of the enemies.

“Hey…hey! You…”

“This has to be done. This city can’t…we can’t lose her.”

Subaru pushed his aching body, trying to draw the boy’s attention.

On the one hand, he did not want the boy to attack Al or Medium, but when their eyes met, when he saw the desperation in the boy’s face, his heart wavered. That face was familiar. Those were the eyes of someone who was willing to take drastic action for the sake of someone.

It was the same expression on the faces of all the people who had faced Talitta.

“I won’t ask you to forgive me. I’m sorry.”

His eyes were still uncertain as he slowly came closer.

Subaru tried to crawl away, but he was still hurting from the fall, and his arms and legs refused to listen to him.

If I can’t get away, then at least…

Determined to not look away, he stared into the boy’s eyes. Then he noticed something peeking out from the sides of his head. Little horns poked out from his white, curly hair. It was almost like seeing a lamb.

With that final thought, the boy with a burning eye raised his arm high—

“………”

Subaru grimaced but watched carefully. He would not miss what the boy did.

“Aa, uuu!!!”

There was a dull thud and a spray of red as the blond girl leaped between them, before she was knocked away like a fluttering leaf.

chapters.title: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29
chapters.text:
Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

CHAPTER 4

A XXXXXXXX THAT DOES NOT FADE

1

The tiny girl spun through the air with a feeble cry. Her body bounced along the ground, across the street, barely losing any momentum until she slammed into the pole of a tent stall that finally stopped her.

“………”

Subaru watched, dumbstruck, unable to say a word.

It all happened in an instant, but he couldn’t claim ignorance. Even if he couldn’t react in that instant, he saw it clear as day with his own two eyes.

His head burned, and he leaped out in a fit of emotion.

“…Louis.”

Louis had spread out her arms to protect Subaru, and she had been swatted aside like a rubber ball, leaving a trail of blood behind her. It was impossible to think she was fine after that.

“I’m sorry.”

As the tent Louis struck collapsed around her, he heard an apology. It had come from the same sheep-boy who had swatted her aside. Now he was standing over Subaru with his arm raised and a pained look on his face. Subaru’s head was next.

As much as he wanted to, after all Louis had done to protect him, he could not bring himself to evade…

“Subaru! Stand up!”

A shadow flitted through the air. Its slender leg kicked the boy in the shoulder. The boy recoiled with a stunned look, and standing there was Medium, her long blond hair fluttering in the breeze. She had shouted at Subaru so loudly, she had gone bright red. Subaru had just been sitting listlessly, unable even to shiver in fear.

“Take care of Louis!”

And yet Medium offered him neither encouragement nor consolation before rushing forward. Holding the one sword she had brought with both her slender little arms, she gallantly charged the sheep-boy, even though it was impossible to use her usual cool and stunning dance-like fighting style.

The boy seemed more surprised by her spirit than by her strength.

“Gh, uugh…”

Roused by the sight of Medium fighting with everything she had, Subaru managed to struggle to his feet with trembling arms and legs before rushing over to the tent where Louis had fallen.

“Louis! Louis! Are you alive?! Louis!”

Desperately calling her name, he felt a heat building in the back of his eyes again. That heat had been building, threatening to burst out. He pushed it back down, hurrying to clear the debris.

“…Aa, uuu…”

“Louis!”

A faint groan led Subaru to Louis’s dust-covered body. She was lying beneath one of the tent stall’s fallen poles. It had gotten wedged in a way that prevented the full weight of the collapsed structure from bearing down on her.

Just as he sighed in relief, he noticed the growing red stain spreading across Louis’s white outfit.

“…Ah…”

Subaru’s eyes widened, and a chill shot through his arms and legs. His mind went blank.

He turned pale. He felt his blood turn to ice.

And his heart pounded like it was about to explode.

“Aaa…”

Louis groaned as the stain gradually spread.

He needed to pull her out of the wreckage so he could perform first aid, but the tent pole was so heavy that even when he leaned his whole body into it, the pole refused to budge.

“Louis. Louis…”

He called her name with trembling lips. His voice cracked, but not from his tongue going numb. It was because for so long, he had taken every opportunity to avoid calling her by name. Thinking back on it, he had hated so much as saying her name.

Louis had been with him ever since he had been transported from that tower with Rem. He had always kept his distance, keeping a watchful eye on her, treating her like an obstacle and a nuisance. And yet she had never once done anything that got in his way or put him in danger.

I didn’t want Rem to hate me. I didn’t want everyone to be afraid.

Those worries had convinced him to avoid getting close to Louis the whole time and to put off the question of what to do with her.

Why was I so scared of her?

His exhausted mind, his cold limbs, his heavy tongue, and his pounding heart all made him forget. In this singular moment, he could not remember what it was that Louis had done to him. Only one thought filled his mind now—she had bled to protect him.

No matter how much I want to forget or avert my eyes, that’s the truth.

“Don’t…die…”

“………”

“Don’t die, Louis! You can’t, you can’t die…! You can’t die!”

Twisting his body into the space below the support pole, Subaru crawled next to Louis on his knees. Clutching her hand in both of his, he shouted with a desperate prayer.

“Don’t die…!”

Forgetting all about trying to find something he could do to actually keep her from dying, he just made an unreasonable prayer.

As she heard his trembling voice, Louis’s eyes opened weakly…

“…Ua, uu…”

2

“Ukyaaa?!”

The single sword she was holding in both hands was knocked back, and Medium slammed into a wall. Slipping to the ground, she saw the sheep-boy swinging his arm wildly. The boy with a flame in his right eye was a total amateur at fighting and not even particularly fast.

“And I still can’t keep up…”

Medium gritted her teeth, unhappy at being pushed back by a boy who was relying on sheer brute force. His movements were haphazard, and he had no technique. It was like fighting a big baby. Not that she had ever seen a baby that big before.

“Al! Al!!!”

She thought there would at least be something she could do if she was not alone, so she called out to her comrade. Out of the corner of her eyes she saw Al huddled over near the ground. He had been shrunk down like she had, but unlike her, he was smart, so she would have liked him to try something, anything.

“………”

But he didn’t answer her call.

Not because he had been knocked unconscious after being thrown back. Al was awake and had actually tried to help once. But now, for some reason, he was crouched down and staying still.

He was just looking at his own trembling right hand while…

“…Why…?”

He was shuddering almost like he had dropped something that he had been holding.

Meanwhile, the boy was slowly walking over to Medium. And more bad news…

“There! It’s them!”

Behind Al, ten people raced down the street. They all were different races, but they all had the same red flame in one eye—more pursuers.

She turned away from the boy and started to rush over to Al to meet the new threat. But just as she started to act on that unreasonable idea, she fell to her knee with the first step. The boy had grabbed her long hair.

“Al…!”

Eyes watering, she reached out, unable to reach Al as the attackers caught up…

“You still can’t move? Fool.”

With Al in such a dangerous predicament, a figure stepped between him and the charging townsfolk. It was the masked man who had been watching in silence from the alley.

“Abel…?”

Though she was still restrained by her hair, nothing interrupted Medium’s surprised murmur. Everyone was awestruck by the strange appearance and powerful aura of the man. But that would not buy them much time. The first of the men barreling down the street, a middle-aged bull-man, shook off his surprise and stepped up to Abel.

“Sorry, kid…but we can’t let you get away. You’re gonna have to—”

“A bull-man. Earlier, there was a sheep-boy.”

“What?”

“You and all of those surrounding the inn are horned…with so many in one place, anyone would notice. So it is the horned tribes of the city who are after us.”

Despite being surrounded and in a dangerous predicament, Abel did not waver, but the men trembled under his piercing gaze.

“Horned…”

Medium’s eyes shifted as she glanced at the boy holding her in place. There were two horns poking out of his frizzy white hair. And all the men surrounding Abel had horns, too. The horns varied in location and number, but all of them had at least one.

And evidently, this was something they didn’t want to draw attention to. The mood in the air grew noticeably more dangerous when the subject of horns came up.

“You may test yourself.”

“…What?”

Abel addressed the man edging closer to him, like a challenge.

“Test whether you are capable of killing me or not.”

Not like a challenge. This was an explicit and direct challenge. Naturally, the bull-man was furious, and the intensity of the flame in his right eye visibly increased.

“…What could be difficult about snapping such a tiny neck?”

“Whether it is simple or not can easily be proven. And so you may test yourself. If you are worthy, then the flames will laud you. However…”

“H-however?”

“If you are lacking, the flames will incinerate you and your very soul. Now, what shall you do?”

Arms crossed, Abel silenced the bull-man with his declaration. None of the other men said anything, either, caught up in Abel’s performance. The sheep-boy gulped and simply waited to see what would happen.

Even Medium, one of Abel’s comrades, could only watch.

“You may undergo the judgment of the flames. Will your life surpass mine?”

“Gh…ugh…ugh…!”

The man’s voice quivered, and he agonized beneath a sudden sheen of sweat. No one could intervene. The moment they saw Abel’s eyes, everyone else was swept from the stage. No one had the right to answer Abel’s call, save for the man standing before him.

Gritting and grinding and grinding and gritting his teeth, the man—

“Ugh, uoooooo!!!”

There was a crack from his teeth, and the pain set the man in motion, raising both his thick arms. It was an attack aimed not just at snapping Abel’s neck but at smothering every last trace of life out of him. If it landed, Abel would die, no matter how good he was at bluffing.

Medium desperately tried to twist away, but she could not escape. Al could not move, either, as he watched it unfold.

And Subaru and Louis also—

“—Eh?”

Louis was underneath both the collapsed tent and Subaru, who had tried to help save her. She could see Subaru underneath the tent pole, holding Louis’s hand.

She saw Louis move slightly, and then—

“Uuu!”

—In the blink of an eye, Louis appeared under the bull-man with his arms raised, hitting him directly in the jaw from right beneath him.

3

Subaru could not make heads or tails of what happened.

He had been clinging to the bleeding girl lying under the collapsed tent, praying for her to survive. Unable to help her or comfort her, just selfishly praying for her not to die. She moved a little in response to his words, and right after that—the scene Subaru saw suddenly shifted, and the world flipped.

“Uu, eee.”

It was not at some crazy speed or as if time stood still. He had moved to a different location in the blink of an eye.

And…

“You…”

Abel caught his breath ever so slightly at Subaru’s unexpected appearance.

It was bewildering to find himself sitting in front of the masked man, who had his arms crossed, and in front of all the people around them. The tears that had been welling up for Louis just a moment ago faded, and his throat clenched.

chapters.title: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29
chapters.text: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

chapters.title: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29
chapters.text:
Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

And the girl who was the source of Subaru’s confusion…

“Aaa, uuu!”

“Gah?!”

Spinning with the speed and erratic movements of a pinball, Louis bounced around between the men, landing critical hits to necks, chests, knees, and making other pinpoint strikes, breaking the encirclement by force.

While the men still struggled to come to grips with the speed and force of the sudden attack, Louis started making her next move.

“Uau.”

Moving around behind them, she put her hands on the ground like an animal and clawed at it, dragging the upper layer of dirt back like it was a luxurious carpet.

There was no carpet spread out across the street, of course, and yet that was what the ground looked like to Subaru. More attackers toppled over when the floor was pulled out from underneath them.

“Au! Au au!”

“Wh-what’s with this kid…?! Shit!”

A young deer-man just barely managed to hold his balance and lunged at Louis, but she threw the thin layer of earth she had just pulled up at him. He swiped at it with his arm, and the moment he made contact, it instantly reverted to its original state.

“Bgh?!”

Slamming into what was now a wall of dirt, the young man reeled backward. Louis then tore through the ragged wall of dirt and landed a flying kick on his face, sending a spurt of blood into the air as she launched off him and flew high up.

Grabbing on to the wall above the men, she pulled away the surface layer of the wall just like she had done with the ground, and then did it again and again, creating several slices of a paper-thin wall. When the peeled-off wall sheets returned to their previous state, they fell down on the men.

“Ywaaaaaa!!!!”

Louis seemed to teleport behind them as they screamed. She stuck out her palm, hitting one in the back while using a different sort of technique on the arm of another man who tried to counterattack, mercilessly throwing him aside.

The attackers were helpless before Louis, who seemed to wield the power of ten people in the body of one little girl.

“L-Louis…that’s…”

It was a nightmare. There was no other word for it. This was very obviously not the result of natural talent or years of training and studies. Subaru knew the true source of that power.

That’s…that’s a power that shouldn’t exist…

“So…this is the reason you were traveling with that girl?” Abel said as he stepped forward to stand next to Subaru.

“Eh?”

For a moment, he didn’t understand, but once he realized Abel meant Louis, his blood rose to his head.

He was about to vehemently deny it, but…

“…Ah.”

He had no other explanation for why he was traveling with Louis. He could not answer it before, and he still could not answer it now.

“St-stop! If you care about this gi—argh?!”

“Auau!”

When he saw the rest of the group crumbling, the sheep-boy still holding on to Medium’s hair tried to take her hostage, but before he could even finish the threat, Louis was already standing right next to him while he was still reeling. She touched his shoulder, and the next moment, the boy and Louis were both somehow five yards overhead. The boy had no idea what to do when he found himself in the middle of the air and falling headfirst toward the street together with Louis. He landed, let out a weak groan, and went still.

“D-did you do all this…Louis?”

“Aauu.”

Medium’s eyes widened just as Louis leaped into her arms. She rubbed Louis’s head and looked around the alleyway blankly now that she was free.

The dozen or so pursuers in the street were all knocked out and scattered around.

“You and the jester have revealed your true natures, I suppose? Well, so be it.”

“Wh-what the heck is going on…? What was that?!”

“Quiet yourself. You will only draw more attention to us. Grab the jester and come.”

Abel gestured with his chin, ordering Subaru to carry on rather than dwell on their escape. He was pointing toward Al, who was still huddling on the ground, not moving. Subaru rushed over, worried Al might have gotten hurt while he was not watching.

“A-Al! Hey, are you all right? Are you hurt somewhere…?”

“…I’m…not all right.”

“…! Were you wounded?! Where? Let’s take care of it…!”

“Not that!”

Al shouted angrily when Subaru shook his shoulder. Still huddled over, he raised his trembling hand and clenched it.

“…I’m useless.”

“Th-that’s not—”

“I’m useless! The way I am now…I’ll die.”

“…? What do you—?”

He was about to ask what Al meant by that, but before he could, an urgent voice from behind him interrupted.

“Abel! Don’t do anything bad!” Medium shouted.

“Silence. There is a question that must be asked.”

“Still…”

Turning around, Subaru saw them arguing over the sheep-boy still on the ground. The boy was sitting up, looking at Louis in terror. The flame in his eyes was weaker, and it was clear that even if he could still fight on a physical level, he was finished mentally. That was understandable. Unlike Subaru and his shrunken friends, he was actually a child. He’d just watched multiple adults get beaten senseless, and he had been completely cornered, too. It made more sense to be scared.

“Answer me.”

Abel showed the boy no mercy. As he crouched right in front of the boy, wearing the mask that prevented anyone from reading what he was thinking, Abel’s eyes peered into that fear and terror and demanded he reveal what he knew.

The boy’s teeth chattered.

“Tell me where your leader is. Where is that girl who called herself Tanza hiding? Speak quickly.”

4

Subaru’s eyes widened. The name that crossed Abel’s lips was the last one he’d expected.

“Tanza? That girl…?”

The kimono-clad deer-girl appeared in Subaru’s confused mind. She was Yoruna’s attendant and had been there both yesterday at the palace keep and earlier today at the inn. She was still a child but was calm and collected, almost curt.

Abel had confidently declared that she was the one who set up this attack.

“Answer me. You are mistaken if you believe youth absolves you of your actions.”

The cold voice bore into the cowering boy, and the flame in his eye wavered, but the weak flame recovered slightly in the face of Abel’s intense questioning.

“Th-there’s no way I would know! You’re the ones who would know…!”

“………”

“You’re the ones who… That’s why we…!”

The boy snapped back at Abel and reached out a hand toward him. In a desperate move, he tried to grab Abel by the throat and strangle him, but before he could, a small palm pushed hard against his forehead.

“Au!”

The boy’s head slammed backward against the wall, knocking him out. The boy slumped over, twitching miserably.

And the one who had done it…

“L-Louis…”

“Uau!”

Louis had disappeared from Medium’s side in the blink of an eye and laid the boy low. When Louis heard Subaru’s voice, her face brightened, and she leaped at him.

Caught in her hug, he was struck by a thought that chilled him to the bone.

That looked a lot like the short-range warp that Gluttony had used in the tower in the desert. And all those various other fighting styles were not the sort of thing a single person could learn on their own in a single lifetime. There was no denying it anymore after seeing that.

“You’re…”

Louis Arneb, Archbishop of Gluttony and wielder of a skin-crawling authority. The girl in that white realm who had torn into Subaru’s heart and tried to devour every last bit of his soul. The very girl who mistook his Return by Death for a blessing and who called Subaru a monster.

“…G-get away from me.”

“Au?”

“I said get away!”

Grabbing her by the shoulders, he pushed her off. Louis fell back, and with some distance, he saw the red all around her torso, reminding him again that Louis had been injured protecting him.

“Ah…the wound?! We have to take care of that…!”

“Au! Aaauuu!”

He quickly started to roll up her clothes to check the wound, but Louis flailed, as if he were tickling her, and fought back, pushing at his face and chest. He ignored that, forcefully peeling back her clothes. But while there were still traces of blood on her clothes and skin, there wasn’t any visible injury.

“It’s…healed…?”

She was definitely bleeding before.

It felt like a fox was playing tricks on him as he blinked over and over. He had questions but also a faint sense of relief. Seeing Louis smiling right in front of him, Subaru looked away.

“We must find that troublesome Orbart at once.”

Abel murmured to himself as he slowly stood up, heedless both of the danger he had been in moments ago and of the fact that he had just been saved.

Subaru agreed that they should focus on finding Orbart, but it was a little too disconnected from what Abel had been saying earlier.

“What did you mean by that?”

“And which part are you asking about?”

“Earlier! You said that Tanza girl is the mastermind, but now you’re saying we have to search for Mr. Orbart or whatever.”

“Hmph.”

Abel put a hand to his masked forehead, as if that was a stupid question. Subaru was already feeling impatient and annoyed, and that reaction only got on his nerves, so in a fit, Subaru leaped up and pulled the mask off Abel’s face.

Abel glowered at Subaru.

“What is the meaning of this?”

“That’s what I should be asking you! Quit just doing everything in your head and explain yourself once in a while! We’re comrades, aren’t we?!”

“Comrades, you say?”

“Ugh…”

The raw emotion of Abel’s glare robbed Subaru of any momentum he had.

His word choice had probably bothered Abel. And Subaru wasn’t all that confident he could call Abel a comrade, either.

His face burned once he realized he had let his mouth run off without thinking again.

“That’s right, Abel. We’re comrades, so you should tell us what you’re thinking.”

Medium came to Subaru’s aid. She was next to Al, who was still hunched over while she rubbed his back. Abel’s eyes narrowed at her earnest and straightforward objection. After some consideration, he said, “The attackers at the inn, and those who followed us here…they are all horned.”

“Horned…meaning people with horns, right? What about it?”

“…The horned have a history of persecution. They were considered inauspicious because their horns bore a passing resemblance to demon beasts’.”

“What…?”

Subaru’s eyes widened.

Being persecuted for having horns. It was a prejudice that struck close to home for Subaru, making it all the more unforgivable. It was a similar sort of reason as why Emilia was persecuted because she resembled an evil witch from long ago, and a ton of different people hated her for it.

The horned demi-humans had the same sort of past.

“But then why? I can understand people being scared of them because of their horns, but it doesn’t make sense.”

“Even if you have become a small child, you should still put your head to work. For those with horns, this city…the way of life in Chaosflame is salvation.”

“Salvation…meaning it’s a good place?”

“Yoruna Mishigure does not give up those whom she has accepted into her heart. There have been times when she raised the flag of rebellion for the sake of a single dead deer-girl.”

The emperor who’d had to deal with her insurrection crossed his arms while calmly giving some much-needed context.

Yoruna had supposedly rebelled many times in the past, but the reason she turned her fangs on the emperor—or at least one of them—was for the sake of a single person.

Subaru’s reaction to hearing that was…

“Then she’s a good person…!”

“Fool. Do you think it’s so simple? Yoruna is a patron of those whom she personally loves and shows no mercy to anyone who falls outside that circle.”

“Ehhh? But it’s normal to be nicer to the people you love, isn’t it?!”

“I think so, too,” Subaru said in agreement with Medium.

Louis raised her hand with an approving shout as well.

Abel sighed.

“What is important is that the horned tribes who have a history of persecution have found peace in this city. And Yoruna Mishigure is crucial to maintaining that peace. Meaning…”

“Meaning?”

“…To these horned people, we are plotters trying to embroil Yoruna Mishigure in a rebellion against the throne. That makes us a menace threatening the foundation of their peace.”

“Ah…”

Subaru finally understood the sheep-boy’s actions.

When he attacked Subaru—when all those townspeople attacked them—they all looked like they were suffering. That was because they felt guilty for killing Subaru and his friends even if it was because they were worried about their home. That was also why the boy had apologized when he threw Subaru.

“They’re all doing their hardest…”

“Sympathy and pity are nothing but a burden. And everything that lives and breathes has their own circumstances.”

“Abel! Don’t say that! Also, I still don’t really get it. Why did you ask about Tanza? And why did you say we have to search for that gramps?”

“…From the way he spoke before, it is likely that they do not know Tanza’s location. And for some reason, they seem to suspect us of hiding her. Why do you think that is?”

“Why? Umm…uh…?”

Looking down at the unconscious boy, Subaru struggled to wrap his head around Abel’s question.

It did not feel like the boy had been lying. He had been convinced Subaru’s party had done something to Tanza, and his comrades probably did, too.

“That’s why they attacked us?”

“That is the logical explanation. However, in truth, we have done nothing to Tanza. So where did she go? In addition, from where did one hundred horned ones appear?”

“Where? They were lying in wait outside, weren’t they?”

“And who gave the order?”

Subaru struggled with the follow-up question. He kicked his brain into high gear, raising a structure around the pillars that Abel had placed down. But before he could finish…

“…That girl told them in advance, before she came,” Al said as he managed to finally stand back up.

Turning around, Subaru saw Medium helping him stay upright. He still looked the worse for wear. When he noticed Subaru’s concerned gaze, Al nodded reassuringly.

“Sorry for worrying you, Bro… Not that things have gotten any better, though.”

“So your condition is unimproved? I suppose that is also due to Orbart’s technique.”

“…I’m not gonna argue there. I’d love to chat about it some more, but we should probably get down to business first. So, about that Tanza.”

Waving his small hand, Al made a conscious effort to rein in his emotions.

I’m worried about what happened to Al, too, but he’s right. We’re still in the middle of this.

The implication was that Tanza had organized their attackers beforehand, but…

“Then that would mean she gathered her horned comrades and had them attack us?”

“But where did Tanza go then?” Medium asked.

It was a question without an answer. She had appeared at the inn to deliver Yoruna’s instructions, and then presumably gone back. Even if they went with the assumption that she had planned everything, the reaction from her comrades was strange.

At the very least, the sheep-boy seemed to believe they had done something to her.

“The little lady clearly didn’t go back to her friends.”

“That is the logical conclusion. And it explains why those who were lying in wait did not attack until after we left the inn. They were afraid of Tanza being caught up in the chaos if they made their move while she was inside talking with us.”

“But then where is Tanza?! What’s going on?” Medium’s eyes spun in confusion.

Subaru, on the other hand, finally had a decent idea what Abel was thinking.

This is probably what he’s got in mind…

“Tanza…if she didn’t leave the inn, then she’s hiding somewhere—and that means Mr. Orbart is helping her!”

5

The horned creatures had attacked them to save Tanza.

But since they were lying in wait outside the inn from the start, the only explanation was that there had been some agreement beforehand in case something happened to Tanza.

And the only one who could have been working with Tanza inside the inn was…

“None save Orbart Dankelken.”

“Couldn’t she…? Couldn’t Tanza have planned it herself?”

“I am confident. Going out of his way to challenge us to a child’s game such as hide-and-seek is the sort of crafty plan he would enjoy.”

Subaru grimaced at Abel’s blunt explanation, both because what he claimed about Orbart’s nasty nature rang true and because the very offer of hide-and-seek was consistent with Tanza being hidden.

“But if that’s why we were attacked, then isn’t that against the rules?”

“You mean the prohibition on harming one another? He would simply say he never raised a hand himself. All the more so if he has joined hands with Tanza.”

“Gh…that’s so unfair…!”

“That is why we must prioritize discerning Orbart’s location. Should we succeed, we may learn Tanza’s location. And having seen through his scheme, there might be no more reason to bother with this hide-and-seek.”

I get that Orbart and Tanza might be together, but I don’t really get why that would mean the end of hide-and-seek.

While Subaru tried to follow this train of thought, Abel turned and ripped the mask from his hands. Subaru yelped in surprise as Abel redonned his disguise.

“Orbart’s goal is to gauge our worth. His true intent is to measure our ability to discern what lies beneath the surface rather than how well we do at some children’s game. If we discover his true motive, then we can avoid troublesome extra steps.”

“Ahh, I get it. I think…?”

“…You are growing progressively dimmer.”

Abel sighed as Subaru barely managed to keep up with the explanation.

Subaru could not really argue. He could feel it, too. His mind was very clearly not firing on all cylinders. And he couldn’t say exactly how bad it was.

My head is getting slower, and the right words won’t come, and I am getting dumber.

“I wasn’t the smartest to begin with, either…”

“In your case, the problem is a decrease in comprehension and imagination… There is a theory that one’s physical condition reflects the ebb and flow of Odo. The details of Orbart’s technique are unknown, though.”

“What exactly does that mean…?”

“Changes in Odo and changes in the body are linked. We can assume that Orbart has manipulated your Odo… That would apply to you two as well,” Abel said as he looked from Subaru to Medium and Al.

The explanation did not really make much sense to Subaru. It had been like that, too, when he broke the gate needed to use magic. The whole thing about mana and Odo just didn’t click for him.

But even if he didn’t really get it…

“So this is all happening because that old man messed with our bodies?”

He was taken aback by the venom in Al’s murmur.

Al was touching his forehead, fingers trembling. His intense mood swings seemed to be a result of his mental regression. The psychological composure he’d had as an adult was fading now that he was a child.

“I’m gonna give that shitty old man a piece of my mind…!”

“Yeah, it’ll be a serious problem if we can’t return to normal,” Medium said, to soothe Al’s seething anger. “Should we go with Abel’s suggestion for now?”

Abel had originally suggested going to a bar to recruit people to search for the old man and to rely on the power of numbers, but…

“The situation has changed if Tanza is acting against us.”

“What do you mean?”

“Now that we have left the inn, it is only a matter of time before the other side makes their move. The strategy of recruiting people for a search is an obvious one, and there are not many options for outsiders without local connections. As such—”

“—It would make sense to station people around the bars to ambush us.”

Al finished Abel’s thought and helped bring Subaru up to speed.

So it’s not just Orbart. Tanza is serious trouble, too.

Orbart had strength and cunning, while Tanza had her position in Chaosflame as Yoruna’s attendant. She was one of the most trusted people in this city.

“If all else fails, forcing our way through may be an option.”

“Forcing our way through… You can’t mean…”

As they discussed how they might need to change plans, Abel glanced to the side. Following his eyes, Subaru froze.

“Uau?”

Louis was standing there, head cocked in confusion as to why Abel was staring at her. She was running her hands through her hair. It was hard to believe that earlier, she had defeated all their attackers. Despite her overwhelming combat ability, she was as sweet as ever.

That only made the chill running down Subaru’s spine worse.

“Oh yeah! Louis was incredible! I had no idea she had moves like that!”

“Auau.”

“Eh-heh-heh, thanks for saving us.”

Heedless of how Subaru felt about it, Medium reached out to pat Louis’s head. Before she could, though, Subaru grabbed her by the wrist.

“Wait!”

“Wah, Subaru?”

“Umm, Medium, you shouldn’t get so close to her…”

“…? Why? She saved me. And she saved you, too.”

“That’s…true…but…”

Subaru didn’t have a good answer to her innocent question. The way she saw it was simple and correct. Louis had saved Subaru. She had put her tiny body on the line to keep him safe.

And Subaru had pleaded for her not to die…

“Isn’t it about time you spilled it already?”

Seeing Subaru’s hesitation, Al spoke up in a low voice.

When Abel fixed him with a dark gaze from behind his mask, Subaru gulped and stared at his feet, reminded that he had withheld the details about his situation with Louis from Al a few days ago on their way to Chaosflame.

He had held back then because he hadn’t decided on how to deal with Louis.

But…

“This ain’t a situation we can keep ignoring. This isn’t just a personal problem of mine. This involves everyone.”

“………”

“What is her secret?”

With all eyes gathering, Subaru reflexively moved in front of Louis. Not to protect Louis, but because he did not know how she would react to all that attention.

…I’m not sure if that’s the real reason.

Only one thing was certain. There would be no more hiding. And now that he could only rely on the brain of a child, spinning a believable lie wasn’t an option, either.

“She is… Louis is…the Archbishop of Gluttony.”

All he could do was tell the truth.

6

Louis Arneb’s true nature.

Subaru had hidden it ever since being transported to Volakia. He had kept it from Rem after she lost her memory, but also from everyone else he met.

He had been keeping Louis’s identity a secret not because of his personal feelings on the matter, but because he could imagine the sort of trouble that revelation would attract.

That was why he had kept it hidden this whole time…

“…Arch…bishop…”

A faltering voice repeated that word. Subaru had fully expected Al or Abel to be stunned by this revelation. It made sense for them to be wary, to want evidence for his claim, or to fly into a fury at how absurd it sounded. But they were not the first to say something.

“Louis is…an archbishop…?”

It was Medium who uttered those words with wide eyes and a disbelieving voice. She froze in place, staring at Louis. The little girl cocked her head in confusion.

The emotion that flickered through Medium’s eyes was what Subaru had feared most.

He had held on to a faint hope that maybe the O’Connell siblings would laugh it off in their openhearted, accepting way. But he quickly realized that was a pipe dream.

“………”

Medium’s eyes were filled with an unmistakable terror.

“That ain’t a funny joke, Bro.”

“I-it’s not a joke—”

“If it’s not a joke, then that’s even worse!”

Still reeling from Medium’s devastating reaction, Subaru jumped when Al raised his voice and reached for the sword slung across his back. Al had a hard time in his current body holding the sword aloft with a single arm, so the point sank into the ground. But even so, he could still manage to swing it by using his whole body, and his violent intent was clear from the way he looked past Subaru at Louis.

“Walkin’ around with an archbishop of the Witch Cult in tow ain’t the mark of a sane man. Don’t tell me you forgot what happened in Pristella.”

“Th-that’s…”

“Me and Priscilla… The princess didn’t get hurt, but that was pure luck. Meanwhile, you and your people got hit by some bad shit. And she’s one of the people responsible!”

He had no response for Al. After all, he was completely right. No matter how you sliced it, Subaru was in the wrong here. He should not have allowed her to roam free, much less brought her along.

He should have immediately revealed her true identity and put her in chains. But he hadn’t. Instead…

“A-Abel…?”

He turned to Abel, who remained silent. Subaru needed to know what he thought about all this.

Medium was terrified, and Al was furious, so Abel was the last bastion. He did not know which side this bastion would stand for, but he clung to hope all the same.

Because if everyone here turned on Louis…

“………”

…then Subaru would have to quell his hesitation and act.

“I do not know how they are handled in other countries…”
