Subaru gulped as the masked man looked straight at him. Two pairs of black eyes locked. Abel’s cold gaze bore into Subaru’s heart. His mind went numb, like he was rejecting the words that he should have been waiting to hear.

The voice slowly seeped into his brain…

“…In the empire, those who worship the Witch for any reason are executed.”

That was the immutable declaration of this country’s supreme leader, even if he had been driven from his throne. A death sentence that ruled out coexistence.

Subaru clenched his eyes tightly—

“—Louis!!!”

“Subaru?!”

The moment he shouted her name, a small pair of arms reached around his waist. Subaru paid Medium’s shouts no mind as his feet left the ground. Louis had grabbed hold of his waist and leaped high into the air.

Subaru did not know why he had called Louis’s name, what the significance of that was, or why he was struggling to hold back the tears that welled up in his eyes even as he gritted his teeth.

But he did know one thing.

“Uau.”

He could not forsake the little girl clinging to him. Not because she had saved his life and he wanted to return the favor. Not because he had grown fond of her and felt a sudden urge to protect her.

No, it was simply that he knew he’d regret making a final decision about this girl he couldn’t even begin to understand while he was turning back into a child not only in body but also in mind.

It had nothing to do with Rem or any of the many people he had met so far. This was a Subaru problem. A problem that Subaru Natsuki had to face head-on.

“Bro! Get back here! Damn it!”

Al shouted after them, but Louis didn’t slow down. She shifted Subaru onto her back and started bouncing between nearby buildings until she reached the top. Then she took a running start and jumped across to the next rooftop over, and then again to the street past that.

There were footholds all over, creating paths that spiderwebbed across the city—perfect for Louis.

“Gah!”

After dozens of leaps, Subaru was set free. He kneeled with his hands on the ground. All the moments of weightlessness, fighting against gravity, plus Louis’s slender arms locking him in a vise grip…it had been a rough ride. Subaru couldn’t help but find it irritating how she hadn’t even broken a sweat, while he was wheezing.

But he did not have time to get annoyed at her.

“Abel and the others…”

He had brought this on himself, so it didn’t make much sense to regret getting separated. But who knew what sort of order Abel might have given if he had stayed. Al’s reaction made it clear he would not let it go. And Subaru didn’t really think he was capable of smoothing things over with Medium.

Ultimately, he blamed himself for not simply handing Louis over.

“Uau?”

Wiping his mouth with his sleeve, he looked over at Louis and studied her easygoing blue eyes. She was completely oblivious to all the malice and terror directed at her. Seeing that, Subaru felt like a fool for letting his heart get all twisted up.

“What am I, stupid? Yeah, guess I am.”

He really was a fool. Al aside, leaving Medium and Al behind and running away with Louis was a terrible choice.

Especially when I have no idea what she’s thinking or what she might do…

“But I’ll regret it if I decide like this. It’s not something for a kid to decide.”

A person’s life and the fate of the empire were too important to leave to a ten-year-old to decide. And to ask a child that under the gaze of a cold and merciless adult—it’s wrong.

“I’m sure I’ll be able to make a proper choice once I’m back to normal. So…”

I’ve gotta undo this age regression and make a comeback as teenage Subaru Natsuki ASAP.

Once he did, Subaru was confident he’d be able to figure out what to do with Louis and what his comrades were all thinking.

And to do that…

“I have to find Mr. Orbart without them.”

“Aaa, uuu!”

Subaru’s head snapped up, and Louis raised her fists, ready to go.

The two children declared their intent to find the Shinobi chief, while challenging the residents of Chaosflame, as well as the emperor driven from his throne.

Subaru and Louis were now both the seekers in a game of hide-and-seek and it in a massive game of tag.

chapters.title: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29
chapters.text:
Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

CHAPTER 5

STARS ALIGNING

1

“Shit! I can’t see them anywhere…!”

Al looked up from the road, glancing around at all the various elevated walkways, before stamping his foot and shouting.

The outrageous development from moments ago had left him seething with anger.

It was a turn of events that could only be called insane.

“Subaru, Louis…”

Meanwhile, Medium’s reaction was the complete opposite. Her usual cheer and good spirits were nowhere to be seen. She was worried about the two who had left, but there was more than that in her voice. It was not purely concern for their well-being…

“Louis is…”

“To think she was an archbishop.”

Medium’s eyes widened at hearing Abel voice the same thing she was thinking. He, like Al, was peering up at the sky. His expression was unreadable with his mask back on, but it was clear from the way he folded his arms and tapped his finger that he was not exactly pleased about this.

“Abel, they…”

“…We should prioritize resolving the current situation. Our priority has not changed. Unfortunately, we have lost one of our cards.”

It was a curt reply, but even if he hadn’t addressed the matter directly, it was clear he had no intention of attempting to find Subaru and Louis.

That was both concerning and a relief to Medium. She wanted to make sure they were safe, but she was glad she wouldn’t have to face them just yet.

“You’re gonna just let him go? Subaru’s mind is reverting back to a kid’s!”

“Then what would you suggest? His position is not so different from your own. I will tell you now that if you or Medium no longer have any use, I will have no choice but to leave you behind.”

“Gh…”

“Do not presume that you are the only one who decides if we work together, jester.”

Abel coldly rejected his suggestion. Al was struggling to respond, but it was clear that he was mainly concerned with Subaru while Louis was almost an afterthought. If anything, Al regarded her with intense wariness now.

“I can’t leave Bro with that kid…”

Al gnashed his teeth with open hostility. Medium looked like she wanted to say something, but maybe because she could not decide how to feel about Louis, she unexpectedly stayed silent.

“………”

Glancing at them out of the corner of his eye, Abel turned his gaze back up to the air, to the chaotic skyline that had consumed all traces of their passing.

“Fool.”

A single word murmured to no one.

2

In the middle of a situation without precedent, Subaru was forced to leave his comrades.

He had made a snap decision in the heat of the moment, and he hadn’t really thought about what would come next, but Subaru had little doubt it would come back to bite him later. At the same time, he had made that choice because he didn’t want to have any regrets.

Of course, he was already having regrets.

Since…

“Au, uau!”

“Stop it, Louis! He’ll die if you keep going!”

He had her in a full nelson, and she was struggling as he pulled her away from the unconscious man she was strangling.

After separating from the others, they had set out across the pathways running through the city in search of Orbart, who was the cause of the age regression. However, the townspeople of Chaosflame must have had descriptions of Subaru and Louis, who had not been at the palace yesterday, because whenever they encountered them, a fight ensued.

Like Abel had gathered, Orbart and Tanza were most likely working together. If so, it made sense they were sharing information, and that was how word about them had spread among the horned townspeople.

As a result, Subaru and Louis had been attacked three times already since going off on their own. Fortunately, Louis’s prowess in combat let her put down their pursuers quickly. Since Subaru couldn’t fight in his current state, he was grateful, but…

“Auu…”

“Not ‘auu’! They aren’t bad people; they’re just scared! Even if we’re in danger…this isn’t okay!”

Louis’s legs flailed, but she calmed down at Subaru’s warning.

He could not say whether she truly understood, but she did at least seem to get that he was mad.

Subaru took the opportunity to give the unconscious man first aid.

He did not have any medical supplies, though, so Subaru laid him down with his head elevated and wiped away the blood streaming from his nose. Then Subaru moved him to the side of the road.

“They’re just desperate because they want to protect their home.”

“Uau?”

Louis cocked her head. The pursuers they had run into were all different ages and genders and races, but the one thing they had in common was horns. Again, just as Abel predicted.

Subaru could only imagine how much hardship those horns brought into their lives, especially when he thought of Emilia…

“…Thank goodness Rem isn’t here… I think?”

She was a survivor of the oni tribe, and she had the ability to sprout a horn from her forehead. Unlike the beast people, her horn was not always visible, but as a race that also grew horns, it was entirely possible she had also experienced the same prejudices.

I’ve never heard Ram or Rem mention anything like that, though.

“Ram probably wouldn’t care at all what other people said.”

Ram proudly walked her own path in life, and it felt like she would just snort in derision at anyone who commented about her horn. She had the strength and fortitude not to let things like that drag her down.

If it was her, maybe she would be calm even if she knew Louis’s true identity?

“…What am I, stupid? Yeah, I’m stupid.”

Putting his fist to his forehead, Subaru backed away from that pathetic and unfair thought.

Ram was not there. Neither was Emilia, and neither was Beatrice, and neither was anyone else. Rem was the closest, but she was in distant Guaral—this was not the moment to be relying on someone who was not around.

“I need to find an abyss with a view.”

Considering when they were supposed to meet Yoruna, there was no time to waste running around and hiding. They needed to find Orbart while being chased.

“I doubt Abel will try to find us. If we run into Talitta…”

“Au.”

“…No, she’s being chased around a city she doesn’t know, either. We can’t make more trouble for her.”

Putting a hand to his head, he shelved the half-formed plan of seeking help from Talitta, who didn’t know about Louis’s identity yet.

Even if I did find her, I don’t think I can explain why we split up. I would have to lie again, and it would only kick the can down the road.

Plus, if Medium was no good, then Talitta was definitely…

“………”

He would run headfirst into the problem of what to do about Louis again. Subaru still had no answer. He did not want to end up in an argument again and be mad at everyone, and he didn’t want to hate himself even more for not being able to explain everything nicely.

“Uau.”

Louis peered at Subaru, patiently waiting for him to say something.

She was already confusing enough to begin with. Now that she could use her power, Gluttony’s authority, she was even more impossible to understand.

So…

“If you don’t want to die, then stay close to me. I don’t want to let you die. For now, at least.”

“Aa, uu.”

She smiled and nodded casually. It was unclear whether she actually understood or not, which just made Subaru sigh.

“—Hey! Those two over there!”

There was no time to carefully think things over. A pursuer had noticed them and raised the alarm. Subaru immediately leaped onto Louis’s back.

“Louis! Don’t fight! Run, run, run, run!”

“Au! Uuu!”

The moment Subaru climbed onto her back, Louis raced forward. His plan to force her to carry him to keep her out of more fights seemed to be working.

However…

“Don’t let them get away! After them!!!”

The horned people patrolling the city were not going to let them go so easily.

As expected, only people with horns seemed to be chasing after them. There were lots of people without horns in Chaosflame, but none of them were coming after Subaru and Louis.

The deer-girl, Tanza, had most likely organized the hunt, but…

“Apparently, Tanza can only order around people with horns…!”

If every last resident of Chaosflame had turned against them, then there would be absolutely no possibility of evading capture. Tanza was apparently pushing the limits of her authority, but that was already enough to push Subaru’s party to the brink.

“Louis, don’t attack! Just keep running away!”

“Uu?”

“Don’t ask me why! Just find a way! Attacking bad! Bad!”

Louis ran through the walkways lining the town, with Subaru on her back, but she clearly didn’t like being told to run, when she could fight and win. Regardless, Subaru kept yelling and tugging at her cheeks to drive home the point. He had no intention of letting her fight.

There was a decent chance she could win no matter what the odds, but her uncontrollable power might also claim the lives of their pursuers.

If that happened, it would be like unleashing Louis Arneb, which was exactly what Subaru feared most. If Louis even looked like she was turning back into Louis Arneb…

“…That would prove Abel and the others were right.”

That would have made all this running away completely pointless. It put Subaru in a strange position where he was oddly concerned for Louis.

So no fighting.

“I won’t let you kill anyone else.”

So long as Subaru Natsuki’s eyes are black, I can’t let that happen.

“—Au.”

Subaru’s arms tightened their grip around Louis, and she quietly focused on the path forward. She seemed to put her discontent aside and listened to Subaru as she leaped through the city to shake off their tail.

But the pursuers knew the lay of the land and had more numbers, so they were gradually closing in.

I won’t let her fight, but at this rate…

“This way, you two.”

A voice called out to them when they dropped from an elevated walkway into the street.

“Eh?”

Turning around in surprise, they saw a slender-faced young man waving them over. At a glance, he did not seem to have horns, but it was so unexpected, Subaru couldn’t help being wary.

The stranger was pointing to a cart filled with cargo right behind him.

“I recommend hiding here. Now, while there isn’t aaanyone watching.”

“Wh-who are you…?”

“You’re being chased, right? And they seem real serious, right? This is for your own good. I’ll even swear it on the stars,” the man with long ash-colored hair said with a wink.

He had an ingratiating smile and was acting suspiciously, and it was hard to believe an offer like that at face value. But then Subaru heard a loud voice down the street. Their pursuers had caught up.

“What will it be, then? The alignment of the stars changes with every moment. Whether you accept this sign or reject it is entirely up to you. Hooowever, just going along now is the best policy, if you ask me.”

He waved his empty hands with a flourish, smiling to demonstrate he bore them no ill will.

Subaru was really unsure whether to trust that smile, but the man was right that there was not much time to be hesitating.

3

“…Why did you help us?”

“Why, huh? Hmm, hrmmm. About that…ah, well, I couldn’t bear watching a couple children being hunted down. How’s that sound?”

Subaru glared at the man.

“That makes it sound like you just made it up on the spot…”

“So that didn’t fly, huh?”

The young man touched his hair, seeming troubled.

Subaru was not really sure how to feel as he pulled Louis out of the wagon.

In the end, Subaru had accepted the guy’s offer and pushed Louis into the impromptu hiding place. Not so much because he trusted the guy, but because it felt like continuing to run for much longer was going to be rough. Fortunately, the guy had not immediately sold them out and had even lied to their pursuers, sending them farther away.

“Worst case, there was always the option of letting Louis go wild, but…”

“Oooooh? Does that mean I was walking a rather dangerous tightrope there?”

“I’m just relieved it didn’t come to that,” Subaru said gratefully.

Their suspicious savior did not have any visible horns. In fact, he didn’t seem to be a demi-human at all. There were some races that did not have many distinguishing traits, like Ram and Rem, so he couldn’t be sure, but the guy’s clothes and general demeanor did not really fit in Chaosflame.

On top of that, while he had helped Subaru and Louis, what he really wanted was completely unclear.

“Thank you for helping us…but seriously, why? Umm…”

“Ah, my name is Ubirk. I can understand why you would be suspicious, but I don’t reeeally have much I can say, either.”

“What does that mean?”

“I just had the feeling that it might be better to help you two, is all.” Ubirk flashed a carefree smile.

It was a really suspicious answer, but his response, his generally neat appearance, and his clothes made it seem like he had a proper job.

He’s got a wagon full of things, so a merchant, I guess.

“Ah, this wagon’s not mine. It just happened to be here.”

“Eh?! But you told us to hide in it…”

“It’s not like it needs to be my wagon to be a decent hiding spot. It probably belongs to that shop riiiight over there, I guess? If you’re grateful, then you should thank them.” Ubirk unexpectedly pointed to a nearby store. “That one? Or maybe there?” And another and then another right next to it.

Ubirk was essentially claiming he had come across the two of them by chance and managed to help them with what just happened to be lying around.

That makes no sense at all, and I think I’d be scared even if I wasn’t a kid.

“Umm, Ubirk, sir, thank you for helping us. But you should probably think more carefully before you act in the future. I think you might end up getting hurt one day…”

“Ohhh? Are you worried about me? Do I really look that unimpressive? I’m actually pretty good at getting by, I think, but then again, everyone’s got different ideas about what that looks like. Also, is it just me, or are you standing kind of far away?”

“Look, it’s not because I’m suspicious of you. We’re just in a hurry.”

Well, I’m also suspicious.

Not because he thought Ubirk was working with Tanza or Orbart, but simply because he might be a dangerous adult all on his own. Since Subaru and Louis were both currently children, a shady adult was something to worry about. Subaru wasn’t confident he could hold Louis back if he turned out to be a dangerous stranger.

An adult acting weirdly around children is a bit hard to forgive.

“A-anyway, we’ll be leaving now. Come on, that means you.”

Subaru grabbed Louis’s hand, and with a parting thank-you, he started walking away.

But…

“Juuuust a moment, please. What a cold reaction. I’m hurt.”

Ubirk hurried his long, slender legs to stand in front of them. The stranger danger gauge in Subaru’s head was rising, putting Ubirk in a more precarious position. More to the point, his hand’s grip tightened a little, and Louis made a little noise, sensing Subaru’s tension.

As a result, she stepped out in front of Subaru, glaring at Ubirk, who was blocking their way.

“Uuu!”

“Whooooa, not a fan? I always assumed most girls like me, but I guess it’s different when they already have someone in their heart.”

“…Mr. Ubirk, you really shouldn’t make Louis angry. She’s a lot scarier than she looks.”

“Ahhhh, I see. So your name is Louis.”

He nodded to himself as a lump lodged itself in Subaru’s throat.

There probably was no problem with him knowing a name, but it was a problem that Subaru had carelessly handed him information. He did not want to reveal any more to an adult he did not know.

“Sorry, Mr. Ubirk, but we really are in a hurry…”

“I didn’t really plan to go out on a walk today.”

“Huh?”

“But here I am, out and about. That’s just how the stars aligned, so there was no helping it. I just aimlessly started wandering…and there you were.”

Putting his hand to his forehead, he ran his fingers down past his kindly eyes, his pale cheeks, and his sharp jaw, and then snapped his fingers. The gesture grabbed Subaru’s attention and surprised him. He broke down what Ubirk had just said in his head, and then…

“…You mean you went out for a walk and just happened to spot us?”

“Well, that is another way to say it. Buuut, I think you could also say it like this: This was all written in the stars.”

“………”

It was a romantic way to look at things, but Subaru’s shoulders just slumped. There was not much romance in a random encounter between this group of people.

“Are you perchance exasperated with me?”

“Umm, that’s fine. It doesn’t matter what people you’ll never meet again think of you.”

“Ugh, that stings. Reminds me of an old friend.”

“You have a friend…?”

“Ah-ha-ha, I did.”

Subaru’s reflexive response was pretty rude, but Ubirk didn’t seem to mind. For a moment, he did seem a little sad. He had an easygoing, unserious sort of air, but he was obviously more complicated underneath.

“Anyway, there is a fate of sorts in us meeting here like this. Ahh, right! My job happens to be giving people advice. What do you say? Anything you’d like to talk about?”

“There it is! I’ve seen this trick on TV! No thank you!”

“Ah-ha-ha, I’m not a con man. I reeeally just want to fulfill my role.”

“Role…?”

“Right, my role. Since fortune brought us together here…I imagine it’s so I can lend an ear to you and Ms. Louis there.”

He was twirling his hair around his finger while nodding.

Unfortunately, even if Ubirk truly did feel that way, Subaru did not find his words very convincing. All that did was raise his stranger danger rating.

The sooner we get away, the better.

“Ah, there’s no point in trying to run away. Iiiif you try, I’ll shout until people come over.”

In exchange for a big jump in his danger rating, Ubirk managed to stop them in their tracks.

Even if he was suspicious and annoyingly persistent, I didn’t want to think he was a bad guy.

“Mr. Ubirk, I think it’s better if you don’t get too involved with us. You might get caught up in our troubles, and I think it would be too much for you to handle.”

“Ahh, you don’t have to worry about me. I don’t ask for personal information when chatting with people.”

“What kind of advice do you even give then?!”

“Just give it a try and see. Here, please just look into my eyes.”

Ignoring Subaru’s concerns, Ubirk crouched down and looked right at him, pointing at his own eyes. Sighing, Subaru gave in and did as he was asked.

Ubirk’s brown eyes were unusually clear, and he could imagine lots of women falling for them in combination with his sweet facade.

If the situation were different and we’d talked more, I…

“The answer you are searching for is already within you.”

“Eh?”

“That’s my advice…or call it my counsel. You can also think of it as the result I got.”

Ubirk cocked his head with a gentle smile. “So what do you think?”

Sorry, but that didn’t really shine a light on anything for me. And the phrasing is so vague.

“I feel like keeping things generic enough to apply to basically anyone is a standard con man’s trick…”

“I don’t think it is such a grand crossroads in life sort of thing. It’s probably something a bit more immediate… Maybe something to do with you being chased just now?”

“But I know why they were chasing us already…”

The young man seemed supremely confident while clinging to a classic con man’s explanation. But as Subaru gave it a little more thought, something clicked.

It was just the smallest thing, but it felt incredibly important.

“An abyss with a view.”

Ubirk was saying that the answer to their immediate problem was inside Subaru.

Subaru did not want to fall for whatever Ubirk was trying to pull, but he couldn’t deny that he did feel something. Focusing on that new wrinkle, he sensed that he was on the cusp of a major breakthrough.

“That counseling may actually have been useful.”

“Uau!”

Subaru’s eyes changed as he latched on to that feeling, and Louis cried excitedly. Ubirk nodded in satisfaction.

“Good, good. I’m glad I was of some use. It would be a shame to not help out when I’m already here. So, what now?”

“We’re gonna get going. Thanks for a bunch of things, Mr. Ubirk. Come on, Louis.”

“Auau!”

Ubirk closed an eye as Subaru took Louis’s hand and started running. Then the young boy stopped and whipped around, Louis still in tow. Ubirk’s eyes widened.

Waving to him, Subaru cried, “Mr. Ubirk, you should stop conning people and go back home! You’ll be happier that way!”

That was Subaru’s advice for Ubirk, imbued with his gratitude for the help.

With that, he watched the boy and girl hurry off.

“Stop conning people, huh? That’s quiiite harsh.”

Ubirk smiled wryly and pulled his hood up to cover his long hair. It had been quite the odd encounter, but from the boy’s demeanor, his advice had been helpful. With that load off his chest, he could breathe a sigh of relief.

“If I go back now, Kafma will still be upset. Perhaps I should keep wandering. Then again, the city’s mood is a bit dangerous. Still…”

He glanced in the direction the two of them ran and closed an eye.

His gaze drifted to the Crimson Lazuli Palace rising from the center of the Demon City.

“Even as a stargazer, sometimes I do have to wonder what it is the stars wish for.”

4

“The answer is inside me.”

“Au.”

After leaving Ubirk and winding through various alleys, they stopped.

Louis stared at Subaru as he reflected on Ubirk’s insistent advice. Meeting her eyes, Subaru exhaled deeply.

“‘Behind our eyelids’ was a riddle, so ‘an abyss with a view’ should be a riddle, too… It’s not about finding a real abyss. We should be looking for something like an abyss.”

“Uuu?”

Louis twisted her head, looking completely lost.

That was understandable. Subaru found most of what Ubirk had said super confusing as well. It was very fishy how he said it was his job to give people advice, and his advice was vague and hard to act on, but it had helped point him in the right direction.

I doubt he ever had the answer I wanted, but…

“I don’t know anything about this city, but that should be true for Orbart, too. He didn’t seem to get along with Yoruna too well, either…”

The old man was primarily here as a guard for the fake emperor. That would make it difficult for him to move around freely. With limited knowledge of the locale, would he really choose a challenge that involved notable locations in the city? Subaru definitely wouldn’t, so…

“An abyss with a view? And a place that isn’t unique to Chaosflame…”

And Ubirk said that the answer was in Subaru.

When he took that advice seriously, one thought struck like lightning. It was the feeling he had just experienced—a memory of falling into an abyss.

“On the street before, when that boy threw me…”

When Subaru snapped and rushed out into the street, the sheep-boy had sent him flying. It had been so intense, he went spinning high up into the air.

It felt like I was falling into the big, blue sky.

Of course that wasn’t what actually happened. Anyone around him could have attested that Subaru had flown up into the air. It had looked like the exact opposite of falling, but to him, it was different. The sky had felt like a massive bottomless blue hole that he was plummeting into.

So…

“Aau!”

It was unclear whether she understood what Subaru was thinking, but Louis broke into a smile and pointed while swinging her other hand. Subaru nodded at where she was pointing. That was their target—the place closest to that abyss in the city: Yoruna Mishigure’s palace, the Crimson Lazuli Palace at the heart of Chaosflame.

“Uu!”

Subaru cursed Orbart’s nasty personality. Given everything about the situation, even if they went to the palace, odds were high they would be turned back at the gate, and that was due to none other than Orbart and his age regression.

“A place we can’t easily get to even if we figure out the answer…that’s just the sort of thing he would do.”

The whole point of this match was to undo the transformation to go to the palace to talk to Yoruna, and Orbart knew that. That was exactly why he did it. What a vicious old man indeed.

Problem is…

“…How do we get into the palace?”

Even though he knew where Orbart was, he could not think of a way to reach him. If Subaru claimed to be the messenger from yesterday, no one would believe him, and while telling Yoruna about Tanza’s plan was an option, it was a risky one. Some kid rolling in out of nowhere and bad-mouthing her attendant was just too suspicious.

“If we can’t walk in through the front door, then the only option we’ve got is sneaking in…”

As much as he tried, that was the best idea he could come up with. But there would be guards patrolling the palace, so it wouldn’t be so easy.

—If Subaru was alone, that is.

“Louis, there’s one thing I’d like your help with.”

“Au?”

Louis blinked several times as Subaru looked at her. For a moment, he felt his chest ache when he saw how innocent she looked, but he brushed it aside by telling himself this had to be done.

“That warp you used…you moved me with it before, right?”

5

Pointing in a direction and holding Louis’s hand tightly.

That was Subaru’s signal that Louis should use her warp. It sounded almost like teaching a puppy a trick, but it was not nearly as cute. If only Louis was a puppy, there would be no need to be so on edge about her seriously hurting someone.

If I’m going to rely on her powers, I have to be extra careful.

But…

“We’re in!”

The surroundings suddenly changed. They had teleported inside the building without a hitch.

Seeing the hallway with its wooden plank floor and an interior befitting a Japanese castle, Subaru knew right away they had succeeded.

“Good work, Louis. We got past the outer stone wall and the inner wall of the palace itself. I don’t think anyone noticed.”

“Uu!”

Louis’s chest swelled with pride.

He did not want it to go to her head, but thanks to her, they didn’t have to endure an interrogation at the gate, nor did they have to fight their way inside.

They had successfully infiltrated the Crimson Lazuli Palace that stood at the heart of the Demon City.

Subaru had hesitated at first, but once he decided to do it, things moved quickly.

Figuring out that the nature of Louis’s warp let her move approximately ten yards, together with whomever she was touching, he devised a plan to enter the palace.

There was no time, so it was nothing especially complex…

“Well, the whole plan is basically just using Louis’s warp. But…urgh.”

“Uau.”

The world twisted as Subaru leaned against the wall and put a hand to his mouth. The nausea was a side effect of the warp messing with his insides. There was no avoiding it. He simply had to deal with it every time they warped.

Louis seemed fine, but it made Subaru feel bad enough that he preferred to take a break after each jump. They had double warped to get into the palace, and that was enough to leave him incredibly woozy.

“It’d be one thing if it just makes me hurl, but if I pass out…”

“Uu?”

Louis peered blankly at Subaru as he fought back the nausea.

If there was some accident and Subaru lost consciousness mid-warp, there would be no one holding Louis’s reins and no one left who could stop her.

I won’t let her kill anyone else.

That was the vow Subaru made when he ran away with her. The child, Subaru Natsuki, could not figure out how he should handle Louis, so he at least wanted to keep that promise.

“…I guess it would be hard to use verandas to jump higher while taking breaks.”

Orbart was most likely at the top of the palace keep that was closest to the sky, so they needed to climb without drawing attention, as hard as that would almost certainly be.

If a guard or a random passerby in the city notices us and raises the alarm…

“The worst possibility would be Yoruna finding us.”

In getting here, they had fought pursuers who carried a portion of her strength because of the soul marriage. It granted the townsfolk immense power, but they were amateurs when it came to fighting, so they were no match for Louis. But Yoruna’s real strength was surely on a different level.

If we wind up in a fight with her, that’ll ruin everything. We won’t recruit any allies, we won’t fix our bodies, and I won’t be able to face Rem.

“So let’s do this really, really carefully.”

Calming down, he put a finger to his lips, gesturing for Louis to be quiet as they carefully looked for stairs to go up, hand in hand.

From his time in the palace yesterday, it seemed like there were hardly any guards around. The guests who had come were just left sitting in the waiting room, so it would make sense there were hardly any guards when they weren’t expecting anyone.

It seems too lax for an important person’s palace, but…

“…There really isn’t anyone around.”

Peering around a corner, Subaru felt oddly worried by the lack of security. There was no sign of anyone in the long hallway, and it felt silly that they were being so cautious about their footsteps. But there were hardly any places to hide, so if they did run into someone, they would have to immediately warp through a wall.

“If it comes to it, maybe it would be better to go straight up. That might be faster than looking for stairs.”

“Aau?”

“Yeah, I think it’s safe to assume an important person’s rooms gotta be higher up. Plus, it’s scary to hang around here for too long, right? There are people in this world who can detect the presence of others, just like in a manga.”

Subaru still didn’t really understand how, but it was apparently a standard ability for anyone sufficiently powerful. This world was inhabited by incredibly skilled people who could detect intruders without obvious signs like audible footsteps or breathing.

If Yoruna was one of those people, then she would find them even if they used Louis’s warp, and if she found them, she would definitely treat them as enemies.

Our only choice is…

“We have to be equal parts careful and bold. If we’re found…”

“—If you are found, what will you do?”

Subaru twitched. A bloodcurdling voice had rung out right behind them.

Louis felt his tension through their locked hands, and opening her eyes wide, she turned around together with Subaru.

“Two little ones holding hands. It is quite adorable. Even I cannot help but smile.”

Yoruna Mishigure, the beautiful master of this palace, the one person they most needed to avoid, was standing right there.

“—Ah.”

There was no one there.

Subaru and Louis should have been the only people in the hallway. He had checked. And yet Subaru’s caution and careful preparation were useless against her.

Yoruna Mishigure was evidently one of the superhumans in this world.

“Neither a familiar face, though.”

She puffed on the pipe in her hand as she peered into their faces.

She was a beautiful and bewitching woman in a dazzling kimono, just as impressive as the first time he saw her the day before. Her long braided hair was a lovely blend of orange and white, with sharp little fox ears peeking out.

She was a blindingly gorgeous woman, yes, but she also exuded an overwhelming presence that had nothing to do with her beauty. Not just because she was a tall woman and Subaru was shrunken down to the size of a young child. There was something different about her. She possessed the uncanny ability to push and pull others.

“You need not be afraid. What business brings you to my palace?”

“Uu…”

Yoruna’s hair ornaments swayed with a silvery tinkle as Subaru cursed himself.

He had been so careful while sneaking around, but he had not prepared an excuse in case they were discovered.

Careless. There’s no other word for it.

And sure enough, at seeing Subaru struggling to respond, Yoruna’s eyes narrowed.

She’s suspicious. Even though I have to say something, I’m so nervous, I can’t think of anything to—

“Is it Tanza?”

“Eh…?”

“The reason why you have come here to the palace.”

Subaru’s blood froze, and he could swear he heard something shatter as she saw through everything.

Just a glance, and she knew why we are here, and probably who we are. I can already hear Abel calling me a fool. Honestly, I’d call myself worse right about now.

The world seemed to grow dark, and he could almost feel the ground crumbling beneath him, as if he was falling…

“Uau.”

But he was pulled back by the hand squeezing his. Looking to his side, he saw Louis peering into his eyes. Her blue eyes were wavering slightly, talking to him. Telling him she could fly at any moment.

“………”

Seeing her earnest gaze, Subaru just barely managed to get ahold of himself. Looking up, Yoruna was waiting quietly for a response to her question, not trying to hurry Subaru at all.

It’s too soon to give up.

She was asking if Tanza was why they were in the palace. That was right, but only partially right. So he gambled on that other part.

“Umm, Miss Yoruna… I mean, Lady Yoruna.”

“What is it?”

“Is Tanza in the palace?”

Making up his mind, he asked the question. Yoruna’s eyes narrowed. It was not even a second, but Subaru experienced what a rat caught by a fox probably felt.

Though that’s probably too generous a comparison. For us.

For a few seconds that seemed like an eternity, he waited…

“Unfortunately, Tanza is out on an errand. Though she should be returning any moment now…”

“…!”

Subaru clenched Louis’s hand at hearing that, clenched it hard enough that she started looking around to see where he was pointing.

He was apologetic, but that was not a signal; it was him celebrating. He had won his gamble.

Yoruna’s question was not because she realized their identity or their reason for being here.

“Dear me, Tanza is a troublesome one. I appreciate her devotion, but I cannot have her work as an attendant if she forgets her promises to her friends.”

“F-friends…?”

“She is an upright and honest girl, yes? Yet I am always telling her that it is not enough for that commendable devotion to be dedicated solely toward me.”

The way she said that made it seem like she really did believe they were Tanza’s friends.

It did not really befit the scary, mischievous, and immeasurable nature of the master of this Demon City that he had seen yesterday, though. It was like a kindly adult showing concern for a familiar child.

As if hammering that impression home, Yoruna exhaled slightly.

“While it is a result of Tanza’s carelessness, it would be unacceptable to send you away… Come, I will show you in.”

“Eh…?! Y-you will, Lady Yoruna?!”

“Au?”

Turning elegantly, she walked with a splendid, careful step that did not make a sound, even with how thick the soles of her shoes were. Subaru was almost taken in just by the sight, and he was taken aback at his slow reaction to her offer.

Yoruna hid her smile behind her sleeve.

“This is my palace. It is of course my role to provide hospitality. With Tanza out, I shall also keep you company.”

“Ah, umm…”

“This is the first time a friend of hers has come here. Now, please follow me.” Yoruna gestured with her chin.

Subaru was deeply unsure of what to do. He did not need to waste any time worrying about the possibility of a trap, since there was no reason for her to set out a trap for them. She only needed a finger to deal with Subaru, and maybe a couple more to handle Louis.

That meant it was an offer made in good faith.

But then what about how she seemed yesterday…?

“Uau.”

Louis pulled at Subaru’s hand as he struggled with doubts. Looking, he saw her pointing at Yoruna, seemingly telling him to follow. That was the last little push needed to get Subaru’s legs moving.

“………”

Shaking his head, he and Louis walked quickly to catch up to Yoruna. Waiting for that, she smiled and started walking again with a stride to match theirs.

And just like that, they began the odd experience of being shown through the Crimson Lazuli Palace by Yoruna herself.

“Are you children from elsewhere?”

“Y-you can tell?”

“Because you are unfamiliar faces, and you have not received my letter of love.”

She had said that before. That they were unfamiliar faces. And the love letter she mentioned did not ring a bell for Subaru, either, so rather than telling a bad lie, he simply nodded.

“Y-yes, Lady Yoruna. We came from outside the city…with, um, a scary adult.”

“A scary adult, you say? It sounds as if you’ve had it quite hard. Why were you with a scary adult?”

“We just sort of ended up together, I guess…”

He was cautious of her questions while sticking as close to the truth as he could.

It was to a large degree happenstance that he was working together with a scary adult: Abel.

Though I guess that should be past tense now.

It was hard to say if Abel would forgive him for running away with Louis.

And also…

“Can I even forgive myself…?”

I don’t think they have any right to blame me. I was wrong to hide her identity. But this is what happened when I didn’t hide it, so I was right to hide it. If anything, the only thing I should apologize for is not holding on to the secret longer and letting it slip now.

“…It seems you have a complicated relationship with that adult.”

“Eh?”

“A child should not wear such a grave expression… Shall I give that scary adult a punishment?”

Yoruna’s raised sleeve swayed gently as she offered her services.

“A punishment… Eh? You, Lady Yoruna?”

“Despite how it may look, I am actually quite strong,” she said with a chuckle.

Imagining Abel receiving the punishment, Subaru shook his head forcefully.

“Thank you for worrying about me, but it’s okay! I’m sure it would be better to just talk it through…”

“Is that so? If it is someone who can be reasoned with, then that is certainly for the best. In this world, there are all sorts who cannot be reasoned with, though.”

“…Lady Yoruna.”

“Hmm?”

He hesitated for a moment, unsure whether to say it, which caused Yoruna to stop.

Shrunken down like this, my decisiveness and mental capacity are worse, but the biggest problem is this lack of control, this feeling like I can’t stop myself. It was the same when I ran off with Louis. And sneaking into the palace without enough preparation. I just acted without thinking.

I was worried about saying it earlier, but…

“Umm, I’m surprised you listened to me. I just assumed that all important people are scary…”

He was fully aware it was a rude thing to say, and he could not bring himself to look her in the eyes as he finished, but her reaction was just a thoughtful sound before she spoke again.

“You do not appear to be demi-humans.”

“Umm, yes, that’s right.”

“From your eyes, how does this city appear to you?”

“This city…?”

It was a sudden question. Subaru looked out the small window in the hallway. It was rather high up in the wall, so with his current height, he could not look outside very well. But he could see a blue sky, and he knew the city lay just out of sight.

“It’s an amazing, bustling city. And it’s home to lots of different kinds of people.”

Carefully choosing his words, he tried to give as honest an answer as he could. He had the impression of a bustling and lively town from the very start. It looked that way, too, with how built up it was and with how everything connected and intermingled, and there was an incredible number of different races all living together there.

It was a city that left an impact on the eyes and ears.

“You are an honest child. But your words are a comfort to my ears.”

Yoruna’s lips broke into a faint smile. And then she looked out the window, at what was surely a different scene than what Subaru saw.

“This city is a gathering place for those who struggle to live elsewhere. Children who were treated as insignificant and had no place to go… Children who would not be noticed even if they called out and raised their voices.”

“Even if they…”

“If I did not lend an ear to those children in this final place they’ve found, then who else would?”

She puffed at the pipe as a warm light filled her eyes. When he realized it was affection, Subaru felt truly ashamed of himself.

“She is a deeply affectionate person. She loves her allies and loathes her enemies—A lover of all who live in the Demon City.”

That was how Tanza had described Yoruna yesterday. At the time, Subaru did not really understand what she meant. When he heard about the soul marriage from Abel, he had assumed it only referred to her power.

But this is probably what Tanza really meant.

It showed exactly what Yoruna Mishigure valued most of all.

“I’m sorry, Miss Yoruna… I thought you were a scary person…”

He acted without thinking again and said what he was truly thinking. Yoruna exhaled a stream of purple smoke with a smile when she heard that.

“There is no need to apologize. The reason important people seem scary is because they are also scared they may not seem scary enough. It is easier to be feared.”

“Important people want to be feared…?”

Huh. It feels like that’s something I should really remember.

It also felt like that was something that applied to Yoruna, too.

“You need not worry. I am not so pathetic as to be angered by a child over something so trivial. I just so happen to be in a good mood.”

“Au?”

“Yes, that is right. I just received a sign that a thing which I have long desired may at last be in reach.”

She looked pleased as she swung her sleeve again.

There was no sign of anger in her response. It was probably like she said; she was in a good mood, and she was not the sort to be immature in dealing with a child.

The letter Abel sent her is probably the reason why she is in a good mood…

“…”

Thinking that, Subaru this time held it in and carefully worried about what to do.

Whether the letter Yoruna interpreted as a step in the right direction would have its intended effect depended on Abel and the messengers safely reaching the Crimson Lazuli Palace. But it was none other than Yoruna’s attendant Tanza who was getting in the way.

It’s clear from before that she cares about Tanza. What side would Yoruna take if her wishes and Tanza’s clashed?

Yoruna, who had rebelled against the emperor before for the sake of a single person.

What will she do if she finds out the real situation…?

“…You have quite the grave expression again.”

Yoruna tapped her own brow, pointing out Subaru’s anguish. Drawn by her gesture, Louis tapped her forehead, too.

Looking at them, Subaru sighed slightly.

This might be getting ahead of myself, too. But I don’t have the brains to figure out if it’s right or wrong…

“Umm, there’s something I’d like to ask you, Miss Yoruna…”

6

A man sat atop the blue and red tiles lining the roof of the Crimson Lazuli Palace’s keep.

Taking in the special clear breeze that such high places enjoyed, he put his lips to a gourd he pulled from his cloak and wet his dry throat with liquor while looking out at the scene below.

“Kah-ha-ha-ha. It’s a grand view.”

The old man laughed while looking out at the various styles all mixing and melding, creating an intricate and fascinating cityscape. His hoarse laughter danced in the breeze, fading into nothingness. The way it seemed to be swallowed up in the hustle and bustle of the Demon City delighted the old man.

He loved chaotic things. A chaotic cityscape, the melting pot of all different races, the various motives and intentions going hither and thither. The confusion of it all just made him want to encourage it somehow.

“It’s a bad habit of old men to mix all their food up together to eat. But…”

Tilting the gourd up and then wiping the liquor that spilled out with his sleeve, he shrugged. Still sitting cross-legged, he spun on his butt and cocked an eyebrow.

It was quite the mouthwatering scene for an old man who loved chaos.

“Now, that’s a group I didn’t expect to see here.”

Three figures stepped out onto the tiles right in front of him.

“I found you, Mr. Orbart!”

A boy who pointed straight at Orbart, a blond-haired girl holding his hand, and standing behind them like their guardian, the ruler of the Demon City.

Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

CHAPTER 6

AN UNYIELDING LOVE

1

He could feel the ticklish warm, sunny breeze gently tousling his hair, Louis’s hand in his, and the firm presence of the tall woman behind him.

He stood at the summit of the Crimson Lazuli Palace, atop the broad room that sat at its highest floor, on the tiles of the palace’s roof, at the place closest to the sky from which they could see all of Chaosflame.

This was the closest place to the abyss Subaru could think of.

“You’re really mean, Mr. Orbart.”

With his free hand, Subaru pointed at the old man drinking from a gourd, sitting on the roof of the palace.

There was a glugging sound as he drank the liquor in the gourd.

“Are you hungry, kiddo?”

“…H-hungry?”

“Aye, that’s right. You’ve been all aflutter since right after waking up. Didn’t have time to eat anything, did you? The condition of your stomach is what determines the condition of your head and your body, after all.”

Setting the gourd down, Orbart pulled another object out of his cloak. Subaru was a little wary as the old man unwrapped it and revealed a dark round thing the size of a golf ball.

“A ration ball. They’re crucial for us shinobi. Just one of these’ll tide you over for a day, keeping your head and body moving smooth. But it tastes terrible, this here ball.”

“It’s bad…”

“That’s right. It’ll make your eyes pop out. But I’ve been a shinobi a long time. I’ve got a long history with these here balls… Every time I ate one out on a job, I would think to myself, ‘When are those old men in the village gonna retire already, so I don’t have to eat this anymore?’”

As he looked at the ball in his hand, Orbart’s lips curled.

It looked like an emergency ration that had been made with no thought given to taste, so Orbart was probably telling the truth.

“But then why not do that? You’re the leader of the shinobi village, right? You’re important, aren’t you?”

“That’s right. I’m stronger and bigger than any of those old-timers who pushed me around… But for some reason, I still eat these.”

Orbart plopped the ration into his mouth, and even though he said how horrible it was, he bit down on it and swallowed, and then he opened his mouth to show he actually ate it.

“In the end, I couldn’t break the habit. This little ball with everything mashed up together without any concern for flavor or appearance is my favorite food. Funny, ain’t it? Kah-ha-ha-ha!”

Orbart’s teeth clicked together as he laughed. Something about his reaction was uncanny.

Subaru did not know what Orbart was trying to say with that story, but he felt like that was not just because of his immaturity. But I don’t think I should just ignore it, either.

It felt like it was some sort of praise or compliment from Orbart.

“Old Man Orbart, this is my palace.”

Once their conversation was finished, the master of the Demon City, Yoruna Mishigure, spoke up.

Meeting her blue eyes, Orbart stopped smiling.

“Of course. I know that well. It feels pretty good to sit my ass down without the owner knowing, too. The secret to a long life is doing things you love.”

“That is an odd thing to say for one who wishes to live long enough to reach an even older age.”

“Oh, you think that’s odd?”

“Is it not foolish for the secret to a long life to shorten your life?”

Putting her sleeve to her mouth, Yoruna smiled bewitchingly, taunting Orbart.

The air crackled as two Divine Generals stared each other down. Orbart just pulled out another ration ball and plopped it into his mouth.

“Well now, seems like you’re awfully angry, but does me having lunch with a great view really bother you so much? That’s not very nice.”

“As it happens, unlike you, I am not the sort to act boorishly over such a trivial matter. However, I have heard that you misled children and deceived my retainer, and as such, there are certain things I must do as the master of this city.”

“Ho-ho-hoo.”

Orbart’s eyes narrowed, and he whistled as Yoruna stared him down. He chewed the ration in his mouth and then turned his heavy brow and eyes to Subaru and Louis.

Guessing the meaning, Subaru gave a big nod.

“Sorry, but I told on you. This isn’t really against the rules you set. And you were the one who had us attacked.”

“Kah-ha-ha! Look at the balls on you, kiddo. But you’re right. I started it, so I won’t grumble, but…”

“…?”

“Your head’s having trouble keeping up with things, isn’t it? Good job figuring all that out. You wouldn’t happen to be a member of the Volakian royal family, would you? You’ve got a nasty personality just like them.”

“Please don’t say something so scary…”

Just on hair color alone, Subaru did have the same sort of black hair as the current emperor Abel, but there were too many differences aside from that. His face, the length of his legs, and…

“I know how to say thank you when someone does something for me.”

“And with a smile and in a loud voice. Just as a child should be. I would like Tanza to learn that from you. Nonetheless…”

Yoruna smiled and complimented Subaru’s mischievous answer, but then her voice settled to a lower register. The air chilled along with that, indicating this was the end of the preliminary discussion.

For no other reason than…

“I cannot chide my admirable retainer when she isn’t even present. Now then, where have you hidden her, Old Man Orbart?”

Yoruna’s question was the main reason she was here.

After stumbling into Yoruna the moment they entered the palace and learning a bit more about her personality, Subaru decided to take a big gamble.

He told Yoruna everything he could, including the general situation, and about the game of hide-and-seek unfolding across Chaosflame. Of course he kept Abel’s identity secret, and that several members of their party had been turned into children by Orbart. He mainly focused on how he and Louis were related to the messengers from yesterday and that they were currently chasing after Orbart in a game of hide-and-seek—and that Tanza was involved.

He pleaded his case as earnestly as he could and tried to the best of his ability to keep things as grounded as he could to resolve her suspicions. Hearing him out after he made up his mind, Yoruna thought for a few moments…

I am not the sort of woman who would fail to discern the truth in an earnest child’s plea.

And she agreed to accompany Subaru and Louis to the roof of the palace.

“Honestly, I didn’t think she was the sort of person who could be reasoned with like this…”

“Auau.”

“Yeah, I know.”

Louis pouted and swung her hand that was holding his. She was warning him not to let his guard down, and he nodded.

The reason they were able to reach this roof was thanks to multiple converging coincidences.

Separating from Abel and his wily tricks; figuring out the riddle, thanks to Ubirk’s advice; and being found directly by Yoruna, rather than by a guard, because he had come with Louis instead of Al or Medium.

And Subaru had gambled big even though he was the one who had changed the most from the age regression. The biggest reason Yoruna had listened was because he had been honest, and she interpreted that as the earnest plea of a child.

There were adults who would laugh off a child and not take them seriously, but there were also adults who took children at their word and answered earnestly.

I never would have thought one of the Nine Divine Generals standing atop the empire would be one, though.

“Someone said that she was mad…”

Logically, anyone who lived by Volakia’s dog-eat-dog philosophy could not condone her behavior.

But it sounded absurd to Subaru after she had been so kind to him. He was determined to correct the misunderstanding for Zikr whenever he got back to Guaral.

While he was deciding that, though, Yoruna had raised two fingers.

“I have two demands.”

“Demands, eh? Well, might as well say them.”

“First of all, return Tanza to me.”

“Hey now, sounds like you just can’t bear to let your kids go. As it happens, that girl’s got a mind of her own. If she didn’t, she wouldn’t go planning something while keeping it secret from—”

“Silence.”

Orbart was laughing as he practically admitted to conspiring with Tanza, but Yoruna interrupted him with a single sharp word. It was quiet but impactful, brimming with a power that seemed liable to change the very color of the sky. Slapping down Orbart’s snarky reply, Yoruna brought the pipe to her lips and slowly filled her lungs with smoke.

“As it happens, I will not hear Tanza’s appeal or explanation from any lips save her own. I especially will not have them twisted by a vicious old man’s tongue.”

“Kah-ha-ha, you really don’t like me.”

“I’m sure you can think of sufficient reasons why that might be.”

Yoruna cocked her head, the hair ornaments jingling as she flashed an aggressive smile. Her luxuriously braided hair and the ornamental hairpin sticking out, and even her adorned visage, were all her weapons.

Important people want to be feared.

It was Yoruna who taught Subaru that. And he started to wonder if it was not just fear. Maybe beauty was the same.

“Well, I heard the first demand. The next up is the second one.”

“But of course. Put an end to the game with these children.”

“Game, huh? You know, it may look like a game, but this is a serious match.”

“I made myself clear in His Highness’s presence yesterday, did I not? Messengers are not to be meddled with. Even His Highness will respect that.”

Ironically, that very message had been conveyed by Tanza as well.

In that light, Orbart’s actions looked like a difficult to accept betrayal. Yoruna showed no interest in any excuses about how he had not directly raised a hand.

Subaru’s heart was racing, caught somewhere between freezing over and emotions boiling over. Yoruna maintained a polite and welcoming tone, and her expression was as gentle as ever.

But she’s mad. I know that much. I’ve seen a lot of seriously mad people.

People who were seriously mad would feed their very life force into their fiery emotions. It was something you could feel on your skin just by being near them. That was the power of pure anger.

“Uuu…”

Louis groaned slightly at the dangerous mood hanging in the air. Even Louis dared not do anything reckless when Yoruna and Orbart were facing off against each other. They were nothing like the pursuers they had run into along the way here, and her animal instincts screamed that loud and clear.

Or maybe she was just concerned about Subaru getting caught up in the fighting…

“Ngh, Mr. Orbart!”

Shaking his head, Subaru shouted Orbart’s name. The mood in the air was crackling with tension, ready to erupt. Orbart dexterously moved just one eye to look at Subaru.

Once he had his attention, Subaru bit his lip and opened his mouth.

“L-let’s just call it a draw.”

“…Eh?”

Orbart’s left eye, and just his left eye, widened at that offer.

“Well…! It is a draw!” Subaru shouted impatiently. “You tried to do something that kinda sorta went against the spirit of the rules, and I told on you to Miss Yoruna. We both went over the line, so…”

“So we just apologize and call it there, huh?”

“Y-yeah, that’s right! That’s not so bad, is it? We can talk about what you wanted to know, and our problem can be resolved, too!”

What Orbart wanted to know was some secret of the emperor’s that Abel knew. Subaru did not know much about it, but Orbart would be more willing to accept that if he got something out of it. The whole point of the hide-and-seek was a test of intelligence and skill to see if their information could be trusted anyway.

“We found you twice, and not the three times we set, but…you can give us that, right? We worked hard to get all the way up to the top of this palace, so we deserve some praise!”

“Kah-ha-ha, ‘praise me,’ eh? You’re an honest kiddo. Out of curiosity, were you the one who figured out my hiding place here? Or was it that demon-masked youngster?”

“M-mhm, I did. I just happened to think of it… There was one other possibility, too.”

And Abel and them might just be going there.

Either way, sooner or later, they would come to the palace. Subaru had just gotten a head start because of Louis’s warp and Ubirk’s advice.

But if he could earn some credit here, it might make it easier for him to convince Abel and the others. And if it was still hard, he could maybe try to get Yoruna on his side.

Though there’s no telling how she would move if she knew Louis’s identity.

“Anyway! What do you say, Mr. Orbart? Will you take my…our offer?”

Brushing aside those negative thoughts, Subaru pleaded with Orbart.

He called it “our offer” because he was going to need Yoruna’s help smoothing this out. If she decided she could not forgive Orbart for involving Tanza in his scheme, then Subaru’s desperate plan would collapse.

But…

“………”

Closing an eye, pipe at her lips, Yoruna did not object. It seemed like she was willing to respect Subaru’s thoughts.

I’m so, so grateful. I seriously appreciate it.

He did not want to waste the trust or kindness or whatever it was that Yoruna had placed in him.

“Mr. Orbart.”

He called out again, expecting a compromise. Meeting his hopeful gaze, Orbart hooked a finger into his gourd and raised it to his lips, drinking the last drop.

“Hey, kiddo. I don’t have a clue if this is only how you think now as a child, or if that’s how your brain always worked, but…”

“………”

“Unfortunately, I don’t like dropping a match once I’ve started. Old men are stubborn, you know?”

Smirking unpleasantly, the old codger crushed the gourd in his hand, shattering it. The fragments flew through the air as Subaru gasped.

The next moment…

“You obstinate old man. You will regret refusing this child’s hand.”

Yoruna leaped, swinging her long leg down and splitting the palace’s keep in two with a thunderous crack.

2

She raised her thick-soled sandal high into the air and slammed it straight down.

In a flash, the palace keep split apart from the impact. It shattered and exploded with a loud crash, like a bomb had landed.

Loose tiles flew through the air, and a dense smoke rose as Yoruna stood gallantly at the heart of the explosion, kimono rustling in the air.

In a single breath, she had leaped and annihilated the palace keep with her awesome destructive power. The palace keep was split clean in two, marring the beautiful exterior of the Crimson Lazuli Palace.

“Whooooaaaa?!”

Subaru shouted as he was pulled away by Louis leaping out of the smoke. Rolling across the roof, he just managed to avoid getting caught in the destruction.

But…

“Damn it! Why’d it have to turn out like this…?!”

Pulled up by Louis, Subaru tearfully bemoaned this result.

Stubborn old Orbart refused my offer, so it turned into a fight even though I didn’t wanna fight and didn’t want to make anyone else fight either.

“Miss Yoruna!”

“You should stay back. I cannot easily restrain myself. And also…”

Yoruna did not look back as she drew her foot out of the roof and then brushed away the rubble from the hem of her kimono and then turned her eyes overhead.

“As expected, you are quite spry.”

In the rubble, smoke, and tile fragments, a small shadow spun in place—Orbart.

He laughed, baring his teeth.

“Weren’t we not supposed to get into it? …Does this mean you don’t mind anymore?”

“I am surprised that you believe you can win against me in this city. If you have gone senile, I would recommend you yield your Divine General title to another.”

“Kah-ha-ha! That’ll never happen. I’m planning to be the longest-lived Divine General.”

Both sets of eyes gleamed as they met, readying themselves.

Yoruna exhaled a puff of smoke from her mouth, and Orbart turned upside down in midair. Kicking off the smoke that had spread in the air, he flew like an arrow.

“Ngh!”

His slicing kick crashed straight into the puff of smoke Yoruna had just exhaled. The smoke, which should not have been solid or had any real mass, caught Orbart’s kick and absorbed the impact.

But even if his attack was blocked in an unexpected way, Orbart did not simply linger.

“Oooooshaaaa!!!”

Spinning his short legs quickly, he unleashed a furious succession of ten, twenty kicks. The smoke dispersed the impact of one or two kicks, but it scattered gradually with each kick, until finally it lost its form and was no longer useful as a shield.

That it even managed to work that way at all is weird, but…

“That’s an interesting trick. I’d like to have a scroll for it.”

“Unfortunately, it is a secret technique impossible for a shinobi who cannot love anyone.”

As Orbart broke through the smoke, Yoruna’s pipe swung right in front of his eyes. It was not really the right weight or length to be useful as a club, but when Orbart tried to meet it with his arm—or no, with a kunai hidden up his sleeve—there was a screech, and the kunai shattered. The old man’s tiny body went flying backward.

“Nuoo?! What is that pipe?!”

“A gift from long ago. One of my beloved accessories.”

“My kunai’s pretty old, and I liked it, too.”

Orbart landed with a splash of tiles, smirking provocatively at Yoruna’s response. The next moment, his smirk faded as he started bouncing all around Yoruna at a speed normal people could not follow.

In years past, there was a boxer who used to float like a butterfly and sting like a bee, and that was exactly what Orbart seemed to be re-creating with the shattered palace keep as his stage.

“You are bursting with energy, but perhaps a little too mischievous.”

The tiles exploded wherever Orbart stepped, and when he appeared the next moment, he let fly with a single sharp blow right at Yoruna, before flitting away again. With her supernatural reflexes, she caught the blows with her pipe or else dodged, responding with moves that seemed like a gentle dance.

Subaru was entranced by their superhuman clash.

“Au…!”

Louis was quivering at Subaru’s side as she watched the same scene unfold. It felt like this battle was being fought on a level where even Louis might not be able to intervene. No matter who won, the resulting destruction would be unbelievable.

If the disaster was left to fester, everyone in the city would notice, in which case, the people who adored Yoruna and Orbart’s presumed comrades in the false emperor’s group would all have to act.

What remained after that would be a war that consumed the entire city—far from the ideal that Subaru had pictured.

“Shiiiiiyaaa!”

The spinning old man raised his voice, piercing the roof right in front of Yoruna. The next moment, there was a shock wave through the roof, exploding beneath Yoruna, sending her high into the air and flipping the things in the air with the things on the roof.

“There, how do you like that?!”

The next moment, countless shuriken raced toward Yoruna from all directions.

When did he throw them? It was an unpredictable shinobi skill. The spinning blades traced different arcs that threatened to tear into Yoruna’s soft skin.

Just before her pale skin and beautiful kimono were shredded and stained with blood…

“Is it not obvious? I am the master of the Demon City.”

…there were a series of thuds as the shuriken stopped all around her. It was not due to some super-fast movement on her part, though. She hadn’t done anything. The shuriken had been intercepted by a roof tile that had risen into the air.

It was not a lucky fluke, either. There were countless shuriken aimed at her, so there was no way random debris could stop them all.

Subaru and Orbart both stared with eyes wide as Yoruna swung her arm. The tile that caught the shuriken was joined by more tiles swirling around Yoruna, forming a winding spiral of steps in midair.

Yoruna stepped calmly onto the tiles, moving with deliberation down each step back to the palace keep. It was like an illusion, or some sort of telekinetic ability. Of course it could also be called magic, but it was different from all the magic Subaru knew.

She was not manipulating fire or water or some other element; she was controlling the objects that made up the building.

“Kah, you really are trouble. This is that mysterious thing Cecils or Araki mentioned. How does that even work?”

“I said it once already. This is a secret technique impossible for a shinobi who cannot love anyone… Despite how it may seem, I am a woman capable of handling objects with care.”

Yoruna smiled as she put her pipe in her mouth and clapped her hands. With that signal, a wave spread across the half-shattered keep. Tiles rose into the air, and the smoke of her pipe wrapped around her like a giant snake.

It was almost as if reality was reshaping itself to match her wishes.
