chapters.text:
Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

“I-is this…?”

“Au! Uauau!”

Louis clung to Subaru’s arm as he gulped in surprise at what was unfolding on the roof. Subaru finally remembered what Abel had said.

It was an absurd and crazy idea, but…

“Is she using her soul marriage on the palace, too…?”

Subaru could not believe how powerful the master of the Demon City was.

3

She was using soul marriage on the palace itself, sending Odo coursing through even inanimate objects.

That was how Yoruna had summoned a spiral staircase of ceiling tiles. Abel had called her technique abnormal when it was cast on the hundred or so people chasing them, but this was something else entirely.

If she had divided her Odo into her palace and her pipe and her household items, then…

“That can’t be good for her body…!”

It was tiring enough just linking with one person and sharing mana. Subaru had experience with that on a regular basis, thanks to Beatrice, so he knew how heavy a burden it could be.

In Yoruna’s case, depending on the scale of her ability, it was a hundred, maybe even a thousand or ten thousand times worse.

“Ha-ha, that is an odd ability. Sheesh, no matter how long I live, there’s always new techniques I don’t know leaping out one after the other. Really makes my head ache.”

“This is the stage you’ve set. There is no point lamenting now. From my perspective, your skill is sufficiently dangerous…in which case I might as well erase you.”

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! I’m not gonna fade away that easi… Whoa?!”

Orbart laughed heartily and then leaped backward at the immediate swell of malice. The next moment, the ceiling beneath Orbart’s feet exploded, launching the tiles straight up. It was payback for his earlier attack—and it continued without end.

Thud, thud, thud. The chain of explosions chased after Orbart as he backflipped away. And right where he was escaping to, there was another thud as Yoruna landed behind him.

Pinning him between her and the rolling shock waves, Yoruna unleashed a kick.

“………”

Her leg swiped through the air, leaving destruction in its wake as if a giant beast had just rampaged across the roof. The ceiling swelled upward, ready to swallow up Orbart’s tiny body.

Subaru could not believe his eyes as the roof became a stormy sea, but what happened next was just as impossible.

“I’m pretty great, huh, using a ground swimming technique like that?”

As the tiles closed in like a torrent, just before they crashed into him, Orbart leaped into the destruction, coming out the other side of the onrushing wave.

Grinding his foot into the roof stripped of tiles, Orbart raised his head and kept a healthy distance from Yoruna.

It had been not even a minute of fighting, but that was more than enough to prove they fully deserved their titles. These two were among the empire’s strongest fighters.

But as this back-and-forth continued, it was hard to imagine the battle ending anytime soon. And it was probably not just outsiders like Subaru and Louis looking on who felt that.

“Sheesh, not just strong, but dangerous. His Highness would be angry if the Third has so much trouble shaking off the Seventh.”

“Then what shall you do?”

“Well, it’s not like I was just running around for no reason…”

Yoruna’s neat brow furrowed as she addressed Orbart, who rubbed his chin, and as he rubbed it, the old man’s cheeks twisted, and he glanced in a different direction.

His yellow eyes were brimming with excitement as they turned toward the two children watching the battle…

“Ngh.”

“Old Man!!!”

Subaru shuddered beneath his sharp gaze at the same moment Yoruna launched a tile with a kick. Another fierce attack aimed at Orbart…

“That’s why you never can reach His Highness even after all those rebellions.”

Orbart raised his leg to meet her, and their kicks crashed with a thunderclap.

Yoruna ground her teeth, Orbart clenched his, and after a second, both of them flew backward in opposite directions.

Seeing the big opening between them, Orbart stuck his arms into his sleeves and pulled them back out. There were four dark balls in between the fingers of each hand.

“The ration balls?!”

“Sure looks like it, right? But it’d be a bad idea to eat these, since they’re stuffed with shards of fire magic stones.”

Orbart grinned maliciously as he swung his arms.

If he had been telling the truth, those dark balls were explosives, and they would explode right as Yoruna was left open…but something different happened.

“I remember the fellows you fought during the last rebellion. I bet none of them would do this, so it should be nice and new.”

Grinning, Orbart threw the explosives into the sky all around the roof.

It did not seem like he was aiming for anything in particular, and that would be correct. As far as Orbart was concerned, it was fine as long as they fell wherever there were people.

Just that would…

“From what I’ve heard, the people in this city of yours are pretty sturdy… But I wonder if they’re sturdier than the kids in my village?”

“—You lout!”

The explosives were small, but there was no telling how hard they would hit. And Yoruna’s soul marriage was cast on who knew how many people in the city. That meant it was too dangerous to ignore those bombs.

Yoruna reached the same conclusion in an instant.

“Hah, aaaaaaaah!!!!”

Yoruna slammed her foot hard enough to crack the roof, then swung the metal pipe that she had used to attack Orbart. It left a swirl of purple smoke trailing in its wake of her pipe as she swung her arm. The purple smoke was like a slash spreading across the sky of Chaosflame.

The weighty smoke swallowed up all the scattered explosives. The next instant, there was a string of terrific explosions that rocked the city and turned the sky red. One of the explosions happened right next to where Subaru and Louis were standing…

“Gah…”

The enormous explosion and shock wave rocked Subaru’s brain, sending him slumping to the ground.

He almost wanted to ask what type of person would walk around with bombs up his sleeve, but considering Orbart had just tried to scatter them all across the city, the answer was obvious.

“Uau!”

Small hands shook Subaru’s shoulders. As he looked up, he saw that the world had at some point turned red, and almost everything was fuzzy. And there was Louis, her face twisted in worry. She was clinging to him, tears in her eyes as he tried to tell her he was all right.

“Ah.”

Out of the corner of his eye, he saw Orbart appear behind Yoruna.

She had just finished swinging her pipe to deal with the bombs. Orbart was right behind her, about to plunge his hand into her back.

If it were a manga, this would be the part where he pierced her heart with a single thrust. Yoruna and Orbart both wielded superhuman power, so it would not be surprising if that actually happened.

She’s going to die…

“Louis!”

Grabbing Louis’s hand, Subaru pointed toward them.

It was the signal they had arranged beforehand with careful practice when entering the palace. Louis’s eyes opened wide, and the next instant, the world flickered. Subaru knew this meant they had teleported.

“Ah.”

Without even a chance to breathe, Subaru let out a limp groan.

The reason was simple: a sudden warm feeling robbed him of his fuzzy, bright red vision. It was some warm liquid drenching his face.

He tried to wipe it away when he realized the source.

“Louis?”

Louis’s hand felt too light.

“What was that? Weren’t you slumped down over there?”

There was a curious tone to Orbart’s voice as Subaru looked up in shock. He could faintly make out the wily old man cocking his head and that there was an arm waving.

A red world, and an even redder arm waving.

“Louis…”

Right in front of a dangerous man, Subaru called out Louis’s name and gripped her hand tighter.

We have to get away from here. A double jump, or maybe even more. I’m gonna throw up, but just suck it up.

I’ll deal with it. We have to get away.

So…

“Louis! Hurry…”

“You’re asking a bit much of the poor girl. She doesn’t even have a head anymore.”

“…Huh?”

Subaru didn’t understand.

Maybe it was because he was smaller and his young brain was less developed, but it was almost like he was resisting. Like he didn’t want to understand.

But hearing him say she had no head…

“Lou…is…”

He pulled her light arm close. He could not see her in the fuzzy red haze over his vision.

He could not say whether that was because of something wrong with his eyes or if it was because her entire body was stained red.

The only thing he knew for sure was that Louis had died.

She had died without him figuring out what to do with her, what to do about her.

Subaru had let her die.

“Child! Child, look at me!”

Two hands grabbed his cheeks as he looked down, pulling his head up.

There was a beautiful woman’s face right in front of him. The only reason he did not immediately recognize it as Yoruna’s was because there was such a pained look on her face.

Seeing himself reflected in her wavering eyes, Subaru understood her reaction.

“…Ah.”

As he knelt there, his face was a terrible sight. His left eye was a bloody mess; his right eye was dangling out of its socket. He hadn’t escaped the explosion at all. It had knocked his eye right out of its socket.

It’s like a lame zombie movie…

“…!”

Realizing the situation he was in, Subaru threw up, and the world he saw through his tattered eye started spinning. But Yoruna’s hands did not let him fall over. She looked him in the eye with trembling lips.

“Child…love me. Right now.”

Looking him right in the eye, she made a crazy demand.

Not just to love her, but right away. It was absurd. What am I even supposed to do? I don’t know. It’s not that easy to just love someone.

She’s a nice person, and beautiful. But…

“Child! If you love me, that wound can…”

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! C’mon now, that’s a pretty tall ask. Not that I know much about it, but love’s not something that just sprouts on command like that, is it?”

“Silence!”

As she roared at Orbart and his taunts, a deep emotion seeped into Yoruna’s eyes. Watching it from so close, Subaru breathed in and out with a rasp, slowly readying his heart for the pain that was sure to come.

Louis is dead. I’m in bad shape. I can’t make this any worse…

“Child.”

The voice drew Subaru’s attention upward. And in that one instant, Yoruna’s face drew near.

“………”

And with a serious face, her lips touched Subaru’s.

There was a soft feeling on his forehead, and he could feel her breath right next to him. It took him several seconds to realize he had been kissed. And then…

“My lips are not cheap. With this…”

As she released the kiss, Yoruna’s face moved away, and her voice faded in desperation. But now Subaru understood what it was she would have said.

She wanted him to love her. Because if Subaru loved her, the situation would change.

That’s the source of her power. Really, that’s the source of her strength.

But…

“I already love someone…”

Through the red fog clouding his vision, he saw the face of the girl he loved in the distance. Thinking of her and her smile, his heart raced.

He could not love Yoruna. He could not lie to himself…

“Well, things usually don’t go smoothly between boys and girls.”

Subaru’s world jolted as a disappointed voice rang in his ears.

“………”

Yoruna’s face that had been right in front of him disappeared, and all he could see was the red sky. But soon the world spun, and the sky disappeared. As it spun, he saw Yoruna kneeling down and Orbart standing in front of her. And the body of girl lay next to Yoruna.

That’s probably Louis.

And he saw something else, someone else in between Yoruna and Orbart.

“…Ah.”

It was the body of a headless child. Of a young Subaru Natsuki.

“Dear, oh dear, killing kids is draining. At least it’s not too much actual work.”

“You bloody old man!!!”

With a shout, Yoruna slammed into Orbart. He met it head-on, and as their attacks clashed, the entire palace rocked.

It swayed, cracked, crumbled, destruction spreading in every direction.

Subaru didn’t know what happened after that.

He didn’t know anything. And in his ignorance, his head bounced against the roof.

Bounced and…

4

He was dragged into a dark, dark space.

Suspended in nothingness, with no arms, no legs, and unable to understand. A space without sky or ground, without swaying, without wavering, without struggling, without taste, without trembling.

It was both utterly familiar and unknown.

Slowly moving away and yet drawing ever nearer.

And in that pitch-black, everlasting darkness, there was an echo.

Echoes of sobs. Someone was crying. A voice rang out, tugging at a heart that did not exist.

“I love you.”

It was a confession of love. A pleading love, a begging love, a beseeching love, a giving love, a loving love.

“I love you. I love you. I love you.”

The love was supposed to be imbued with all sorts of emotions. Joy, anger, sadness, celebration. A vortex of emotion.

“I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you.”

And yet there was just one emotion in this love that tried to consume the impenetrable darkness.

“I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you…”

All of that emotion, all of that swirling love was filled with sadness.

The sadness, the grief, the grieving sadness made the love sob.

The sobbing did not end.

The sobbing that made him want to die just listening to it was unending.

A grieving love, a sad love, a love that was sadness itself. The loving love wept, and grieving its sadness, at last—

“…Where are you?”

5

“From what I’ve heard, the people in this city of yours are pretty sturdy… But I wonder if they’re sturdier than the kids in my village.”

“—You lout!”

The red spinning world shifted, and an urgent voice rang in his ears.

On one side was an old man, and on the other, a woman.

Orbart and Yoruna. I’ve realized that much. But that’s it.

“Eh…”

“Hah, aaaaaaaah!!!!”

Just as he murmured dumbly, there was a heavy thud—Yoruna’s foot slammed into the roof of the palace, and she simultaneously swung the metal pipe in her hand. The pipe spun in a big arc with terrible speed and destructive force, scattering smoke into the sky above Chaosflame.

Subaru already knew what was about to happen and why.

And yet before his mind could catch up to reality…

The bombs struck her smoke and exploded. The blast swallowed up everything nearby.

“Gah…”

Subaru’s vision went red again. The exact same impact from just a minute ago struck him again.

The distinct sound of something breaking in his head rang out. That sound and his red vision were directly connected, since both were the result of his eyeball rupturing.

And the other half of his vision going black was…

“Agh, gh, gaaaaaaaaah!!!”

Covering his face with both hands, Subaru screamed as he was hit by a wave of pain and the realization of what had happened.

He realized that one eye was ruptured and the other had popped out of its socket. When his brain refused to understand, he had managed to ignore the pain somehow. That was impossible now that he was fully aware.

“Aaargh! Agh, gyaaaaaah!”

“Uau! Uauu!”

Subaru fell over backward, wailing as something clung to him.

Someone’s saying my name. Who is it? My ears are ringing, and my own voice is so grating. God, the pain. I can hear my blood pumping. Inside? Outside? I don’t know, but it hurts. Agh. Everything hurts. It hurts so much.

Someone save me. I don’t want it to hurt anymore. Make it stop. It hurts, it hurts, it hurts.

“Chi—”

“Hey now, that’s a bad move.”

Subaru’s head spun from the pain, and the red world gleamed with light.

He cried and screamed and shouted and tried to flail, but something was holding him down. It was in the way. If he screamed louder, if he flailed louder, maybe the pain would leave.

No, it’s my face that hurts. My eyes and ears. If another part hurts…if this pain was somewhere else…

“Uau! Auaa.”

He slammed the back of his head against the ground over and over, when suddenly, he was pulled up by a pair of slender arms and locked in a grapple. It hurts so! Why? It hurts. It’s killing me.

“Gh…”

“Kah, are you serious, fox-girl? What kind of body do you have not to die from that? When Cecils said he couldn’t take your head, was he being literal?”

“…A maiden would never reveal her secrets to a cur who dared raise his hand against a child.”

He could hear an argument in the distance. But he could barely hear it between his own voice and the voice of whoever was holding him down.

I can’t hear well. I don’t know. It hurts. Everything hurts.

Everything hurt. There was red, and there was pain, and everything hurt. It was all because of that.

“It’s that…! It’s wrong! Not me! It’s not me! So wh-ughiiiii!”

“Uuu!!!”

Struggling and flailing, Subaru tried to push it away. Push and run away. And then what?

I’ll worry about that after I get away. It can wait, so…

“I can’t stand listening to a child squealing. It’s such a pain.”

“Stop!”

A woman’s desperate cry and a low, merciless murmur. Then there was the telltale whistling sound of something drawing closer. From behind, the person grappling him squeezed Subaru tight. But that was not enough to do anything, since a red-hot light swelled and swallowed them both up.

Swallowed them both up, erasing the pain, and then…

“From what I’ve heard, the people in this city of yours are pretty sturdy… But I wonder if they’re sturdier than the kids in my village.”

“—You lout!”

The next instant, he heard the exact same voices he’d heard before.

“Huh…?”

It was all so sudden. Just as the world cut out, it immediately restarted. Other colors filled out his vision. He could hear the breeze in his ears again. He could feel the warmth of the girl holding his hand, and…

“Hah, aaaaaaaah!!!!”

After the woman’s gallant shout, an explosion shattered the air. His vision grew red and dark again.

“Ghhh, aaaaaaaargh!!!”

He clawed at his face, his ruined eyes radiating pain as he fell onto his back with a scream.

“Uau! Uaau!”

He could feel someone leap toward him with a tearful shout, and then the world sank into an earsplitting screech. Subaru’s head was blotted out by pain and suffering and tears and terror and a bright red question mark asking why.

I…I probably died. I died. I definitely died. It hurt. It was awful. But then I came right back to this place and died, and it hurt, and there was a red explosion.

Even as he understood that much, though, the giant question of why kept echoing in his head.

—This isn’t right.

That vague, instinctual reaction rang out in his mind, though the pain and red threatened to drown it out.

My eyes are burst and missing, and my eardrums are torn, and it hurts, and I’m dying, and I’m just going to die miserably again right away. I just want it to stop hurting.

That was all he could think of as tears and snot and pee all leaked out.

“…is wrong…”

“Uau! Au, uu!”

“…wrong…it’s not…my…”

Wrong. Wrong wrong wrong. Wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong.

Wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong wrong—

“Hngh…!”

Before the pain consumed everything in his head, there was one thing he thought that he could not forget.

The red and painful world that kept repeating and repeating, the suffering Subaru had been cast into.

This…this is…

“Wrong…!”

This was not Subaru Natsuki’s Return by Death. It was something different.

chapters.text:
Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

CHAPTER 7

BEYOND THE ELEVENTH SECOND

1

“From what I’ve heard, the people in this city of yours are pretty sturdy… But I wonder if they’re sturdier than the kids in my village.”

“—You lout!”

It was the same voices again: a husky old man’s voice, and a woman’s voice brimming with anger.

And…

“………”

—The thundering chain of explosions and the agonizing red.

Clutching his face in pain, he collapsed on the spot. The light body that clung to him, pushing down on him was familiar, too.

It was all familiar, but he could not handle it. There was not enough time.

From the depths of his soul, he sobbed at the blurry red vision and the head-splitting pain.

It was all wasted. The ten seconds of pain and despair looped over and over, accomplishing nothing.

The pain made it hard to think; the red haze and destruction of his eyes made it hard to see anything. And then they disappeared, only for him to go through that same vivid hell again.

Pain, red, fear, why, death. Pain, red, fear, why, death. Pain, red, fear, why, death. Pain, red, fear, why, death. Pain, red, fear, why, death. Pain, red, fear, why, death. Pain, red, fear, why, death. Pain, red, fear, why, death. Pain, red, fear, why, death. Pain, red, fear, why, death. Pain, red, fear, why, death. Pain, red, fear, why, death. Over and over and over again.

I’m going crazy.

“From what I’ve heard, the people in this city of yours are pretty sturdy… But I wonder if they’re sturdier than the kids in my village.”

“—You lout!”

The same voices again. And the pain and blurry red stopped for just a moment.

But the thought of experiencing it all again terrified him and tore at his soul.

I don’t want to hear anymore. I don’t want to hurt anymore. Make it stop.

“Aaaaaaaaaaaagh!!!”

He screamed at the top of his lungs, closed his eyes to stop seeing anything, and crouched down, covering his head and cowering.

The explosion rocked his small body, knocking him over. There was a ringing in his ears, and he shuddered, expecting the pain and blurry red to come again.

“…!”

There’s…no pain.

There was no pain from one eye bursting and the other being knocked out of its socket. His ears were ringing and not really working, but the world was not red. His throat was the only thing that really hurt, and that was from screaming at the top of his lungs.

“Why…?”

“Uau!”

A small body clung on to him as he gaped in dumbfounded shock.

Louis. Louis was pulling at his arm, trying to get him to stand up. But his legs would not move, and he could not stand or figure out why this was all happening. He just hiccupped, and, unable to hold it in, he curled up and cried tears of joy that the red suffering was held at bay for even just a moment.

“Chi—”

“Hey now, that’s a bad move.”

The otherworldly battle continued in the distance as he hunched over and sobbed. The balance of the fight had shifted, and he could vaguely see the woman kneeling.

Yoruna’s knee was bent, and Orbart was standing behind her. He swung his bloodstained right hand, cocking an eyebrow as he looked down at Yoruna in surprise.

“Gh…”

“Kah, are you serious, fox-girl? What kind of body do you have not to die from that? When Cecils said he couldn’t take your head, was it literal?”

“…A maiden would never reveal her secrets to a cur who dared raise his hand against a child.”

A trickle of blood ran from the corner of Yoruna’s mouth as she gritted her teeth, but the spirit in her voice was unwavering.

“Kah-ha-ha-ha!” Orbart laughed loudly and swung his blood-drenched arm again. “What a strange thing to say. This is how you raise a hand against a child.”

“Stop!”

A dark ball escaped his sleeve. The bomb flew toward Subaru and Louis. Louis immediately moved in front of Subaru, but she was too late.

The red light erupted right in front of Subaru again, consuming and shattering Louis’s body and Subaru’s body both.

“From what I’ve heard, the people in this city of yours are pretty sturdy… But I wonder if they’re sturdier than the kids in my village.”

“—You lout!”

And Subaru heard the same voices again.

2

The moment the red and pain disappear, close your eyes and scream.

Subaru had discovered how to escape the red agony he had experienced time and time and time and time again.

If the red and the pain came again, Subaru was helpless. He would just cry and scream and howl and die. And once he died, he would hear the voices again, and then the explosion and the red and the pain.

Not again. Make it stop. Please make it stop.

“From what I’ve heard, the people in this city of yours are pretty sturdy… But I wonder if they’re sturdier than the kids in my village.”

“—You lout!”

The same voices again.

In that one moment, the pain and red and everything receded, and it felt like he could relax, but he didn’t let his guard down and did what he had to do.

“Aaaaaaaaaaaagh!!!”

He squeezed his eyes shut and screamed at the top of his lungs.

He could not hear during the scream, but Yoruna was probably swinging her pipe, setting off the bombs Orbart threw.

So next is…

“…!”

An explosion and shock wave rocked his body, knocking him down. The sharp corner of a tile poked his butt, causing a sharp pain that made him want to cry.

Don’t. Don’t cry. I need to be able to see…

“I can see…!”

He tentatively opened his eyes. Thankfully, neither had burst. Both were still in their sockets. He could see.

His ears were ringing and useless like always, and his throat hurt, but that red agony didn’t come.

It worked. Thank goodness.

If he closed his eyes and screamed, he would escape that awful red hell.

“Uau!”

He almost broke down in tears when Louis frantically grabbed on to him. He could finally see her face. Her blue eyes were open wide, and she was obviously worried about him.

Without thinking, Subaru hugged her back tightly.

“Uu.”

“I’m fine! The pain, the red… Argh, I’m fine…”

He shouted, so he had to fight back the tears again. But his observation had been right. The red and the pain were gone. All he had to do was close his eyes and scream.

If I just do that, it’ll be okay…

“Yeah, this isn’t all right at all yet. This is just the beginning.”

Subaru reflexively looked up as a chill ran down his spine.

Orbart was smirking and threw shuriken right as surprise appeared on Subaru’s face. There was no way to tell how they would fly as they homed in on Subaru and Louis with a dangerous gleam.

“Ahhhh!”

“I won’t allow it.”

Yoruna appeared right in front of Subaru. She thrust her pipe into the path of the shuriken, deflecting and knocking them all down. At the same time, the tiles to the left and right of Orbart flipped up like a mousetrap or flyswatter.

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! That’s an interesting technique! Showy and pretentious!”

Orbart twisted his little body, casually dodging the waves of roof tiles crashing into each other.

Subaru always thought that when it came to fighting for a living, having a bigger body was better, and attacking from a distance was advantageous. Orbart’s agility turned that idea on its head.

“But it’s maybe a little too flashy. A single needle can be more than enough to kill someone.”

“Such compliments are uncomfortable coming from you. What do you think of this?”

The sole of Yoruna’s sandal clicked, and tile after tile flipped and floated into the air, creating a spiral.

A swirl of destruction began to form inside the palace like a tornado right around Orbart…

“Ooo?! Now, this is something…”

“Please enlighten me as to whether shinobi techniques can help you escape from a place with no openings.”

Before she finished speaking, Yoruna clenched her raised hand. The next instant, the swirling tornado of tiles crashed down on Orbart. They crashed and clattered mercilessly into each other as the loud crash echoed across the warping palace keep.

“What a waste this is. If you didn’t saddle yourself with something so pointless, you could have had it out with me a bit more seriously.”

“…Why is that?”

“If you’re fighting to protect someone but make yourself weaker in the process, you’re getting your priorities all wrong. This is why you can never reach His Highness.”

Orbart’s yellow eyes looked past Yoruna to Subaru and Louis.

As his fear swelled, Subaru immediately hugged Louis and grabbed her hand. He pointed at his feet and yelled, “Ms. Yoruna! Louis and I will disappear! Do your best!”

He felt terrible running away and leaving her behind after getting her involved. But if they stayed, she would have to fight while protecting them, and Orbart would take advantage of that to kill them.

“…!”

The world around him shifted. Subaru and Louis teleported into the palace. Obeying Subaru’s signal, Louis activated her warp. They descended into the wreckage of the palace keep, successfully escaping the battlefield above.

“Ugh…”

Just as he confirmed that, he felt dizzy and nauseated from the warp. For a second, he recalled the red and pain, but this discomfort was paradise compared to that agony.

And with her no longer having to protect them, Yoruna could unleash her full—

“But what now?!”

But his thoughts were interrupted by the return of the thunderous explosion that provoked his newest trauma.

A tremendous series of explosions shook the entire palace. Crouching, Subaru almost fell over and struggled to stay upright as he looked up at the ceiling.

He could not see it, but that had to be Orbart. As many bombs as he had already scattered, he still had that many more just tucked away.

“…Oh. There you are.”

“Eh?”

Looking up, he saw a face slithering around on the ceiling. Orbart’s small body dropped smoothly from the ceiling.

That’s how he dodged the tornado of tiles and the waves.

“H-how…?”

“You just up and disappeared on me. Look at me makin’ a fool of myself thinking you were a regular pair of brats.”

“Uuu!”

Seeing the old monster’s malicious grin, Louis immediately kicked up at him with her slender leg. This didn’t catch him by surprise. He cut off her foot with a kunai. It spun and spurted blood as it separated from her leg.

“A, uuuuuuu!”

“Noooooo!!!!”

Subaru reached out to Louis in desperation as she screamed, but he failed to pull her close or hug her. Before he could do anything, her heartrending cry went quiet.

A kunai was sticking out of her neck.

“…Ngh!”

Then he heard a light thud, and a new scorching heat tore at his throat far worse than all his screaming did. Burbling blood filled his throat, stopping him from saying anything or even breathing.

“It’d be a pain if you ran away. But the heads’ll be enough to make her cry.”

Orbart’s finger pushed against the back of Subaru’s head. He dropped to his knees, and his head fell forward, coming to a rest in his lap. The head was still connected by a bit of skin, so it lay there without rolling away.

“That’s what you call a headrest.”

That terrible, unfunny joke was the last thing Subaru heard.

And then…

“From what I’ve heard, the people in this city of yours are pretty sturdy… But I wonder if they’re sturdier than the kids in my village.”

“—You lout!”

The same voices, yet again.

He immediately pulled Louis close, wanting to do something.

But as he was thinking about what to do next, the explosions rang out.

His vision exploded into blurry redness, and the pain swallowed Subaru Natsuki again.

3

The moment you hear the same words you heard before, close your eyes and shout.

That was the law of survival Subaru had discovered after reliving those ten seconds of despair dozens of times.

He had not yet found a path that led much farther.

“From what I’ve heard, the people in this city of yours are pretty sturdy… But I wonder if they’re sturdier than the kids in my village.”

“—You lout!”

The moment he heard those words, Subaru moved on instinct. Covering his ears, closing his eyes, and shouting, he endured the blast of the now familiar explosions.

By covering his ears, he could protect his eardrums, and by closing his eyes, his eyes were saved. He did not know what his shouting did, exactly, but he had shouted every time he avoided the pain and the red, so it was unthinkable not to do it.

He did not want to risk falling into that hell again just because he tried something slightly different. Even as he reminded himself, if he messed up the timing even once, it would mean repeating the ten seconds of despair ten or more times before he would get another chance.

Not again. Never again. No more pain. No more scary and bad things.

It never got easier. He did not get used to it at all. Pain always hurt. The terror was always just out of sight. And death came without fail after the pain and the terror.

“Uau!”

With eyes and ears still in working condition, Subaru grabbed Louis when she clung to him.

Once more, he made it through the initial explosions unhurt. Holding tightly on to Louis, he pictured the chain of events that came next.

First is…

“Shuriken.”

“Don’t think it’s over if you just hold out!”

He remembered just as he heard Orbart. A storm of shuriken came flying from every direction to hem in Subaru and Louis. There were a dozen shuriken, and if any landed, Subaru wouldn’t be able to move.

Yoruna got ready to stop them.

“I won’t allow—!”

“It’s okay, Miss Yoruna!”

Holding his hand up to stop Yoruna from leaping to their aid, Subaru then pointed his finger while squeezing Louis’s hand with his other hand.

“What?!”

In an instant, they disappeared, and Orbart’s shuriken hit nothing but air.

Louis’s warp bamboozled even Orbart on the first encounter. Looking at Orbart in the distance as he stepped down on the ceiling tiles, Subaru gritted his teeth.

They had successfully warped into the palace to escape a bunch of times before, but every time, they had been followed by Orbart and died miserably…

“If it’s just once…”

They could take Orbart by surprise. This was an opportunity that presented itself after countless attempts, and a figure leaped into that opening.

“Foolish of you to look away!”

Yoruna’s furious ax kick slammed into Orbart. Slow to react, the old man sacrificed his left arm rather than have his head caved in. There was a boom and a shock wave as the old man’s arm practically exploded from the kick.

His withered arm was broken in a bunch of places and was now useless. Even for him, that has to be a serio—

“Here—a ninety-year-old gift.”

“No way?!”

But against all Subaru’s expectations, Orbart did something crazy. Holding out his bloody left arm, he cut it with a kunai at the upper arm, tossing it toward Yoruna with a spray of blood.

“………”

She was forced to make a split-second decision. Whether to knock it away or dodge.

“Unfortunately, they’re both wrong.”

“Gh…?!”

Before she could react, there was an explosion at her feet. While sacrificing his arm to block her kick, he had laid a trap in a place she wasn’t paying attention to. The attack caught her by surprise from below. A stream of blood trickled from her mouth.

“Shinobi fundamentals. While they wonder right or left, hit them somewhere else.”

“You are…an impudent old man…!”

Yoruna glared at Orbart after taking that piercing shock wave. She stepped forward, ignoring the arm spinning toward her in the air to grab the old monster.

Just as she advanced, Orbart spoke again.

“I lied, though.”

That was when his severed arm exploded.

“…!”

“Miss Yoruna!!!”

Caught in yet another explosion, Yoruna was knocked back. As he watched her skid across the top of the roof, Subaru’s eyes widened, and he shouted with his sore throat.

Even his useless arm could be booby-trapped and give him a decisive foothold toward victory. It was an appalling performance befitting his title.

The old monster turned toward Yoruna to rob her of her life.

I have to stop him somehow.

“Louis!”

To save Yoruna, Louis had to warp. The burden of using it consecutively without rest was heavy on Subaru’s body, but after facing this battle dozens of times with her, he could not bear to abandon her now.

Clutching Louis’s hand, he pointed toward Yoruna’s side—

“Auau!”

With her gallant response, the world blinked. Yoruna was right in front of him. Reaching his hand out to touch her, he tried to warp away before the internal trauma could catch up to him.

“Huh?”

But something hard hit his toes before he could reach Yoruna’s body. Looking down, he saw what it was—a dark round ball. The same ball that he had seen so many times now. The sight plunged him into the depths of despair.

“I don’t know how you’re doing it, but you’re flying wherever you point. I’ve already seen it before.”

Even if warp was effective the first time, the second time it wasn’t.

The vicious old man, off-balance from losing an arm, made the only move he could with his remaining arm.

“Uau.”

Again, Louis called his name and pulled on his arm. Light swelled around the black ball, sending countless deadly fragments into Subaru, Louis, and Yoruna, tearing and shredding their flesh.

There was a crimson spatter as the blades tore into his eyes, mouth, and everywhere else, drowning everything in stinging pain as his limbs were torn off.

He did not even have time to feel the pain as the blades chewed through his body.

“Pretty fun, right? Never know what you’ll get till you take a bite.”

The pain flashed red again, and Subaru could only question his sanity.

“From what I’ve heard, the people in this city of yours are pretty sturdy… But I wonder if they’re sturdier than the kids in my village.”

“—You lout!”

The same voices.

“Ngh.”

The moment he heard them, he covered his ears and closed his eyes and opened his mouth. But a scream did not emerge. There was just a hoarse rasp. But the blast and explosion still came. It rocked his body, knocking him down. I didn’t follow the rules. I didn’t shout. Please don’t hurt me.

But…

“Uau!”

There was a light impact as Subaru exhaled. He double-checked that his eyes and ears and everything else were fine. Even without the scream, they were still okay. The shout was unrelated. Keeping his mouth open might still be important.

I don’t know. I don’t know for sure, but…

“Ghhhh…”

Hugging Louis, he ground his teeth and sobbed, unable to find a way to survive for long after the explosion.

And so he simply cried and huddled in place without moving.

“I can’t stand listening to a child squealing. What a racket.”

An inescapable death consumed Subaru Natsuki again.

4

The red and pain came again and again. After that came powerlessness, and then the suffering, and the agony and the terror, repeating over and over. Even then, he still couldn’t reach it…

“Love me. Right now.”

How many times had she tried to save him when he became horribly battered? And sadly, he could never do what she asked.

“Uau! Uaau!”

Louis desperately pulled Subaru’s arm, trying to keep him alive, refusing to let him die. It was terrible how she died before him every time.

Time after time after time, he repeated those ten seconds of death and despair.

The red world, the agony that consumed everything, the powerlessness he felt no matter how many times he tried. He went through it countless times.

I’m going crazy. My spirit’s going to break. This isn’t Return by Death.

This was something else gripping Subaru Natsuki. He had never once thought that it was a mercy, but compared to the desolation of this endlessly looping ten-second span…

This was so lacking in love that it made Return by Death feel like a loving embrace.

5

“From what I’ve heard, the people in this city of yours are pretty sturdy… But I wonder if they’re sturdier than the kids in my village.”

“—You lout!”

The same voices again.

Orbart’s easygoing patter and Yoruna’s sharp snap.

His mind was numb, the continuation of his scream from before dying rang out, and his knees gave out. But even so, on pure reflex, he closed his eyes and covered his ears and left his mouth open with a scream.

“Hah, aaaaaaaah!!!!”

Yoruna swung her pipe with a shout, creating multiple explosions in the sky over Chaosflame. The hot blast and thundering boom hammered Subaru, and no matter how many times it happened to him, he still could not help getting knocked down.

“Uau!”

Louis leaped toward him when he fell. He caught her and hugged her tight. That, too, was a reflex at this point. Having died so many times over and over, he longed for the warmth of a living person.

There was no deeper meaning than that. None. So he gritted his teeth.

“Here it comes…”

There was no time to relax as another lethal attack came.

“Don’t think it’s over if you just hold out!”

In sync with the voice, Orbart threw his shuriken at Subaru and Louis. Subaru already knew those dozen blades coming from all angles could easily tear through children. He had been killed by shuriken more times than he could count now, but he could not remember which one had caused the pain. There hadn’t been any painless deaths, so there was no way to keep track.

“I won’t allow it.”

While he dwelled on that thought for a moment, Yoruna appeared in front of him. She parried and deflected every shuriken with her pipe and hammered back at Orbart with roof tiles.

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! That’s an interesting technique! Showy and pretentious!”

He deftly avoided them. Because Subaru was slow to react, he had ended up going down the same route as before, but after seeing this scene so many times, he knew there was nothing left for him to do.

The times Yoruna covered him when it looked like he would be hit by the attack, the times he escaped into the palace, the times he lost his mind and leaped out at Orbart… He always died, no matter what.

If every route, every move led to death, then what did that leave?

“But it’s maybe a little too flashy. Since a single needle’s enough to kill someone.”

“Such compliments are uncomfortable coming from you. What do you think of this?”

Orbart taunted her, and Yoruna responded by hitting the roof with the sole of her sandal. The tiles flipped up and floated into the air one after the other, creating a swirling tornado of destruction centered around the palace. Subaru already knew that it was incredibly powerful. But he also knew it would not defeat Orbart.

“What should I do…?”

I don’t know. And the pain and terror are coming.

I messed up. What do I do? Can I avoid it? That red world and the chorus of pain.

Even if I want to help Yoruna, I just get in the way. Even if I escape with Louis, he catches up right away. If only I had come back earlier. If only I had never come up onto the roof with Yoruna.

If I had let her go alone, if I had just gone without her, if I hadn’t run away from Abel and the others, if I hadn’t said anything about Louis, if Al, if Medium, if Talitta, if we weren’t shrunken, if I was the right Subaru, if Zikr, and Flop, and Mizelda, and Kuna, and Holly, and Utakata, and Priscilla, and Rem, Rem, Rem, Rem…

“Rem…”

Even though I still need to bring her back, I’m dying here. If I’m stuck in an inescapable death loop, just doomed to die over and over, then there’s nothing I can do. Nothing Subaru Natsuki can do.

The countless deaths, the pain, they weighed on Subaru, drowning him with a sense of powerlessness.

He could feel it weighing on his heart and his body, crushing him…

“Uau.”

The girl’s warm hand sat in his. Subaru inhaled.

The warmth reminded him.

Subaru Natsuki might be hopeless and helpless, but…

“What would everyone else do?”

6

Pain, red, fear, why, death.

Pain, red, fear, why, death. Pain, red, fear, why, death.

Pain, red, fear, why, death. Pain, red, fear, why, death. Pain, red, fear, why, death.

The ten seconds of despair repeated over and over and over again.

The pain and powerlessness layered in an unending hell that threatened to break Subaru’s spirit. He died over and over. He died, and the pain and suffering repeated over and over.

It never once went right. Every single time, Yoruna grieved, Louis sacrificed herself to save him, and he died.

But there was something beyond those ten seconds of despair. Time did not just end there.

Use all the time.

Even if death is certain, use it all and figure out how to reach the eleventh second.

What would everyone else do?

“From what I’ve heard, the people in this city of yours are pretty sturdy… But I wonder if they’re sturdier than the kids in my village.”

“—You lout!”

The same voices again.

In that instant, Subaru covered his ears, closed his eyes, and opened his mouth to endure the explosions. The blast wave and impact rocked his body, knocking him down. Right away, Louis leaped onto him with a shout of “Uau!” He caught her, hugged her reassuringly, and racked his brain.

What would everyone else do?

“………”

Subaru had been turned into a child again. His arms and legs were shorter, and his brain had surely regressed, too. Normally, he probably would have been able to do more, to think better. But that Subaru was not here, and he could not do much about that.

This was a problem that Subaru Natsuki could not solve.

So…

“If it was them…”

He had faced all sorts of problems and made all sorts of mistakes, but he had overcome them with the help of everyone else.

He was alone right now in the empire, and there was hardly anyone he knew here. But the things he had received from everyone were still there inside him.

“If it was them…”

What would they do? Otto, Garfiel, Roswaal, Frederica, Petra, Clind, Annerose, Meili, Puck, Ram, Beatrice, Emilia… What would they do?

“If it was them…”

What would they do?

Julius, Anastasia, Foxidna, Ricardo, Mimi, Hetaro, TB, Reinhard, Felt, Old Man Rom, Larry, Moe, and Curly, Al, Priscilla, Wilhelm, Ferris, Crusch, Liliana, Shaula… What would they do?

“They’re so strong.”

All of you who can fight Orbart head-on, I want your support.

Sorry, but the ones who don’t seem like they can do anything to deal with Orbart’s craftiness or crazy tricks, you can take a seat for now. Sorry, but thanks. Love y’all.

“And some of them could use magic.”

I probably can’t copy the people who could support Yoruna directly.

I want to avoid burdening her more when she’s already been so kind, but I don’t think healing magic will be very useful here. Sorry, but thanks. Love y’all, too.

“In which case…”

Then what about the ones who never give up and struggle to the very end?

What if I copy the ones who use everything they have and keep trying to reach the eleventh second and beyond?

“I won’t allow it.”

Yoruna swung her pipe, driving the shuriken away from Subaru and Louis with sharp clangs. Meanwhile, the roof tiles to the left and right of Orbart flipped up to crush the old monster.

“………”

He thought as hard as he could while watching Yoruna and Orbart fight.

How many times have I died? How many times have I seen this? I can still remember the pain. It aches just thinking about it.

The memory alone made him shrink back. His spirit flagged, and his soul cowered. It was as if Subaru Natsuki’s very being was freezing over. But…

“Uau.”

The warmth of one girl’s hand would not let the cold claim him.

I can’t just freeze up here. I can still remember everyone.

You can’t insert yourself in their fight.

Even if you want to help Yoruna win, you will just get in the way, because he’s targeting you. The fight’s already begun, so one of them has to win.

Orbart will probably always win this fight and kill both of you.

Well, is it enough for you two to survive?

I feel like that’s reeeeeally not enough.

Yoruna has to come out of this okay, too.

There must be a better way.

Don’t you dare stop thinkin’.

Idiot.

Don’t even joke about giving up now.

It’ll turn out all right.

Everyone’s here for you.

And you don’t wanna get hurt anymore, right?

Every battle must end.

There has to be an opening to intervene somewhere.

You’re gonna find your way back to Ria, right?

Find a way, I suppose.

That’s the key to victory.

“The key…to victory.”

Whose? The people fighting, of course.

Yoruna and Orbart are the ones fighting, so—

“No.”

“Uu?”

“No, no, no, that’s wrong.”

Subaru shouted as Louis cocked her head.

No, that’s not right. Everyone…

“The winner is—”

Once again, the red and pain appeared, and—

“From what I’ve heard, the people in this city of yours are pretty sturdy… But I wonder if they’re sturdier than the kids in my village.”

“—You lout!”

The same voices again.

The moment he heard them, he covered his ears, closed his eyes, opened his mouth, and crouched. The next moment, the blast rocked his body, but this time he didn’t get knocked down.

Then he looked up.

“Uau!”

Louis leaped at him, worried and looking concerned. Catching her in a hug, Subaru stood up.

“Thank you.”

“Uu?”

Louis’s eyes widened as he looked over her head. The pain of the fire scorching his whole body, of having his bones laid bare, of having his organs turned to a pulp—it stayed with him. If he let his focus slip even a little, he might scream and cry and roll around. But…

“Don’t think it’s over…”

Orbart prepared to throw the shuriken he had pulled from his sleeves, when his gaze met Subaru’s. The vicious old man who showed no mercy even to children stared into the eyes of a child who had confronted his own powerlessness countless times and was even now struggling to hold back his tears.

Orbart’s yellow eyes gleamed, as if sensing something significant.

“…Interesting.”

This time, the vicious old man threw his shuriken at Subaru Natsuki—not just as a ploy to distract Yoruna, but to kill him.

There was no playfulness in those shuriken. Subaru could feel the impending danger and malice on his skin, even though he could not follow them with his eyes, but he immediately raised his finger and pointed straight ahead at Orbart.

What would everyone else do?

When he thought as hard as he could about it from everyone else’s perspective, it dawned on him.

If it was them, then no matter how many times he died and how powerless he felt and how hopeless the situation was… No matter how battered Subaru became, they would still have faith in him.

They believed in Subaru no matter how painful and awful and scary it was, no matter how much he cried and wet himself and how pathetically he died.

I love you all.

The match here at the summit of the palace where I’ve died who knows how many times, the match to reach the eleventh second after these ten seconds of despair. The winner is—

The winner is always Master!

“Louiiiiiiis!!!”

Pointing straight at Orbart, he shouted the name of the girl who was the source of his warmth and clenched his hand around hers—in that moment the world shifted.

“—What?!”

Orbart shouted in surprise when his target who should have been killed by his shuriken disappeared.

It was completely outside of Orbart’s expectations, a technique the cautious shinobi did not recognize. He would be able to react the second time, but the first warp was their one and only way to catch Orbart by surprise.

And using Louis’s power, Subaru leaped—

“Aaaaaaaaaa!!!!”

“Nuoooh?!”

He clung ferociously to the back of Orbart’s head that had appeared right in front of him. Latching on to the small old man like a cornered animal, he bit into the tuft of white hair. Even Orbart could not react to suddenly being grappled from behind. Subaru latched on to the old man who was not much taller than he was.

Of course, Orbart immediately tried to pull him off, and Yoruna, surprised by the unbelievable development, started to rush over.

“Whoa! Wh-whaddaya think you’re doin’, kiddo?!”

“Child! Get away at once! Old man Orbart is—!”

Orbart’s hand grabbed Subaru by the hair, trying to pull him away, and though she wanted to stop it, Yoruna hesitated for fear of accidentally hitting Subaru.

Ignoring both of them, Subaru held on tight and shouted as loud as he could—

“—I win!!!”

“—What?”

Orbart’s grip loosened. And Yoruna’s eyes widened in confusion at what he was saying. Not paying any heed to them, though, Subaru clung on tightly, refusing to let go of Orbart. With the old man’s grip loosening, Subaru could finally raise his head.

“I win…I win!!! You lose, Mr. Orbart! Right?!”

“What are you talking about—?”

“Once is enough! That’s what you said!”

“Huh?”

Subaru shouted right into the puff of white hair in his face. Tears welled in his eyes, and his nose started to run from the sheer excitement, and his heart pounded. He sniffled, and his voice cracked.

“T-tag! Hide-and-seek was three times…but tag was only once…so…”

“………”

“So I win! I caught you! I win this match! You and Miss Yoruna lost to me! It’s my win…!”

Even Subaru thought it was an absurd leap in logic. They were the ones who chose hide-and-seek over tag in the first place. It was unfair to change that all of a sudden and try to claim victory. But even if it was unfair, he could not think of any other way.

And…

“You were the one who cheated first…”

“………”

“S-so it’s my win…”

He couldn’t hold back anymore. His voice got sticky and burbly as he began to sob. But he still held on tight, refusing to let go of his unfair victory. He had caught Orbart. That counted as a win.

“…What will you do, old man Orbart?”

Unexpectedly, Yoruna questioned the wily old man who had fallen silent. Glancing over, Subaru could see she had relit her pipe and there was a new trail of smoke rising. As she took a puff, she looked just as beautiful as she had before the fight began.

Depending on Orbart’s answer, she was ready to continue protecting Subaru and Louis even if that meant resuming their fight, even though she hardly knew them.

But that was not the only difficulty facing Orbart.

“Uau! Aa, uu!”

“That hurts.”

Louis had also warped to Orbart and was currently violently stomping on the old man’s feet. She narrowed her big round eyes as best she could to glare at him.

Faced with Subaru’s assertion, Yoruna’s question, and Louis’s glare, Orbart stayed silent for a moment and then scratched his head.

“I’m the one who said I don’t like dropping a match once I’ve started, but I never thought it’d come back to bite me like this.”

“Is that your answer?” Yoruna asked quietly.

Watching Orbart, she dropped her eyes down a level. It was not a special gesture. She was simply following Orbart as he promptly sat down. With Subaru still clinging to his back, he flashed a grin.

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! This is my loss no matter how you look at it. If I started saying winning or losing don’t matter, then I wouldn’t be a shinobi; I’d be nothing more than a beast.”

Orbart slapped his knee and looked up.

“I lose. It’s my loss!”

Underneath that blue sky, with the beautiful palace gradually repairing itself, the eleventh second after those ten seconds of despair came, and time gradually, steadily moved forward…

“I wiiiiiiin!”

Subaru sniffled and sobbed while still screaming his victory.

Orbart cackled.

“It’s aggravating hearing that again and again, so cut it out.”

And he smacked Subaru on the forehead.

Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

CHAPTER 8

UTOPIA CHAOSFLAME

1

“Uh, ugh, agh…”

Subaru kept struggling to hold back the sobs and the snot and the tears.

It was a crazy experience that even now he could hardly believe he had made it through.

The despair-inducing ten seconds that Subaru had gone through, and the eleventh second on the other side—just how many deaths had he experienced? It felt like a miracle that he had not given in, that his spirit had not broken, that his soul had not been ground down into dust. But on the other side of that hellish experience, this was the world he had arrived at.

“Uauu.”

Louis’s hair was a mess as she clung to his arm. In those countless loops, she had faced the same fate as Subaru, dying countless times, just like him. It seemed ridiculous to claim victory, but even that would have been impossible without her.

“I really…really don’t understand you.”

“Auu.”

“But I…couldn’t have done it…without you… Thank you…”

Subaru’s mind was a complete and total disaster zone. He knew just how dangerous a person she could be. He knew that, and yet he was still brimming with gratitude.

“…Louis?”

The levees suddenly burst. When she heard his halting thanks, the tears welled in her big round eyes and started pouring down her cheeks. The tears flowed like she did not know how to stop them.

“Louis, you’re…you’re crying…”

“Uu, uu!”

Louis did not try to wipe away the tears as she shook her head and clung to Subaru’s arms. It was like she was afraid he would disappear the moment she let go to wipe them away.

“Wipe your face, dummy…you dummy…”

Just as he was starting to calm the emotions roiling inside him, they threatened to bowl him over again when he saw her crying. Subaru had already shed so many tears himself.

Just when it felt like he and Louis were going to keep crying forever…

“You did very well. Both of you.”

“Ah…”

“You may cry as much as your heart desires. As the master of this city, I shall allow it.”

…a pair of arms reached around them from behind and gently hugged them. Subaru already knew the character of the voice’s owner. He understood that there was nothing but kindness in those words and the warmth of those arms. He knew that he would be forgiven for letting go completely.

“Uu, ghhh…aa, uu, aaaaaaa.”

“Uau…uauu, ua, u, uau…!”

“There, there… All children have the right to cry and rest in the comfort of an adult’s arms. If my bosom is sufficient, you may spill as many tears as you wish.”

Looking up, Subaru burst into tears again, and Louis clung even harder to him. Hugging both of them gently, Yoruna patted their small backs.

At the end of the battle, there atop the palace keep of the Crimson Lazuli Palace—

“I’m not sure how I should feel with all this happening on my back, though.”

“Silence.”

The old monster’s tactless banter was silenced by the lady of the city.

2

“Now then, what do you have to say in your defense, Old Man Orbart?”

“Defense? Was there something I had to defend? You’re the one who came at me, fox-girl.”

After Subaru let everything out and had finally actually calmed down—the palace keep was swallowed up in a dangerous mood.

The cause was, of course, Orbart and his carefree, shameless response. The old man had plopped down on the roof, scratching his ear with his pinkie.

“I kept my word, you know? I’ll admit treading the line, but the same’s true for the kiddo there.”

“Ugh…b-but that’s…”

“Now, now, you should just take the win, kiddo. If you wanna say anything goes, I’m the one who benefits most, after all, kah-ha-ha-ha!”

Subaru hesitated at that roaring laugh.

Orbart was right. If it was no-holds-barred match, he could not begin to imagine how a win would even be possible. Orbart had his shinobi techniques and experience and no compunction at all about getting other people involved. Subaru had learned the hard way that those sorts of opponents were the strongest of all since coming to Volakia.

“You kind of remind me of a scary guy I know, Mr. Orbart…”

“Really? Whoever that is must be a bad guy, and you’d definitely be better off killing him.”

“In that case, you must also agree it would be better for me to snuff your life out here.”

“Hey now. You must really hate me. Can’t say I don’t get why, though.”

He ignored Yoruna’s stern gaze without breaking a sweat.

His insolence was exasperating, but the reason he could take such a casual stance was because he knew Yoruna would not make the first move herself.

Sorry, Yoruna.

And the reason was none other than the problem afflicting Subaru and the others.

“I do not know the details, but I have heard that you have treated these children quite terribly.”

With pipe in mouth, she inhaled a puff of smoke while watching Orbart. When Subaru had asked for her help, he explained the situation while keeping certain parts unspoken. One of those parts was that Subaru himself was one of the people Orbart had turned into a child.

If Orbart undid his age regression, his body would go back to normal. He fully intended to apologize with all his might and ask for Yoruna’s forgiveness when it happened.

Of course, I don’t think that will cause all her impressions to change.

Subaru was sure now that Yoruna was the sort of person who could be reasoned with.

“Old Man Orbart, you acknowledge your defeat in the match you set?”

“Aye, I admit it. No way to see this as anything but a complete loss. I’m just lucky to lose without dying. But what a surprising way to lose.”

“Surprising, you say?”

“I figured it would be the kiddos’ boss who’d give me a run for my money.”

Despite Subaru’s concerns, Yoruna and Orbart continued their conversation.

“Boss,” Yoruna murmured softly, putting her hand to her chest. “The author of the letter. I had been looking forward to our meeting, but…”

Yoruna stopped there, and her eyes narrowed.

Orbart cocked his head at the sharp gaze.

“What? Ain’t nothing scarier than a glare from a beauty. What do you want?”

“Do not give me that. I had Tanza pass along word that the messengers should come to the palace. Where have you taken her?”

The air froze. Yoruna’s anger always made itself known when children or people of the city were put in harm’s way. And Tanza was both.

Though the suspicion is that Tanza and Orbart were conspiring together to keep us from meeting Yoruna…

“I thought Tanza would be with you, too, Mr. Orbart…hidden under the tiles or something.”

“Inside the palace is no different than inside of me. I would never miss that.”

“R-really? Your ability is really incredible, Miss Yoruna…”

Subaru was staggered by her seemingly absurd claim. And then he realized that she had immediately discovered him and Louis the moment they infiltrated the palace.

“She said she just happened to be walking around and found us, but…”

In the end, Yoruna had been protecting them from the very moment they entered the palace. The more he learned of her character, the more he started to question whether they should involve her in a battle that would embroil the entire empire in war.

That was the same feeling that the residents of Chaosflame who had blocked their way had felt, too. They had endured terrible hardship and been persecuted. Now that they had finally found a sanctuary, they would protect it no matter what.

Who could blame them for wanting to protect their peace? All the more so when the lord of the city cares so much about them.

What was so different about that from the world the girl he loved wanted?

“………”

Subaru peered down at the chaotic streets and alleys of the Demon City in silence. It was a complicated, chaotic mess. When he first came here, he had been a bit confused by the chaos. But in just a short amount of time, having seen the people living here and seen Yoruna, he started to understand.

This was a place where no one was tied down, where everyone had the freedom to be themselves and not hide, so this was a place where people felt free to express themselves, and it was brimming with an untamed energy that no one could deny.

In a sense, this was a utopia where anyone could live.

Should we really pull Yoruna away from a place like this?

While Subaru struggled with that inner turmoil, Yoruna continued.

“Old Man, answer me. Where is she? Where is Tanza?”

“Don’t look at me like that. I’ll tell you. The reason I accepted that deer-girl’s offer is ’cause she fit the conditions for the match so nicely.”

“—Where is she?”

Yoruna repeated herself, indicating that she had no interest in his extra banter. Orbart tilted his neck and looked out at the city beneath the palace—at the beautiful scene of the Demon City.

“It’s not too hard a riddle. I’m an outsider, aren’t I? Not a lot of places I can hide a girl, are there?”

3

Back in time to a little bit before Orbart answered Yoruna’s question.

The location was a certain inn in Demon City Chaosflame. It was a plain and simple inn, neither particularly large nor particularly elegant. But its walls and doors were of stout construction, and hardly any noise could be heard from inside it.

It was a place at odds with the feel of the rest of the city, the one and only lodging in the city provided for VIPs. The room that had become center stage was made by removing the walls between three rooms and combining them all into a unified space. It was not furnished with high-quality furniture and decorations, nor did it have the finest selection of alcohol. It spoke to the preference for utility of the one who was residing inside.

In that sense as well, this seemed almost heretically out of step with the way of life in Chaosflame. Despite being called a lawless zone, despite the general freedom and acceptance of chaos in the city, the residents of Chaosflame were astonishingly unified in spirit under the master of the Demon City.

The people rallied to a sort of shared delusion, unforgiving of external enemies and merciful to each other, and so such inns were generally unnecessary and tactless.

Just as…

“Citizens of the empire must be strong. This demonic city can be said to fly in the face of that ideal.”

The girl gulped faintly, and her cheeks tensed as the man intoned the empire’s motto with crossed arms.

The man, Abel, wore a black and red outfit and was covering his face with an oni mask. And facing him was a horned demi-human girl in a beautiful kimono: Tanza.

Abel and Tanza were not the only two enemies meeting here like this, though.

“Do you have any comprehension of the location you have just set foot in…?!”

“………”

“Answer me! Depending upon your response, there may be nothing left of you!”

There was also a man with dark skin turning red with wrath: Imperial General Second-Class Kafma Irulux, who was bellowing at Abel after he had barged into the room, as well as the boy and girl Abel had brought with him.

He held nothing in his outstretched hand, but he had no need for a weapon. Weapons of all sorts were lying in wait within his body. His statement that there may be nothing left of them was no idle threat, either. It was a simple statement of fact.

That was the true strength of the Insect General Kafma Irulux.

“Hey, are you being serious here, Abel?”

Al spoke in a tense, wary voice. Abel glanced at the masked boy with a sword on his back that he could not properly wield.

“How many times must you ask that before you have made up your mind?”

“I keep askin’ ’cause I still haven’t figured out anything even after barging in. And I’m still questioning your sanity! Damn it! Why’d I even go along with this…?!”

“For the obvious reason. The current you is too cowardly to be alone.”

“…!”

Al was at a loss for words. It was obvious from his reaction that Abel was right on the mark, and Al’s lack of a comeback only confirmed it. The current Al could not remain calm even just walking in the streets, for some reason.

“Abel.”

In his stead, Medium rose to argue. Feeling her gaze on his back, Abel harrumphed. Medium had pushed herself with significant effort to accompany Abel here, all while protecting Al, who had become unable to defend himself. However, there were all manner of troubles bringing a shadow to her expression, all involving Subaru and Louis, who had left the group partway.

Either way, though, it could be said that both Al and Medium were badly limited.

“And so we have no intention of fighting as well. Lower your arm, Kafma Irulux.”

“You…are you mad? You fail to answer my question while high-handedly pushing your own agenda. Do you think you have become some king?!”

“…That is not quite correct, but not far off.”

“You—!”

Kafma, devoted and faithful to the emperor, had reached his limits, and his eyes ran red with fury. Without realizing it, he was close to grasping Abel’s identity, but he could not manage to connect the last dots. It was a testament to the strength of the perception inhibition effect of the oni mask Abel received at the Shudrak village.

Only those who already knew the wearer’s identity or those to whom the wearer wished to reveal themselves could overcome the effects of the mask.

Meaning…

“Silence, Kafma Irulux.”

Kafma’s furious momentum was halted by a voice from behind him. The source was a handsome, black-haired man sitting calmly in a seat at the back of the room—seeing that familiar face again, Abel was, as always, impressed by the construction of that mask.

Regardless of his reaction, though, the man looked at the three of them in turn.

“They bear us no hostility. At the very least, not in this situation.”

“But! This one has disrespected Your Highness and refuses to reveal his face in your presence, and he shows no sign of obedience! He has even brought children—”

“What of the children?”

“Nothing, Your Highness. It’s simply incomprehensible…!”

Kafma could not hide the deep bewilderment he was feeling. He was struggling mentally while rubbing his eyes. The reason was because of his overly serious demeanor. He had, in the past, given up the title of Divine General, believing himself unsuited to it. As such, personality aside, he was equivalent to a Divine General in strength.

If a struggle occurred, Abel would of course have no hope of winning. However, his goal now lay elsewhere.

“I apologize for disturbing your bedchamber; however, I have business with this girl. At present, I have no intention of confronting you.”

“Hoh. That is an exceedingly bold stance to assume in our presence. You surely have some memory of this face and this voice. Doubly so if you have some relation to the messenger that we happened to meet yesterday at the palace keep.”

“Hmph.” Abel observed the man who Subaru called the false emperor and whose identity he had already discerned: Chisha Gold, disguised as Vincent.

Al and Medium stood beside Abel with complicated, sullen looks. Outside the effects of the mask’s perception obstruction, they could hear him conversing with Vincent, using the exact same voice. In that sense as well, the white spider Chisha’s transformation was perfect.

By changing his voice, behavior, and appearance to match Vincent Volakia, Chisha Gold could embody the emperor even better than Abel.

However…

“I received a report from my subordinates regarding that. For the stern Emperor Volakia, you were quite forgiving of an insolent woman’s disrespect.”

“We are not so capricious as to take issue with every person who knows not their place. However, should those who oppose us demonstrate enough worth, they will be dealt with accordingly. Since—”

Vincent answered Abel’s prodding and left just a moment’s pause as their gazes locked. Their lips moved at the same exact moment.

““Citizens of the empire must be strong.””

That was the ideal of the Holy Volakian Empire and emblematic of its way of life. Abel could not but admit that such a response was befitting of the emperor of Volakia and considered it a splendid belief. Abel himself would have given the same answer had someone said the same to him. No matter what he might feel in his heart.

“Kafma, regarding that girl…”

“Your Highness. Old Man Orbart indicated that she be kept here… However, Orbart himself has gone out into the city and has yet to return.”

“I see.”

Nodding at Kafma’s embarrassed response, Vincent turned his gaze to Tanza. She gasped. Tanza had retreated to the corner of the room and was now trapped by the gaze of the man who stood at the top of the empire.

“Your involvement with Orbart, the agreement with Yoruna Mishigure, and the fact that a person involved with the messengers from yesterday has appeared in search of you is enough to grasp the gist of the situation.”

“I—I…”

“No excuse is necessary. Once you have begun a struggle, you may simply struggle in earnest to the end. Decide for yourself whether the path you chose burns out or not.”

Vincent calmly and deliberately declared that Tanza would not be protected any further. However, to say that that left Tanza in despair would be false.

“I…”

As she murmured, there was a resolve in her eyes. It seemed like she had decided to fight to the end.

Abel could easily imagine that as a horned girl, Tanza had by no means had a peaceful life. The salvation she found with Yoruna must have been so warm.

“I am sorry for the trouble I have caused Lord Vincent; however, all of this was arranged by myself and without the knowledge of my mistress Lady Yoruna.”

“As stated, no excuse is necessary. Depending on the outcome, Yoruna Mishigure will be questioned. Should she not answer, your statement will be kept in consideration.”

“Yes sir. Thank you, sir.”

Tanza adjusted herself into a proper sitting position and bowed deeply to Vincent. Raising her head, she looked over at Abel.

Unlike with Vincent, there was a clear and present hostility.

“…!”

Al quivered beneath her gaze. He had become consumed by cowardice, but even without that, the intensity of that gaze was more than enough to overwhelm him. And Abel could well imagine what sort of life she must have lived to make her go so far.

All of it was—

“—Please do not draw Lady Yoruna into the flames of war.”

“Ah…” Medium’s voice trembled in wonder.

“She is kind, and for the sake of the many who are weak, she would charge into battle and wear herself down. I cannot allow such a thing to happen. Lady Yoruna is everything to me.”

Al and Medium were seemingly surprised by Tanza’s motive; but it was within Abel’s expectations that the residents of the Demon City, including her, might act upon such thoughts.

What convinced him was the soul marriage that had permeated through the people of the city. It was an ancient secret technique that could not function with an arbitrary and one-sided emotion.

Her soul was connected to such an absurd number of partners that she should have lost all sense of herself. Abel’s conjecture had pinned down the nature of the ability, but either way…

“That will be decided by Yoruna Mishigure. The situation will not change, no matter how many times you lower your head to me.”

“No, that is not true. It is not Lady Yoruna who will decide, but you, sir.”

“………”

“Lady Yoruna is exceedingly kind, considerate, and accepting…and she has an extraordinarily distant dream with which we cannot help. You, however, possess the means of achieving that dream.”

“…You know the contents of the letter to Yoruna Mishigure?”

“No sir.” Tanza shook her head. But when her head returned to level, there was a terribly fragile expression on her face, and she looked down. “However, I know—I have never before seen Lady Yoruna bear such a maiden-like expression.”

“A maiden-like expression, you say?”

“Yes sir. I planned all of this.”

Lowering her head toward the ground, Tanza confessed her plot.

It by no means explained everything. Her plan had surely been altered by Orbart’s hand, twisting it into something more vicious. However, she was attempting to take responsibility for starting it, and for including Orbart.

It was all too…

“Beautiful.”

It was an unvoiced word left only in the back of his mouth where none could hear. Abel nodded silently at Tanza’s gaze.

“I have grasped the extent of your involvement in this plot. However, I should advise you of one thing.”

“…What is that, sir?”

“I have no intention of demanding you pay for your actions with your life. Should your head roll, Yoruna Mishigure’s hand would be lost. Or was that also a part of your plan?”

There was a slight twitch in Tanza’s neck as she looked down. That convinced Abel that Tanza had been ready to offer her life if it came to that.

It would have been a final resort. But there were not many who would have given it such serious thought before acting.

“You even intended to die…? That’s insane.” Al gasped.

“That’s…! We won’t let that happen! We won’t let that happen, right, Abel?”

Medium looked at Abel. She was afraid of the small chance that he might do so, but he shook his head, dismissing such concerns as absurd.

“As I said, if even her death is part of her plan, then to take her life would be to assure the success of her plan. Unfortunately, I have no intention of indulging such a stratagem.”

“Abel…!”

“People should die more efficiently.”

“Abel…”

A piece that could not be predicted was dangerous, whether it was in the enemy’s camp or one’s own. On that point, the existence of Tanza was an unmanageable poison. However, without the resolve to swallow that poison, it would not be possible to win over an even greater poison to his side.

Adjudging that, Abel looked at Tanza sitting on the floor.

“I shall not take your life. However, I will have you withdraw the order you have given your compatriots.”

“…Then regarding my request?”

“To not draw Yoruna Mishigure into the flames of war…? That is impossible.”

Tanza’s voice caught in her throat at his flat rejection. From her perspective, it was the prophecy of the very thing she had risked her life to stop, but she suffered from a misunderstanding. A fatal misunderstanding.

“Even had I not come, Yoruna Mishigure would be swallowed up in the flames of war. That is the position she has chosen and a nigh inescapable fact of the way of life she follows.”

“What do you see in—?”

“I have no intention of revealing what my eyes see to others; however, so long as it is possible, I shall prepare for what may come. Regardless of how that may appear to those around me.”

After he answered Tanza’s trembling voice and gaze, Abel’s eyes moved away from her and instead flitted to Vincent sitting silently at the back of the room. The Vincent Volakia sitting upon the throne. The false emperor.

Whatever intentions he had in repudiating me…

“My truth is unchanged. Unchangeable. All bridges are burned, and there is only one path forward. You would do well to sear that into your soul.”

“…We shall bear that in mind,” Vincent answered quietly.

That exchange seemed to scorch the very air of the room, unleashing a heat that felt like a fever. In truth, everyone in the room besides Abel and Vincent was starting to sweat.

“Tanza, raise your head.”

As the two emperors stared at each other, Abel called to the girl regretting her lack of strength. The girl slowly raised her head, eyes wet with tears. Abel exhaled.

“From the start, I had no intention of using your mistress as a disposable tool. The question of how to use her requires deep consideration, but such a valuable asset shall be used in the most appropriate way. People should die efficiently.”

“…May I put my trust in that?”

“Whether you trust it or not, my actions will be the same.”

Tanza clung to a faint, budding hope, but the response she received was by no means kind. Behind Abel, Al put his hand to his forehead, and Medium sighed, but after some small amount of hesitation, Tanza nodded. And then…

“…How did you realize that I was here?”

“I deduced that this is what Orbart would do. I also considered the possibility you would be hidden in the Crimson Lazuli Palace, but considering the location of the pursuit and the problem of distance, I prioritized this location first.”

“Oh.”

“And above all, if I did not pin you down, there were too many threats to our lives.”

Talitta was being chased by the one hundred horned people, and Subaru and Louis had effectively gone out on their own. So long as they were being chased by so many pursuers, there was no guarantee they would survive. Of course, Abel was no exception, either, considering that Al was in no state to fight and Medium was not nearly as effective as normal.

To continue Orbart’s match, he had prioritized capturing Tanza.

“…It’s my loss.”

“Of that there is no doubt. However, you need not feel ashamed.”

“Eh…?”

That was all Abel said as he turned around. Tanza’s round eyes blinked in confusion.

“Girl.” Vincent spoke up behind her.

Turning around, she saw the false emperor nodding.

“What he said is correct. You need not feel ashamed.”

“B-but I…”

“You were defeated. But that means that you fought. That is also how we all should wish to be.”

Still propping his head up with his arm, Vincent turned his eyes to look slightly into the distance. Tanza was stunned by his words, but tears slowly welled up in her eyes, and she looked down.
