chapters.text:
Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

Looking down and crying, the tears falling silently as she apologized to her beloved mistress.

“Lady Yoruna, I am sorry… I was not prepared enough…”

4

“I have discerned Orbart’s location. The Crimson Lazuli Palace.”

“Huh?!”

Medium’s eyes widened in surprise when Abel returned from his exchange with Tanza.

She had just thought this was about Tanza or maybe the fake emperor, so it was a double shock to hear not just about Orbart, who was not here, but also about the hiding place they were looking for.

“How do you know, Abel? And hiding in the palace is…”

“Tanza’s reaction. Her eyes wavered when the subject of the palace was raised. I am sure she heard it from him when he hid her at this inn. I am sure she will not know the exact hiding place, though.”

“Y-you really are cunning…”

Al looked at Abel like he could scarcely believe what he was hearing.

Most likely, the sequence was Orbart and Tanza partnering up, Tanza delivering Yoruna’s message, and then Orbart challenging them to a match. Then after the first hiding place was found, Orbart brought Tanza to the inn here.

Of course, he could always have given her fake information to mess with them, but…

“The tactic of hiding within Yoruna Mishigure’s palace is precisely the sort that Orbart would enjoy.”

“…Mmm, then next up is Yoruna’s palace. Ah, but if Tanza is going to call off those people chasing us, then maybe we should look for Talitta?”

“If the goal is to meet up, then it would be a poor plan for us to move. Talitta’s eyes will find us before long, and she will come to rejoin us. As for those fools…”

“Y-yeah…”

“…So long as he has not become exceedingly incompetent, he will discern that Orbart is at the palace. So long as they have not died, they will be going the same place as us.”

Abel’s cold explanation was not quite enough to really reassure Medium. She wanted to talk with the three who had been separated from the group—particularly Subaru and Louis. Even though she still did not know how she should act.

“…Don’t die on me, Bro…”

“Al…”

“We gotta get that gramps to put us back to normal… If I can get my body back, I’ll be better. And, Bro will…”

Al clenched his fist in a mixture of prayer and curse.

Al had no composure under the effects of the age regression, and he was incredibly fixated on the connection between Subaru and Louis. He was probably thinking about getting Subaru back to normal so he could deal with Louis correctly, but who could say if his judgment would be normal once he was back in his original body?

And even before that…

“Whatever you may be thinking, I have no intention of allowing Orbart’s technique to be undone so simply.”

“Huh?”

“Eh?”

“More to the point, I do not mind for you or Medium, but I do not intend to have it undone for Subaru Natsuki for now. It will be better to have him remain in that form for a time.”

Al and Medium both opened their eyes in shock at Abel’s abrupt decision. And then, a moment later:

“Don’t screw with me!” Al grabbed Abel by the lapels. “You’re not bringing Bro back?! I ain’t acceptin’ that! What do you mean by that?!”

“As I said, I will have him remain in a young form for now.”

“You bastard…”

“Is this to bully Subaru more?”

Medium put her hand on Al’s shoulder, stopping him as he engaged in a staredown between adult and child. She was looking carefully at him, prepared not to move until she got an answer.

Abel quietly exhaled.

“I do not recall doing anything as vulgar as bullying.”

“Call it whatever you like! But for a long time, you were constantly scaring Subaru and not explaining anything! Is it because of that?”

“………”

“That’s not right! If there’s something you want to know, then just ask him, and he’ll tell you! So you don’t have to—”

“Unfortunately, it will not go so well.”

It was so quiet, fragile, and almost self-derisive that Medium was speechless. Noticing her surprise out of the corner of his eye, Abel easily brushed aside Al’s arm clutching him.

“My thoughts are unrelated to Medium’s suspicions. It is simply a necessary thing.”

“Necessary?! What is?! Why is it just Bro…? Why not me or Medium?!”

“You would not fit the requirements. Your one arm and Medium’s hair and eye color.”

“Huh…?!”

Al was getting angrier and angrier at that seemingly meaningless response. Medium looked lost as well, but there was also a different surprise lingering.

And Abel himself…

“The situation is currently unchanged, and the pieces are gathering. As such…”

Abel looked through his mask out the window of the inn toward the Crimson Lazuli Palace. It was a gesture that seemed to signify a glare at something more symbolic than just the palace itself, and he reached out his hand, as if to grasp something out of reach.

“You and I are not the sorts to hide and run away forever.”

There was venom in his voice as he addressed an unseen person.

5

“The deer-girl is with His Highness.”

“I thought it might be at your inn if it wasn’t the palace, but…”

Orbart was sitting there on the roof, short arms crossed as he answered honestly. Subaru was stunned and exasperated.

“Either way, Tanza’s location is now known… It seems the residents of my city have been rather unreasonable in their treatment of you, so I shall offer my apologies.”

“Eh, that’s… Miss Yoruna, let’s just call it even! There’s nothing you need to apologize for!”

Subaru panicked, leaping and shouting when he saw Yoruna kneel and lower her head in apology. For Yoruna to lower her head was an incredible gesture.

She had listened to Subaru and taken him seriously and gone as far as fighting Orbart to save him so, so many times. And…

“Ugh…”

“…? What is it, child? Your face is red.”

“No, it’s just, I remembered a bunch of things…”

Right when he had managed to calm down, he remembered the scene that had happened so many times during that loop of despair. Yoruna commanding him to love her and kissing him.

Of course, the memory of that remained only in Subaru’s head now, and he had not really been in a position where he could register what it felt like to be kissed by her. Even so, he respected Yoruna for putting herself on the line to save a child on the verge of death, and honestly, he had started to like her.

All the more reason I don’t want to get her involved.

She was so kind and beloved by everyone in this city, he was reluctant to get her wrapped up in it all.

Was him feeling like that an effect of his becoming younger and more childlike? Maybe he would be able to write it off as a mistake and forget about it if he got his body back.

But even if he started thinking differently when he got his grown body back, he could not imagine it would change how he felt now.

Because if he did, then…

“Uau?”

“I wouldn’t trust the bigger me with knowing how to handle you, either.”

Subaru still did not have an answer for what to do with the girl holding his hand.

There would be no avoiding it once he met back up with Abel and the others, but there was one thing he was sure of after those ten seconds of despair.

I don’t want to let her kill anyone, and I don’t want to let her die.

“The palace’s repairs can wait. I shall go to get Tanza first.”

“Mhm. Right. In that case…”

Yoruna prepared to find Tanza with a bright and cheerful face. Subaru wanted to talk to Tanza, too, so he prepared to leave the palace, too.

“Wait just a moment there, kiddo. You don’t wanna go back to normal? Or did you take a liking to this body? I don’t really mind either way.”

“Ah, sorry, no, no. I’d like to be big again, please. I have gotten pretty used to this, but it’ll be a problem finding things to wear, so I’d like to return to normal.”

Subaru spun around when Orbart called out to him. He had only spent a few hours as a child, but he had experienced more deaths in this form than all his previous deaths combined.

The only fear is my way of thinking suddenly changing, but…

“Don’t worry, Louis. This time, I’ll stop dodging you.”

“Uau…au.”

Louis looked down, but then she nodded. Pushing her forehead with his finger, he left her in Yoruna’s care. Louis bumped into Yoruna, who caught her gently.

“Child, regarding what Old Man Orbart is about to do…”

“Mhm. I don’t blindly trust him, but I’d like to believe he has just enough humanity to honor the results of a contest.”

“Hey, I can hear you, brat.”

“That’s why I’m saying it.”

Subaru smiled wryly at Orbart’s banter. Yoruna’s eyes narrowed as she hugged Louis from behind.

“If you understand, then there is nothing more for me to say. I have not heard what will happen, child, but this girl and I shall be watching.”

“Uu!”

“Mhm. I understand. Um, I hope you’ll get along with the other me, Miss Yoruna.”

“…? You are quite the worrier, child.”

With Yoruna’s wry smile and Louis’s cheerful expression, Subaru went over to Orbart. The old man stood up and brushed off his bottom.

“You just don’t let up, do you? Sheesh. Let’s get this over with.”

“Yeah… Umm, is this going to hurt?”

“Did it hurt when you shrank? There’s your answer. Ha!”

Smirking maliciously, Orbart put his hand around Subaru’s solar plexus.

Al’s thought was that the age regression technique had to do with some interaction with Odo, in which case the spot should be somewhere around the heart, maybe.

The mechanism by which interfering with the flow of Odo caused a body to shrink was hard to imagine, but…

It felt like these few hours shrunk down were the biggest pinch he had had since coming to the empire. Though it had really just been a series of worse and worse predicaments ever since landing, too.

Those ten seconds were the worst thing I’ve ever been through, including everything I’ve seen before coming to the empire.

“Oh yeah.”

He remembered something he had made a point not to think about. The hellish deaths in that ten-second loop were something entirely different from the Return by Death that he knew.

What caused that? And what happened to my Return by Death authority…?

“I found you.”

6

It was difficult for anyone in that place to fully perceive everything that happened in that moment.

“Ngh!”

Orbart immediately pulled back his outstretched hand, but it was too late. His wrinkled old right hand turned to dust from the wrist down and disappeared.

“Child—”

“Uau!!!”

Yoruna’s eyes opened wide in shock as she pulled Louis close, holding the struggling girl tight while leaping back as fast as she could.

The next moment, a dark shadow filled their entire field of view, swallowing the tower of the beautiful Crimson Lazuli Palace, and then the upper floors and the middle floors.

“Your Highness! That…”

“………”

Kafma was bristling as he stood beside the emperor he was duty bound to protect. He sensed the insects within him all cowering as he watched the incredible scene unfolding in the distance through the window.

Vincent stood up and turned his sharp gaze on the blackening palace, eyes blinking in deep and careful thought.

“That’s…the palace…Lady Yoruna…”

“Aaa, aaaaa, aaaaaaaaaaa!!!!”

“Al?!”

Dumbstruck, the young ones stared in shock at what was happening.

As the destruction unfolded, Tanza feared for her mistress, and Al screamed louder than anyone in the city, perhaps the world.

Medium ran over, supporting Al’s shoulder, and unable to understand what was going on at all, she gulped and looked pleadingly toward Abel.

“Dear oh dear…this is a little beyond what I saw coming.”

“You are…”

Ubirk shaded his eyes, looking at the destruction of the palace in the distance while murmuring to himself, while Talitta, standing across from him, ground her teeth.

“…Is this the true nature of what you carry inside you?”

Abel saw the same thing that the false emperor and the crying child saw. Clenching his fists, hiding the lip he was biting hard enough to draw blood behind his mask, his expression became as twisted as the visage engraved in the mask as he glared at the darkness.

7

I love you.

I love you. I love you. I love you.

I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you.

I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you.

It exceeded all dimensions in scale, overwriting and crushing Subaru Natsuki’s very being—a love like a curse that would never let him go.

He had experienced a hellish world without love, and he also knew that he was still loved. But at the same time, it was important to understand that not every love should be affirmed.

There was a price to pay for not knowing that. Because he was ignorant of why it was feared, why it was avoided.

He transformed into a black shadow, swallowing and destroying everything while cheering.

Cheering a reunion, a confluence, an embrace, fetters, fate, striving.

Cheering a confession, regret, jealousy, mystery, exaltation, dedication.

He had known a hellish world devoid of love, so what hell would befall a world overflowing with love?

Subaru did not know. He did not know at all. But in this situation where no one understood anything, there was only one thing he could say.

The utopia for the persecuted, Demon City Chaosflame, had been toppled by none other than Subaru Natsuki’s karma.

chapters.text:
Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

INTERLUDE

FILLING THE BLUE SKY

1

At the same time a beautiful palace far to the west was being consumed by a dark shadow…

“Ms. Priscilla?”

Rem, who was washing a bathing woman’s hair, watched as the woman stood up. Her hair slipped from Rem’s fingers as the woman went calmly to the bath’s window.

This was Priscilla Bariel, a regal woman with dazzling orange hair and snowy white skin, a woman whose connection with Rem was difficult to describe.

She was a fiery woman who acted with greater haughtiness than anyone in the fortified city where Rem had remained. She had declared she would keep Rem at her side while she remained in the city, and true to her word, she brought Rem everywhere, tasking Rem with waiting on her hand and foot, but also making time to speak with her.

The one constant was this daily bath time, but…

“Ms. Priscilla, you haven’t finished bathing…ah!”

Not listening, Priscilla opened the window without hesitation, her naked body entirely bare as the outside wind blew through the bathhouse.

The steam that had been billowing so luxuriously quickly scattered, but the surprises did not stop there. Priscilla leaned out the open window, stepping onto the balcony.

Rem frantically followed, holding a towel.

“Wh-what are you doing? People can see you! Just because this is the highest floor…”

“The sky.”

“The sky…? This balcony isn’t that high. Come now, let’s return before the water—”

She did not manage to finish her plea, though. Priscilla brought her finger to Rem’s lips. Wearing the towel laid over her shoulders like a cape, she looked at Rem with her blood-colored eyes.

“Look at the sky, Rem. It seems our vacation is at an end.”

Grasping the seriousness in Priscilla’s eyes, Rem gulped. And, wearing a bathing suit herself, she peered up at the same sky as Priscilla. She strained her blue eyes to see what Priscilla had seen.

But there was no need to try so hard, since…

“That…is…”

Atop the balcony, at the brightest point of the wind hour, there was a glittering in the enormous sun overhead. Black dots appeared in the almost white light. One, then two, then more and more. They continued increasing, until finally their identity became clear.

“Have those below raise arms at once. There is no trifling with a swarm of winged dragons.”

2

She peered down upon the city surrounded by high walls. Her golden eyes narrowed.

High up in the blue sky streaked with clouds, the greatest of beings flapped their wings as a strong wind roared past.

“Fortress city of Guaral.”

Her blood boiled in anticipation at the sight of her target.

That eagerness gradually spread around her, merging with the flapping wings and bestial cries.

It was a little hasty, but it was only natural that it stoked their instincts as hunters. They were apex predators, after all.

“………”

“I know. Let’s do our job properly, like the old-timer said.”

Heeding the admonition of the dragon she was astride, the girl crossed her arms and nodded.

Her blue hair gathered at her shoulders, and her golden eyes glimmered. She wore a flashy uniform, and on her back was her trusty winged blade. That was hardly enough to tell what sort of person she was, but there was one trait that proved she was special—the two black horns growing from her head.

“Everyone ready?”

Countless cries rose up in response, each coming from a majestic master of the open skies. A flock of several hundred dragons had arrived.

Once they descended, there would be roars and shrieks as countless lives were snuffed out.

On the precipice of a grand hunt, the horned creature—Madelyn Eschert—looked upon Guaral once more with her golden eyes and smiled.

This was a declaration of war from the Ninth Divine General, the flying dragon commander who had been ordered to raze the city.

“Tremble in fear. Flee. There’s nowhere to run. The dragons have come.”

<END>

Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

AFTERWORD

Hello, everyone! Good job! This is Tappei Nagatsuki and the mouse-colored cat!

Thank you for reading Volume 29 of Re:Zero! This whole book was dedicated to the Chaosflame arc, but how did the worst hardship to befall Subaru since his sudden arrival in the Volakian Empire appear to you, dear reader? For me, it was very fun to write!

I’ve come up with all sorts of difficulties to inflict on Subaru Natsuki with his Return by Death ability, but I really put a lot of effort into the (self-described) Palace Clash Arc. As an author, it would be a great honor if you enjoyed it.

Incidentally, this volume was as densely packed as ever, and this time I could not choose what to do for the cover and went with something extravagant. The eye-catching cover illustration is, of all things, a character who only appears in the interlude at the very end!

This time, I selfishly pressed Otsuka to make the cover illustration something that anyone who read to the end of the interlude would recognize.

Please take the cover this time as a part of the story! Enjoy!

Now that I’ve cleared that up, it’s time to move on to the usual thanks.

Thank you to my editor I for the warm and generous forgiveness for the significant change to the plot’s contents. I believe your statement that “It’s important to just try writing it” is a wise view. In similar struggles in the future, I will keep to the idea of the plot as a general compass!

Thank you very much to the illustrator Otsuka for creating the illustrations with such attention to my requests with regular discussions! The age-regressed trio are practically new characters, so having an updated design and the like was a great help!

The designer Kusano played an even greater role in the cover illustration than usual, setting it up big and beautiful. Thank you very much! It is thanks to the work and support of everyone that this book exists!

Atori and Aikawa’s adaptation of the fourth arc in Gekkan Comic Alive is ongoing, and getting to see a copy of the draft every month, the beauty of the complete draft is breathtaking!

In addition, thank you very much to everyone else at MF Bunko J’s editorial division, the proofreader, and all of the bookstores. You all do so much to help make these books happen.

And my greatest thanks again go to you, the readers who continue to support this super-long series!

Honestly, it is still a shock to me, but next time is really the thirtieth volume! There still is no end in sight, so I will do my best to keep writing to the end, so please continue to support me! I really am always grateful for it!

May we meet again in the next volume, Volume 30!

February 2022

<<With the round number thirty coming up, even I’m a little shocked>>

Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, Vol. 29

“And so the curtain falls on Volume 29. I have taken a leading role in the postscript in preparation for the thirtieth volume, but…”

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! Whoever was doing the casting messed up making me the costar! Me and the fox-girl got pretty chippy in the book, after all.”

“Agreed. Were it not for the child, I suspect you would not have stayed on this earth long enough for us to casually chat like this.”

“Well, it’s not so rare for even dead people to speak up here. Who knows? Even if one of us kicked it in the main story, we still might have ended up paired off here.”

“………”

“Oh, did I say something tasteless? Whoops, my bad, my bad.”

“The longer this continues, the shorter your life span seems to shrink, Old Man Orbart. Let us get to the subject at hand for both our sakes.”

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! That sort of consideration ain’t like you. But it’s not like I especially enjoy putting myself in harm’s way, so let’s get to it.”

“…As mentioned at the start, the next volume will be the thirtieth, a nice, big round number.”

“Kaaah! Thirty! That’s a pretty big number. I’m a nasty old man, obviously, but I can still be impressed by something that’s lasted so long.”

“Either way, the schedule is unchanged, and the release should come in June. Additionally, Volume 7 of the short story collection will also be released on the same day.”

“A short story collection! Well, with all that the kiddo’s suffered in the main story, it’d be hard to keep going without a little rest. Not to mention that I caused a lot of that suffering.”

“That you can behave so blithely despite knowing that shows you know no shame, Old Man… I must say I am impressed by the ease with which you live.”

“Hey now, don’t give me that. This is a little secret for you, but a shameless man’s got his own troubles, too.”

“Such thick skin that even sarcasm cannot penetrate. If that child had not intervened, I would have trampled you underfoot.”

“Kah-ha-ha-ha! Then I’ll have to thank the kiddo.”

“But of course, Old Man Orbart. I shall assuredly snap the unforgivable, haughty old tree with my own two hands.”

“Aye, aye, scary. I don’t wanna wet myself or die, so I’ll run to the ends of the world and wait for you.”

“Do so if you are able.”
